akhfash:9-9.t: He said ﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعاً مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ﴾: "البِدْع" is the novel one (البديع), i.e. the first.

akhfash:12-12.t:
And He said ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ مُوسَىٰ إِمَاماً وَرَحْمَةً﴾: accusative because it is the khabar of a definite (i.e. a ḥāl).
And He said ﴿وَهَـٰذَا كِتَابٌ مُّصَدِّقٌ لِّسَاناً عَرَبِيّاً﴾: He put "tongue" and "Arabic" in the accusative because it is not an attribute of "the Book"; it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or by an implied verb, as though He said: "I mean an Arabic tongue". Some said its accusative is by "مُصَدِّق" (confirming): he made the Book the confirmer of the tongue.

akhfash:33-33.t: As for His word ﴿وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يُحْيِـيَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾, it is with the bāʾ like the bāʾ in His word ﴿كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ﴾, and it is like ﴿تَنبُتُ بِٱلدُّهْنِ﴾.

akhfash:35-35.t: And He said ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوۤاْ إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِّن نَّهَارٍ بَلاَغٌ﴾: He means "that is a proclamation". Some said: "The proclamation is the Quran", and admonition is only by the Quran. Then He said ﴿بَلاَغٌ﴾, i.e. it is a proclamation.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿حم﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran; a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ its khabar (predicate) ﴿الْعَزِيزِ﴾ in His dominion ﴿الْحَكِيمِ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿مَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا﴾ a creating ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ so that it may point to Our power and Our oneness ﴿وَأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾ until their annihilation on the Day of Resurrection ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَمَّا أُنْذِرُوا﴾ the punishment they were made to fear ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ inform me ﴿مَا تَدْعُونَ﴾ you worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. the idols; the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) ﴿أَرُونِي﴾ inform me; a tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿مَاذَا خَلَقُوا﴾ the second object ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ an explanation (bayān) of «مَا» ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ﴾ a partnership ﴿فِي﴾ the creation of ﴿السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ with Allah; «أَمْ» has the meaning of the hamza of disavowal (inkār) ﴿ائْتُونِي بِكِتَابٍ﴾ sent down ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ هَذَا﴾ Quran ﴿أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ﴾ a remnant ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ﴾ handed down from the ancients, attesting to the soundness of your claim regarding the worship of idols, that they bring you near to Allah ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in your claim.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ an interrogative with the meaning of negation, i.e. no one ﴿أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ يَدْعُو﴾ worships ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿مَنْ لَا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ and they are the idols, which never answer their worshippers in anything they ask of them ﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ دُعَائِهِمْ﴾ their worship ﴿غَافِلُونَ﴾ because they are inanimate objects that do not understand.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَإِذَا حُشِرَ النَّاسُ كَانُوا﴾ i.e. the idols ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ to their worshippers ﴿أَعْدَاءً وَكَانُوا بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ﴾ the worship of their worshippers ﴿كَافِرِينَ﴾ denying.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿آيَاتُنَا﴾ the Quran ﴿بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ manifest; a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ among them ﴿لِلْحَقِّ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ هَذَا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear, manifest.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ with the meaning of «بَلْ» (rather) and the hamza of disavowal (inkār) ﴿يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿قُلْ إِنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ﴾ supposing so ﴿فَلَا تَمْلِكُونَ لِي مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. from His punishment ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ i.e. you would be unable to ward it off from me if Allah were to punish me ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾ what you say about the Quran ﴿كَفَى بِهِ﴾ Exalted is He ﴿شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ﴾ to whoever repents ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ to them, so He has not hastened the penalty upon you.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿قُلْ مَا كُنْتُ بِدْعًا﴾ something novel ﴿مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ i.e. the first one sent; many of them preceded me, so how can you call me a liar? ﴿وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ﴾ in this world: will I be driven out of my land, or killed as was done to the prophets before me, or will you stone me, or will the earth be made to swallow you like the deniers before you? ﴿إِنْ﴾ i.e. «مَا» (not) ﴿أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ﴾ i.e. the Quran, and I do not invent anything of my own ﴿وَمَا أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear in warning.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ inform me: what is your state ﴿إِنْ كَانَ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ he is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām ﴿عَلَى مِثْلِهِ﴾ i.e. upon it, that it is from Allah ﴿فَآمَنَ﴾ the witness ﴿وَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾ you were too arrogant to believe. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), together with what is conjoined to it [the protasis], is «أَلَسْتُمْ ظَالِمِينَ» ("are you not wrongdoers?"), indicated by ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ i.e. concerning them ﴿لَوْ كَانَ﴾ faith ﴿خَيْرًا مَا سَبَقُونَا إِلَيْهِ وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا﴾ i.e. those who said this ﴿بِهِ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿فَسَيَقُولُونَ هَذَا﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿إِفْكٌ﴾ a lie ﴿قَدِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿كِتَابُ مُوسَى﴾ i.e. the Torah ﴿إِمَامًا وَرَحْمَةً﴾ for those who believe in it; two ḥāls (circumstantials) ﴿وَهَذَا﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿كِتَابٌ مُصَدِّقٌ﴾ of the scriptures before it ﴿لِسَانًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾ a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُصَدِّقٌ» ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ the idolaters of Mecca ﴿وَ﴾ it is ﴿بُشْرَى لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ the believers.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقَامُوا﴾ in obedience ﴿فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿جَزَاءً﴾ accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by its implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e. «يُجْزَوْنَ» (they are recompensed) ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا﴾ and in one reading [إِحْسَانًا], i.e. We commanded him to be good to them; «إِحْسَانًا» is put in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by its implied (muqaddar) verb, and «حُسْنًا» is likewise ﴿حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهًا وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهًا﴾ i.e. with hardship ﴿وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصَالُهُ﴾ from nursing ﴿ثَلَاثُونَ شَهْرًا﴾ six months are the minimum period of pregnancy and the rest is the maximum period of nursing; and it is said: if she carried him six or nine months, she nurses him the remainder ﴿حَتَّى﴾ marking the limit of an implied clause, i.e. «وَعَاشَ حَتَّى» ("and he lived until") ﴿إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ﴾ it is the perfection of his strength, intellect and judgement, at the least thirty-three years, or thirty ﴿وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً﴾ i.e. its completion, and that is the upper limit of «الْأَشُدّ» ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ﴾ etc. It was revealed concerning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq: when he reached forty years, two years after the Prophet ﷺ was sent, he believed in him; then his parents believed, then his son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān's son Abū ʿAtīq ﴿أَوْزِعْنِي﴾ inspire me ﴿أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ﴾ with it ﴿عَلَيَّ وَعَلَى وَالِدَيَّ﴾ and it is tawḥīd (the affirmation of Allah's oneness) ﴿وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ﴾ so he freed nine of the believers who were being tormented for the sake of Allah ﴿وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ and all of them were believers ﴿إِنِّي تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ i.e. those who say these words, Abū Bakr and others ﴿الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ﴾ in the meaning of «حَسَنَ» (good) ﴿مَا عَمِلُوا وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَنْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ فِي أَصْحَابِ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. being among their company ﴿وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِي كَانُوا يُوعَدُونَ﴾ in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ}

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي قَالَ لِوَالِدَيْهِ﴾ and in one reading with assimilation (idghām); the genus is meant by it ﴿أُفٍّ﴾ with kasra and with fatḥa on the fāʾ, in the meaning of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. stench and ugliness ﴿لَكُمَا﴾ I am fed up with you two ﴿أَتَعِدَانِنِي﴾ and in one reading with assimilation (idghām) ﴿أَنْ أُخْرَجَ﴾ from the grave ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتِ الْقُرُونُ﴾ the nations ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِي﴾ and they were not brought out of the graves ﴿وَهُمَا يَسْتَغِيثَانِ اللَّهَ﴾ asking Him for help through his turning back, and they say: if you do not turn back, ﴿وَيْلَكَ﴾ i.e. your perdition, meaning "you have perished" ﴿آمِنْ﴾ in the resurrection ﴿إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ فَيَقُولُ مَا هَذَا﴾ i.e. the talk of resurrection ﴿إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ their lies.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَقَّ﴾ became binding ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلُ﴾ of punishment ﴿فِي أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا خَاسِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ﴾ of the kind of believer and disbeliever ﴿دَرَجَاتٌ﴾ the degrees of the believers in the Garden are high and the degrees of the disbelievers in the Fire are low ﴿مِمَّا عَمِلُوا﴾ i.e. the believers, of acts of obedience, and the disbelievers, of acts of disobedience ﴿وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ﴾ i.e. Allah; and in one reading with nūn ﴿أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ i.e. their recompense ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ in anything: nothing is reduced for the believers and nothing is added for the disbelievers.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ by its being uncovered to them; it will be said to them: ﴿أَذْهَبْتُمْ﴾ with one hamza, and with two hamzas, and with a hamza and a madda, and with both [hamzas] while lightening (tashīl) the second ﴿طَيِّبَاتِكُمْ﴾ by your being occupied with your pleasures ﴿فِي حَيَاتِكُمُ الدُّنْيَا وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ﴾ you enjoyed ﴿بِهَا فَالْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذَابَ الْهُونِ﴾ i.e. humiliation ﴿بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ you were arrogant ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَبِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ﴾ by it, and you will be punished by it.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ أَخَا عَادٍ﴾ he is Hūd, peace be upon him ﴿إِذْ﴾ etc. is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) ﴿أَنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ﴾ made them fear ﴿بِالْأَحْقَافِ﴾ a valley in Yemen in which their dwellings were ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ﴾ the messengers had passed ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ i.e. before Hūd and after him, to their peoples ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. by his saying ﴿لَا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ﴾ and the clause «قَدْ خَلَتْ» is parenthetical ﴿إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ if you worship other than Allah ﴿عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿قَالُوا أَجِئْتَنَا لِتَأْفِكَنَا عَنْ آلِهَتِنَا﴾ to turn us away from worshipping them ﴿فَأْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَا﴾ of punishment for worshipping them ﴿إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ in that it will come to us.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Hūd ﴿إِنَّمَا الْعِلْمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ He is the One who knows when the punishment will come to you ﴿وَأُبَلِّغُكُمْ مَا أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ﴾ to you ﴿وَلَكِنِّي أَرَاكُمْ قَوْمًا تَجْهَلُونَ﴾ by your seeking to hasten the punishment.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ﴾ i.e. what the punishment was ﴿عَارِضًا﴾ a cloud that appeared across the horizon of the sky ﴿مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قَالُوا هَذَا عَارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنَا﴾ i.e. raining upon us. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ of punishment ﴿رِيحٌ﴾ a badal (substitute) of «مَا» ﴿فِيهَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿تُدَمِّرُ﴾ destroys ﴿كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ it passed over ﴿بِأَمْرِ رَبِّهَا﴾ by His will, i.e. everything He willed to destroy by it. So it destroyed their men, their women, their young and their wealth, by flying with all that between the sky and the earth and tearing it apart; and Hūd and those who believed with him remained ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا لَا يُرَى إِلَّا مَسَاكِنُهُمْ كَذَلِكَ﴾ as We recompensed them ﴿نَجْزِي الْقَوْمَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ others besides them.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِيمَا﴾ in that which ﴿إِنْ﴾ negating (nāfiya) or redundant (zāʾida) ﴿مَكَّنَّاكُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿فِيهِ﴾ of strength and wealth ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ سَمْعًا﴾ in the meaning of «أَسْمَاعًا» (hearings) ﴿وَأَبْصَارًا وَأَفْئِدَةً﴾ hearts ﴿فَمَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَلَا أَبْصَارُهُمْ وَلَا أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ i.e. anything of avail; «مِنْ» is redundant ﴿إِذْ﴾ governed by «أَغْنَى», and it has been imbued with the meaning of causation ﴿كَانُوا يَجْحَدُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ His clear proofs ﴿وَحَاقَ﴾ descended ﴿بِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ i.e. the punishment.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا مَا حَوْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْقُرَى﴾ i.e. of their people, such as Thamūd, ʿĀd and the people of Lūṭ ﴿وَصَرَّفْنَا الْآيَاتِ﴾ We repeated the clear proofs ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿فَلَوْلَا﴾ why then did not ﴿نَصَرَهُمْ﴾ by warding off the punishment from them ﴿الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿قُرْبَانًا﴾ as a means of drawing near through them to Allah ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ alongside Him, and they are the idols. The first object of «اتَّخَذَ» is an omitted pronoun referring back to the relative noun, i.e. «هُمْ» (them); «قُرْبَانًا» is the second, and «آلِهَةً» is a badal (substitute) of it ﴿بَلْ ضَلُّوا﴾ they disappeared ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ when the punishment came down ﴿وَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. their taking the idols as gods as a means of nearness ﴿إِفْكُهُمْ﴾ their lie ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ they lie; «مَا» is maṣdariyya (infinitival) or a relative noun, with the referring pronoun omitted, i.e. «فِيهِ» (in it).

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ صَرَفْنَا﴾ We inclined ﴿إِلَيْكَ نَفَرًا مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ the jinn of Naṣībīn in Yemen, or the jinn of Nīnawā; they were seven or nine, and he ﷺ was at Baṭn Nakhl leading his Companions in the dawn prayer; the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim] narrated it ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ الْقُرْآنَ فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قَالُوا﴾ i.e. some of them said to others ﴿أَنْصِتُوا﴾ listen attentively to hear it ﴿فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ﴾ its recitation was finished ﴿وَلَّوْا﴾ they went back ﴿إِلَى قَوْمِهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ﴾ making their people fear the punishment if they did not believe; they had been Jews, and they became Muslims.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا قَوْمَنَا إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا كِتَابًا﴾ it is the Quran ﴿أُنْزِلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسَى مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ i.e. what preceded it, such as the Torah ﴿يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ﴾ Islam ﴿وَإِلَى طَرِيقٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ i.e. its path.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿يَا قَوْمَنَا أَجِيبُوا دَاعِيَ اللَّهِ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ ﴿إِلَى الْإِيمَانِ ﴿وَآمِنُوا بِهِ يَغْفِرْ﴾ [Translator's note: the bracketing is as printed in the source; «إِلَى الْإِيمَانِ» ("to faith") is al-Jalalayn's gloss and not Quranic text.] Allah ﴿لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ i.e. some of them, because among them are wrongs done to others, which are not forgiven except with the consent of those wronged ﴿وَيُجِرْكُمْ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ painful.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَمَنْ لَا يُجِبْ دَاعِيَ اللَّهِ فَلَيْسَ بِمُعْجِزٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ i.e. he cannot frustrate Allah by fleeing from Him and so escape Him ﴿وَلَيْسَ لَهُ﴾ for the one who does not answer ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ i.e. Allah ﴿أَوْلِيَاءُ﴾ helpers who would ward off the punishment from him ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ who did not answer ﴿فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear, manifest.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ know, i.e. the deniers of the resurrection ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ﴾ was not incapable of it ﴿بِقَادِرٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «أَنَّ»; the bāʾ was added in it because the statement has the force of «أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِقَادِرٍ» ("Is not Allah able?") ﴿عَلَى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتَى بَلَى﴾ He is able to give life to the dead ﴿إِنَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ by being punished in it; it will be said to them: ﴿أَلَيْسَ هَذَا﴾ punishment ﴿بِالْحَقِّ قَالُوا بَلَى وَرَبِّنَا قَالَ فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ on the harm of your people ﴿كَمَا صَبَرَ أُولُوا الْعَزْمِ﴾ those possessed of patience and steadfastness in hardships ﴿مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ before you, so that you become one possessed of resolve. «مِنْ» is for explanation (bayān), so all of them are possessed of resolve; and it is said it is partitive (tabʿīḍ), so Ādam is not among them, because of His saying, Exalted is He, {وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا}, nor Yūnus, because of His saying, Exalted is He, {وَلَا تَكُنْ كَصَاحِبِ الْحُوتِ} ﴿وَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلْ لَهُمْ﴾ for your people the descent of the punishment upon them. It is said: it was as if he had become weary of them and wished the punishment to descend upon them, so he was commanded to be patient and to stop seeking to hasten the punishment, for it will descend upon them inevitably ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ مَا يُوعَدُونَ﴾ of punishment in the Hereafter, because of its length ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا﴾ in this world, in their estimation ﴿إِلَّا سَاعَةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ﴾ this Quran is ﴿بَلَاغٌ﴾ a conveyance from Allah to you ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ i.e. «لَا» (not) ﴿يُهْلَكُ﴾ at the sight of the punishment ﴿إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers.

daas-irab:1-5.t: ﴿حم﴾ ﴿تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ﴾ their i'rab has preceded in Sūrat al-Jāthiya. ﴿ما خَلَقْنَا﴾ mā is negative, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ its object. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to السماوات. ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to الأرض. ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause mā خلقنا is resumptive. ﴿وَأَجَلٍ﴾ conjoined to الحق. ﴿مُسَمًّى﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَمَّا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to معرضون. ﴿أُنْذِرُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of الذين; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle of rebuke (tawbīkh), and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ its object; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿تَدْعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَرُونِي﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the speaker is its object; the clause أروني is a tawkīd (emphasis). ﴿ماذا﴾ a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of خلقوا. ﴿خَلَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause ماذا خلقوا is the second object of أرأيتم. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of bal, for digression (iḍrāb). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿شِرْكٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to shirk. ﴿ائْتُونِي﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, the nūn is for protection, and the yāʾ of the speaker is a mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِكِتابٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of كتاب. ﴿هذا﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَثارَةٍ﴾ conjoined to كتاب. ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of أثارة. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ its khabar; the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَضَلُّ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أضل. ﴿يَدْعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a mafʿūl bihi of يدعو. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَسْتَجِيبُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila of man. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿إِلى يَوْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَنْ دُعائِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to غافلون. ﴿غافِلُونَ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:6-8.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and إذا is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿حُشِرَ النَّاسُ﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَعْداءً﴾ the khabar (predicate) of كانوا; the clause كانوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَكانُوا﴾ a conjunction, and kāna and its noun. ﴿بِعِبادَتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar كافرين; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كافِرِينَ﴾ the khabar of kāna. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ like the preceding one. ﴿تُتْلى﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿آياتُنا﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾ ḥāl; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لِلْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قال. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ adverbial, of time (ḥīniyya). ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿هذا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and مبين is an adjective (ṣifa); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of bal. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿افْتَراهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the object of the saying, and the clause يقولون is resumptive. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِنِ﴾ conditional. ﴿افْتَرَيْتُهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and lā is negative. ﴿تَمْلِكُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the clause qul is resumptive. ﴿لِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أعلم. ﴿تُفِيضُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila of mā. ﴿كَفى﴾ a past verb. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and the hāʾ is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of كفى. ﴿شَهِيداً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿بَيْنِي﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾ conjoined to بيني. ﴿وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ and two khabars; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:9-11.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿كُنْتُ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿بِدْعاً﴾ its khabar (predicate); the verbal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause qul is resumptive. ﴿مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) بدعا. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is negative. ﴿أَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is circumstantial. ﴿ما﴾ interrogative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُفْعَلُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of أدري. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is negative. ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative. ﴿أَتَّبِعُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿يُوحى﴾ a passive imperfect verb; its nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is negative. ﴿أَنَا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿نَذِيرٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of نذير; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying, and the clause qul is resumptive. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of kāna. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَكَفَرْتُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ بَنِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to شاهد. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلى مِثْلِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to shahida. ﴿فَآمَنَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْقَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ an adjective; the clause يهدي is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قال. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿كانَ خَيْراً﴾ kāna and its khabar, its noun being latent; the clause is initial. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿سَبَقُونا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time. ﴿لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فَسَيَقُولُونَ﴾ a conjunction, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿هذا إِفْكٌ قَدِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and قديم is an adjective; the nominal clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:12-14.t: ﴿وَمِنْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and min is a preposition. ﴿قَبْلِهِ﴾ a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿كِتابُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مُوسى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِماماً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَرَحْمَةً﴾ conjoined to إماما; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهذا كِتابٌ﴾ a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿مُصَدِّقٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿لِساناً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿عَرَبِيًّا﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مصدق. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَبُشْرى﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بشرى; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اسْتَقامُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to قالوا. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and lā is negative. ﴿خَوْفٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿وَلا﴾ a conjunction, and lā is negative. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدين. ﴿جَزاءً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جزاء. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause أولئك… is a second khabar of inna.

daas-irab:15-16.t: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِوالِدَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿إِحْساناً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿حَمَلَتْهُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿أُمُّهُ﴾ a postponed fāʿil. ﴿كُرْهاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl). ﴿وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهاً﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَحَمْلُهُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَفِصالُهُ﴾ conjoined to حمله. ﴿ثَلاثُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw. ﴿شَهْراً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of beginning (ibtidāʾ). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿بَلَغَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَشُدَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and the clause ﴿وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿سَنَةً﴾ tamyīz. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive, and has no grammatical position. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker. ﴿أَوْزِعْنِي﴾ a verb of supplication; its fāʿil is latent, the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْ أَشْكُرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, with its fāʿil latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of أوزعني. ﴿نِعْمَتَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of ashkura. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿أَنْعَمْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيَّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَلى والِدَيَّ﴾ conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صالِحاً﴾ conjoined to an ashkura نعمتك. ﴿تَرْضاهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is an adjective of عملا. [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is صالِحاً.] ﴿وَأَصْلِحْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the verb is conjoined to أوزعني. ﴿لِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿تُبْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِنِّي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of inna; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿نَتَقَبَّلُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿أَحْسَنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ما﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَنَتَجاوَزُ عَنْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to nataqabbalu, and ﴿فِي أَصْحابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَعْدَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿الصِّدْقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila of الذي.

daas-irab:17-19.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لِوالِدَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي. ﴿أُفٍّ﴾ a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, in the sense of "I am vexed" (أتضجر). ﴿لَكُما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to uffin. ﴿أَتَعِدانِنِي﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil and its object. ﴿أَنْ أُخْرَجَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أتعدانني. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿خَلَتِ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الْقُرُونُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿وَهُما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَسْتَغِيثانِ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the alif is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of هما, and the nominal clause is circumstantial. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَيْلَكَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿آمِنْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause آمن is the object of an implied saying. ﴿إِنَّ وَعْدَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a fatḥa (اللَّهَ); as muḍāf ilayhi it is اللَّهِ.] ﴿حَقٌّ﴾ the khabar of inna; the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl). ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿هذا﴾ mubtadaʾ; the verbal clause is conjoined to the implied clause before it. [Translator's note: this remark on the verbal clause evidently refers to فيقول; it stands here in the source.] ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَساطِيرُ﴾ khabar. ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of الذي in the previous verse. ﴿حَقَّ﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْقَوْلُ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي أُمَمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realization. ﴿خَلَتْ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of umam. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَالْإِنْسِ﴾ conjoined to al-jinn. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿خاسِرِينَ﴾ its khabar; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation. ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and li-kullin is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿دَرَجاتٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ an adjective of درجات. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit an after the lām of causation, with its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is its first object. ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ its second object; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He requited them" (جازاهم). ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:20-21.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿يُعْرَضُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يعرض; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). [Translator's note: so in the source; the remark on the ṣila evidently belongs to كفروا.] ﴿أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿فِي حَياتِكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to adhhabtum; the clause is the object of an implied saying (maqūl qawl muqaddar). ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of حياتكم. ﴿وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an adverb of time. ﴿تُجْزَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْهُونِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to tujzawna. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of kuntum, and the clause kuntum is the ṣila. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ﴾ conjoined to بما kuntum. ﴿وَاذْكُرْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَخا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عادٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) of أخا ʿĀd. ﴿أَنْذَرَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿قَوْمَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, with the fāʿil latent; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿بِالْأَحْقافِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khalat. ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا﴾ an is lightened from the heavy anna, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); lā is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to andhara. ﴿أَلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). [Translator's note: the source prints the word as أَلَّا; the particle of restriction in the verse is إِلَّا.] ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَخافُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl) of the worship. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَظِيمٍ﴾ an adjective.

daas-irab:22-24.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَجِئْتَنا﴾ the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī), and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لِتَأْفِكَنا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl); nā is its object and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿عَنْ آلِهَتِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فَأْتِنا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; nā is its object and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿تَعِدُنا﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿كُنْتَ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar (predicate); the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes it indicates it. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿الْعِلْمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَأُبَلِّغُكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its first object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿ما﴾ its second object. ﴿أُرْسِلْتُ﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلكِنِّي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lākinna and its noun. ﴿أَراكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ its second object; the clause أراكم is the khabar of لكني. ﴿تَجْهَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of qawman. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and mā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. [Translator's note: so in the source ("mā"); the particle meant is لما.] ﴿رَأَوْهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿عارِضاً﴾ an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مُسْتَقْبِلَ﴾ an adjective of عارضا. ﴿أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿هذا عارِضٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of the saying. ﴿مُمْطِرُنا﴾ an adjective of عارض. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿هُوَ مَا﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of an omitted saying. ﴿اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿رِيحٌ﴾ a badal (substitute) of mā. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is an adjective of ريح.

daas-irab:25-27.t: ﴿تُدَمِّرُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is a second adjective (ṣifa) of ريح. ﴿بِأَمْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿رَبِّها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أصبح and its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُرى﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مَساكِنُهُمْ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause يرى is the khabar (predicate) of أصبحوا, and the clause فأصبحوا is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿نَجْزِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْقَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ an adjective; the verbal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive, the lām is [that of] the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿مَكَّنَّاهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِيما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿إِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿مَكَّنَّاكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَمْعاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَبْصاراً وَأَفْئِدَةً﴾ both conjoined to سمعا. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and mā is negative. ﴿أَغْنى﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَمْعُهُمْ﴾ the fāʿil of أغنى. ﴿وَلا أَبْصارُهُمْ وَلا أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ﴾ the words are conjoined to سمعهم. ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, a mafʿūl muṭlaq; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time, conveying the sense of causation (taʿlīl). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿بِآياتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَحاقَ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يستهزئون. ﴿يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ see the previous verse. ﴿أَهْلَكْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ its object. ﴿حَوْلَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿مِنَ الْقُرى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَصَرَّفْنَا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْآياتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ لعل and its noun. ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لعل, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:28-30.t: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿نَصَرَهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿اتَّخَذُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿قُرْباناً﴾ ḥāl; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb اتخذوا. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿ضَلُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِفْكُهُمْ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to ifkuhum. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا. ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿صَرَفْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿نَفَراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of nafaran. ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ a conjunction, and لما is an adverbial conditional particle. ﴿حَضَرُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَنْصِتُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause قالوا is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive, and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ a conjunction, and لما is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿قُضِيَ﴾ a passive past verb; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَلَّوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مُنْذِرِينَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا قَوْمَنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿سَمِعْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿كِتاباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of إنا. ﴿أُنْزِلَ﴾ a passive past verb; its nāʾib fāʿil is latent, and the clause is an adjective of كتابا. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مُوسى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ an adjective of كتابا. ﴿لِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to مصدقا. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is an adjective of كتابا. ﴿إِلَى الْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِلى طَرِيقٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ an adjective of طريق.

daas-irab:31-33.t: ﴿يا قَوْمَنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿أَجِيبُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿داعِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَآمِنُوا﴾ conjoined to أجيبوا. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿يَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), with its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb. ﴿وَيُجِرْكُمْ﴾ conjoined to yaghfir, and the kāf is its object. ﴿مِنْ عَذابٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the verse is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and man is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُجِبْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), with its fāʿil latent. ﴿داعِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلَيْسَ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿بِمُعْجِزٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of laysa; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause man lā yujib is resumptive. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to معجز; the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of man. ﴿وَلَيْسَ﴾ a conjunction, and a defective past verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَوْلِياءُ﴾ the postponed noun of laysa. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ khabar. ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾ an interrogative particle, the wāw is a conjunction, and lam is a particle causing the jussive. ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective. ﴿خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to السماوات; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلَمْ يَعْيَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِخَلْقِهِنَّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿بِقادِرٍ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and قادر is genitive in form, nominative in position, the khabar of anna; anna with its noun and its khabar stands in place of the two objects of yaraw. ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition. ﴿أَنْ يُحْيِيَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿الْمَوْتى﴾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to قادر. ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قدير. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:34-35.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ its i'rab has preceded in verse 20. ﴿أَلَيْسَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of rebuking interrogation (istifhām tawbīkhī), and laysa is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿هذا﴾ its noun. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of laysa; the clause is the object of an implied saying (maqūl qawl muqaddar). ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَرَبِّنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "we swear by our Lord" (nuqsimu بربنا). ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ its object; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ذوقوا. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَكْفُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of kuntum. ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a particle of comparison and of the genitive, and mā is maṣdariyya (yielding a verbal noun). ﴿صَبَرَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿أُولُوا﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الْعَزْمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial); mā and the verb are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb. ﴿وَلا تَسْتَعْجِلْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, lā is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ كأن and its noun. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of كأن, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ساعَةً﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿مِنْ نَهارٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿بَلاغٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "this Qur'an is a proclamation" (هذا al-Qurʾān بلاغ). ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and hal is an interrogative particle. ﴿يُهْلَكُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿الْقَوْمُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿الْفاسِقُونَ﴾ an adjective.

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأثارة) With fatḥa on the hamza: a remnant of knowledge, an inherited noble trait, and a glorious deed; from their saying "the she-camel grew fat upon an athāra of fat", which is the remnant of it. From Ibn al-Aʿrābī: "so-and-so angered me upon an athāra of anger", i.e. on the trace of an anger that had been before that. And they have an athāra of knowledge, i.e. a remnant of it which they transmit (yaʾthurūnahā) from the ancients. One says: "the Banū so-and-so have an athāra of nobility" when they have ancient testimonies to it, and in other things. Al-Rāʿī said:
وذات أثارة أكلت علينا ... نباتا في أكمته قفارا
(And a she-camel with a remnant [of fat], which grazed, to our cost, on plants in its hillocks bare of all else.)
I.e. a remnant of fat. Al-Wāḥidī said: the speech of the lexicographers on this word revolves around three views. The first: al-athāra, derived from "athartu al-shayʾa uthīruhu athāratan", as though it were a remnant that is brought out and stirred up (tustathār). The second: from al-athar, which is narration (riwāya). The third: from al-athar in the sense of a sign.

* I'rab:
(حم تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ) (حم): the discussion of the openings of the surahs has already been given. (تنزيل الكتاب) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (من الله); and (العزيز الحكيم) are two naʿts (adjectives). (ما خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى) (ما) is negating; (خلقنا السموات): a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (بالحق) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. a creation bound up with the truth. The wāw is a conjunction; (أجل) is conjoined to (الحق), and (مسمى) is an adjective. (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَمَّا أُنْذِرُوا مُعْرِضُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (عمّا) are attached to (معرضون); the clause (أنذروا) is a ṣila, and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. "from what they were warned of"; and (معرضون) is the khabar of (الذين). It is also permissible for (ما) to be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. from their being warned of that Day. (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَرُونِي ماذا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ) (قل) is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) agent; (أرأيتم) is a verb and its agent; (ما) is a direct object; the clause (تدعون) is the ṣila; (من دون الله) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (أروني) is an imperative verb with its agent and its object, and the clause is a tawkīd (emphasis) of (أرأيتم). The clause (ماذا خلقوا) is the second object of (أرأيتم); (ماذا) is a fronted object of (خلقوا); or (ما) is a mubtadaʾ and (ذا) a relative noun as its khabar, with the clause (خلقوا) as its ṣila. It is also permissible that (أروني) not be an emphasis of (أرأيتم), so that the matter belongs to the chapter of rivalry [of two governing words] (al-tanāzuʿ), because (أرأيتم) requires a second object and so does (أروني), and His words (ماذا خلقوا) are what they compete for. The text of Abū Ḥayyān's wording: «(قل أرأيتم ما تدعون) means: inform me about those whom you call upon besides Allah — and they are the idols. (أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض) is an interrogation of rebuke. The first object of (أرأيتم) is (ما تدعون), and (ماذا خلقوا) is an interrogative clause that (أرأيتم) requires, because its second object is an interrogative, and (أروني) requires it by way of suspension (taʿlīq). So this belongs to the chapter of governing (al-iʿmāl): the second was made to govern, and the second object of (أرأيتم) was omitted. It is possible that (أروني) is an emphasis of (أرأيتم) in the sense of "inform me", as though they have one meaning. Ibn ʿUqba said: (أرأيتم) admits two aspects: one, that it be transitive and (ما) its object; and it is possible that (أرأيتم) be a word of alerting, not transitive, with (ما) being interrogative in the sense of rebuke, and (تدعون) meaning "you worship".» [Translator's note: "Ibn ʿUqba" is as printed; Abū Ḥayyān here is likely quoting Ibn ʿAṭiyya.] End of quote. That (أرأيتم) is intransitive and a word of alerting is somewhat doubtful; al-Akhfash said it regarding His words (قال أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة). What appears is that (ما تدعون) is the object of (أرأيتم), as in His words (قل أرأيتم شركاءكم الذين تدعون) in Sūrat Fāṭir, where the discussion of the counterpart of this clause has been given; and the discussion of (أرأيتم) was given in Sūrat al-Anʿām.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is as printed; the quotation from Abū Ḥayyān apparently continues to this point.] (من الأرض) is a ḥāl, because it explains the vague element in (ماذا خلقوا). (أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ فِي السَّماواتِ ائْتُونِي بِكِتابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ هذا أَوْ أَثارَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) (أم) is in the sense of the hamza of disapproval and the bal of digression (al-iḍrābiyya), so it is disjoined (munqaṭiʿa): it is as though He turned from the first interrogation to asking whether they have a share with Allah in the creation of the heavens and the earth, for shirk here means sharing. (لهم) is a fronted khabar and (شرك) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) are attached to (شرك). (ائتوني) is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object, and the clause is part of the completion of what is said; (بكتاب) are attached to (ائتوني); (من قبل هذا) is an adjective of (كتاب), i.e. existing from before this. (أو) is a conjunction; (أثارة) is conjoined to (بكتاب), and (من علم) is an adjective of (أثارة). (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then bring me [it]"; (صادقين) is the khabar of (كنتم). (وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ يَدْعُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَنْ لا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is an interrogative noun whose meaning is disapproval, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (أضل) is the khabar; (ممّن) are attached to (أضل); the clause (يدعو) is the ṣila of (من); (من دون الله) is a ḥāl; (من) is the object of (يدعو), and the clause (لا يستجيب له) is the ṣila. They also permitted (من) to be a complete, described indefinite noun, so that the clause (لا يستجيب له) is an adjective. (إلى يوم القيامة) is a ḥāl. The meaning of the limit will come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَهُمْ عَنْ دُعائِهِمْ غافِلُونَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (عن دعائهم) are attached to (غافلون); (غافلون) is the khabar of (هم); and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words (إلى يوم القيامة) there is a splendid rhetorical subtlety: He made the Day of Resurrection the limit of their not responding, and it is in the nature of a limit that the meaning ends at it; yet the non-response continues after this limit, because on the Day of Resurrection too they will not respond to them. The right view is that it is one of those limits which indicate that what comes after them, even if it agrees with what precedes, exceeds it by a clear increase that attaches it to the second [state], so that the two states, though of one kind, are — because of the disparity between them — like a thing and its opposite. For the first state, whose limit is made the Resurrection, does not go beyond non-response, while the second state, on the Resurrection, adds to non-response enmity and the disowning of their worship of them. So it is of the same kind as what preceded in Sūrat al-Zukhruf in His words: (بل متّعت هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى جاءهم الحق ورسول مبين ولما جاء الحق قالوا: هذا سحر وإنّا به كافرون).
2- Predominance (al-taghlīb): the rational was given predominance over the non-rational, by way of going along [with them] (al-mujārāh), because the worshippers of idols used to describe them as having discernment, out of ignorance and stupidity.

dervis-irab:6-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِدْعاً) There are two views on it. One: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and so it involves the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being "one of novelty" (dhā bidʿ). The second: that bidʿ is itself an adjective on the pattern fiʿl in the sense of badīʿ (novel), like khiff and khafīf (light) and ḥibb and ḥabīb (beloved). The discussion of al-badīʿ has already been given at length, and that it is that whose like has never been seen, from al-ibtidāʿ, which is invention.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا حُشِرَ النَّاسُ كانُوا لَهُمْ أَعْداءً وَكانُوا بِعِبادَتِهِمْ كافِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (حشر الناس) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (الناس) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause (كانوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (كان) and its noun; (لهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and (أعداء) is the khabar (predicate) of (كانوا). (وكانوا) is conjoined to the first (وكانوا); (بعبادتهم) are attached to (كافرين); the hāʾ is annexed to (عبادة) as an annexation of the maṣdar to its object, i.e. "their being worshipped"; and (كافرين) is the khabar of (كانوا). (وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ قالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَهُمْ هذا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا) is conjoined to what preceded; (بيّنات) is a ḥāl; and the clause (قال الذين كفروا) is the apodosis of (إذا), with no grammatical position. (للحق) are attached to (قالوا). The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «The lām in (للحق) is the lām of connection (lām al-ṣila), i.e. on account of the truth.» (لما) is temporal ("when") or linking; (جاءهم) is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent). (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (سحر) a khabar and (مبين) a naʿt (adjective); and the clause is the object of their saying. (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ قُلْ إِنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ فَلا تَمْلِكُونَ لِي مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً) (أم) is in the sense of bal and the hamza of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī): He turned from mentioning their calling it magic to mentioning their saying that Muḥammad fabricated it and wove its style of his own making — and that is more hideous than what came before, even though both spring from one source deeply sunk in error and disbelief. The clause (افتراه) is the object of their saying. (قل) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (إن) is conditional; (افتريته) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition; (لا) is negating; (تملكون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its agent; (لي) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تملكون); (من الله) is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective and was placed before what it describes; and (شيئا) is a direct object. (هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِما تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ) The clause is circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (أعلم) a khabar; (بما) are attached to (أعلم), and the clause (تفيضون فيه) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (كَفى بِهِ شَهِيداً بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ) (كفى) is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and the hāʾ is a pronoun genitive in form, in the position of nominative as the agent; (شهيدا) is a tamyīz (specification); (بيني) is an adverb attached to (شهيدا), and (بينكم) an adverb conjoined to its like. The wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, and (الغفور الرحيم) are two khabars of it. (قُلْ ما كُنْتُ بِدْعاً مِنَ الرُّسُلِ وَما أَدْرِي ما يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلا بِكُمْ) (قل) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (ما) is negating; (كان) and its noun, and (بدعا) is its khabar; (من الرسل) is a naʿt of (بدعا). (ما) is conjoined to the first negating (ما); (أدري) is a nominative imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "we" [Translator's note: so in the source; the latent pronoun of (أدري) is "I" (أنا)]. (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يفعل), in the passive, is its khabar; it suspends (أدري) from governing, so it stands in place of its two objects. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The (ما) in (ما يفعل) may be a relative noun in the accusative, or an interrogative in the nominative.» (بي) are attached to (يفعل), and (ولا بكم) is conjoined to it. (إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا ما يُوحى إِلَيَّ وَما أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) (إن) is negating; (أتبع) is a nominative imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "I"; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ما) is the object of (أتبع), and the clause (يوحى إليّ) is the ṣila. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (أنا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (نذير) is a khabar and (مبين) a naʿt.

dervis-irab:10-14.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ) The clause (أرأيتم) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The two objects of (أرأيتم) are omitted, their implied form being "Have you considered your state if such-and-such were the case — are you not wrongdoers?" The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is also omitted, its implied form being "then you have done wrong". Al-Zamakhsharī supplied it as "are you not wrongdoers?", and Abū Ḥayyān rebutted him: were it so, the fāʾ would be obligatory, because when an interrogative clause occurs as the apodosis of a condition the fāʾ is required; then, if the interrogative particle is the hamza, it precedes the fāʾ, as in "if you visit us, do we then not honour you (a-fa-mā nukrimuka)?", and if it is something else, the fāʾ precedes it, as in "if you visit us, then do you see anything but good (fa-hal tarā)?". It was also said that the apodosis is (فآمن واستكبرتم); and it was said that it is omitted, its implied form being "then who among us is in the right and who is in the wrong?"; and it was said: "then who is further astray?". The noun of (كان) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it", and (من عند الله) is its khabar (predicate). (وكفرتم): the wāw is a conjunction and the clause (كفرتم) is conjoined to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); al-Jalāl and al-Samīn chose that it be circumstantial. (به) are attached to (كفرتم). (وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (شهد شاهد) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (من بني إسرائيل) is an adjective of (شاهد); (على مثله) are attached to (شهد). The pronoun refers back to the Qur'an, i.e. to the like of the Qur'an in the meanings found in the Torah that correspond to it — the affirmation of divine unity, the resurrection, the raising, and other matters. This likeness is in respect of the correspondence of meanings, even if the wordings differ. (فَآمَنَ وَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (آمن) is a verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "he", i.e. the witness; (استكبرتم) is conjoined to (فآمن). (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يهدي القوم الظالمين) is the khabar. (وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْ كانَ خَيْراً ما سَبَقُونا إِلَيْهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (قال الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (للذين) are attached to (قال), and the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila. (لو) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb whose noun is latent, referring to what Muḥammad brought; (خيرا) is its khabar. (ما) is negating; (سبقونا) is a verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إليه) are attached to (سبقونا). The [whole] clause is the object of the saying, and the clause (ما سبقونا إليه) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا بِهِ فَسَيَقُولُونَ هذا إِفْكٌ قَدِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "their obstinacy became manifest", and His words (فسيقولون) are caused by it. (فسيقولون) does not govern (إذ) because the two times contradict each other, and also because of the fāʾ. It was also said: if there is no obstacle to (فسيقولون) governing the adverb except the incompatibility of indicating past and future, this is no obstacle, for the future here is only used to signal the continuation of what has occurred and passed; because the people were deprived of guidance and said "this is an ancient falsehood", "tales of the ancients", and so on. So the meaning of the verse is then: and they said, when they were not guided by it, "this is an ancient falsehood", and they continued in that and persisted in it; so its occurrence and then its continuation were expressed with the future form — just as Ibrāhīm said (إلا الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين), when guidance had already occurred and passed, but he spoke of its occurrence and then its continuation and so expressed it with the future form; and this is the way to reconcile His words (سيهدين) with His words in the other [verse] (فهو يهدين). Were it not for the fāʾ entering the verb, what we have mentioned would be the right view; but the causative fāʾ, by entering, indicated an omitted element which is the cause, and cut the verb off from the preceding adverb, so it became necessary to supply the omitted element as what governs it.
Abū al-Suʿūd said in his tafsīr: «(وإذ لم يهتدوا به) is an adverb of an omitted element indicated by what precedes it and on which what follows it is consequent, i.e. and since they were not guided by the Qur'an they said what they said; (فسيقولون), not content with denying its goodness, (هذا إفك قديم), just as they said "tales of the ancients". It was said that the omitted element is "their obstinacy became manifest", but that is not quite it.» The wording of al-Karkhī: «His words (وإذ لم يهتدوا) are an adverb of an omitted element such as "their obstinacy became manifest", not of His words (فسيقولون), because that is for the future while (إذ) is for the past. It may also be said that (إذ) is causal, not adverbial; or it may be said that (فسيقولون) expresses continuity across the three times, with the sīn merely for emphasis. As for the fāʾ, it does not prevent governing what precedes it, as al-Raḍī and others stated explicitly; and the causation may be from their disbelief.»
(لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past meaning] and jussive; (يهتدوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and the wāw is the agent. The fāʾ is a conjunction; the sīn is a particle of the future; (يقولون) is a nominative imperfect verb and its agent; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (إفك) a khabar and (قديم) an adjective; and the nominal clause is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying. (وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ كِتابُ مُوسى إِماماً وَرَحْمَةً) The wāw is resumptive; (من قبله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (كتاب موسى) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and (إماما) and (رحمة) are two ḥāls (circumstantials) of (كتاب موسى). The implied form is: and the Book of Mūsā exists from before the Qur'an, in the state of being a guide and a mercy. (وَهذا كِتابٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِساناً عَرَبِيًّا لِيُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَبُشْرى لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ)
The wāw is a conjunction; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ, (كتاب) a khabar and (مصدّق) an adjective; (لسانا) is a ḥāl of the pronoun in (مصدّق) or of (كتاب), and what governs it is the meaning of the demonstrative. Abū al-Baqāʾ parsed it as a direct object of (مصدّق), in which case the reference is to something other than the Qur'an. It was also said that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in an Arabic tongue". Abū Ḥayyān permitted all these aspects. The lām is causal; (ينذر) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (مصدق); or it is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (الذين) is a direct object, and the clause (ظلموا) is the ṣila. (بشرى) is conjoined to the position of (لينذر) if it is an object of purpose; and it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and it is glad tidings"; (للمحسنين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (بشرى). (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ قالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا) (إن) and its noun; the clause (قالوا) is the ṣila; (ربنا) is a mubtadaʾ and (الله) a khabar, and the reverse is permissible; (ثم) is a conjunction, and the clause (استقاموا) is conjoined to the clause (قالوا). (فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of (إن), because of the scent of condition in the relative noun. Al-Samīn said: «The fāʾ is redundant in the khabar of the relative noun because of the sense of condition in it; and (إن) did not prevent that, because the meaning of al-intidāb remains [Translator's note: so in the print; probably a misprint for al-ibtidāʾ, "the subject–predicate relation"], unlike laʿalla, layta and kaʾanna.» Sībawayh holds that (إن) is supposed to be removed, and then the fāʾ entered the khabar of (الذين). (لا) is negating; (خوف) is a mubtadaʾ, allowed to begin the sentence [though indefinite] because the negation precedes it; and (عليهم) is the khabar. (ولا هم يحزنون) is conjoined to the preceding clause, and the clause (فلا خوف عليهم) is the khabar of (إن). (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ خالِدِينَ فِيها جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and (أصحاب الجنة) its khabar; (خالدين فيها) is a ḥāl; (جزاء) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) made accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense", and Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted parsing it as a ḥāl.
