(بما) are attached to (جزاء); (ما) is a relative noun or maṣdariyya; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يعملون) is its khabar; and the clause [أولئك أصحاب الجنة] is a second khabar of (إن).

dervis-irab:15-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَفِصالُهُ) In al-Mukhtār: «al-fiṣāl is weaning (al-fiṭām).» It was also read (وفصله); faṣl and fiṣāl are like ʿaẓm and ʿiẓām in form and meaning [Translator's note: so in the source]. What is meant by it will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ) The explanation of al-ashudd has been given before. The wording of al-Kashshāf: «Reaching al-ashudd is that he enters mature age and completes the age at which his strength, intellect and discernment become firm, and that is when he passes thirty and approaches forty.»
(أَوْزِعْنِي) Inspire me; its explanation has been given before.

* I'rab:
(وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ إِحْساناً) Resumptive speech, introduced to show the lesson in the varying state of a person with his parents: he may obey them and he may oppose them; and as long as a person is grounded in this disposition, the like of this with the Prophet ﷺ is not far-fetched. (وصينا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (الإنسان) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بوالديه) are attached to (وصّينا); and (إحسانا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) made accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. We enjoined him to do good to them with a doing of good. It was also said that it is a direct object, with (وصينا) carrying the meaning of "We made binding", so that it is a second object; and it was said rather that it is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. We enjoined him concerning them out of beneficence from Us towards them. It was also read (حسنا), and its i'rab is as above. (حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهاً وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهاً) The clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for the injunction mentioned. (حملته أمه): a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent. (كرها), with ḍamma or fatḥa on the kāf — it has been read with both — is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent, i.e. "in a state of hardship"; it may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a hard carrying". (ووضعته كرها) is conjoined to what preceded. (وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصالُهُ ثَلاثُونَ شَهْراً) The wāw is of ḥāl; (حمله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (فصاله) is conjoined to (حمله); (ثلاثون) is the khabar (predicate) and (شهرا) a tamyīz (specification). (حَتَّى إِذا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً) (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive, i.e. and he lived until he reached his full strength. (إذا) is an adverb of future time; the clause (بلغ أشده) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (بلغ) is conjoined to the first (بلغ); (أربعين) is a direct object and (سنة) a tamyīz; and a muḍāf must be supplied, i.e. "the completion of forty". (قالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلى والِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صالِحاً تَرْضاهُ) The clause (قال) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (رب) is a munādā (one addressed) annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, as has been established before. (أوزعني) is an imperative verb used for supplication; (أن) and what is in its domain are in the position of accusative as the object of (أوزعني); (نعمتك) is the object of (أشكر); (التي) is an adjective of (نعمتك), and the clause (أنعمت عليّ) is the ṣila (relative clause). (وأن أعمل) is conjoined to (أن أشكر); (صالحا) is a direct object or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; and the clause (ترضاه) is an adjective of "a deed" (ʿamalan). (وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي إِنِّي تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ) (وأصلح) is conjoined to (أوزعني); (لي) are attached to (أصلح); (في ذريتي) are attached to an omitted ḥāl. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «If you say: what is the meaning of (وأصلح لي في ذريتي)? I say: its meaning is that He make his offspring a place for righteousness and a likely seat of it, as though he said: grant me righteousness in my offspring and make it occur in them.» Better than that is the wording of al-Shihāb al-Khafājī in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī: «That is, the apparent form would have been "make righteous for me my offspring", because iṣlāḥ is transitive, as in His words, Exalted is He, (وأصلحنا له زوجه). So it was said that it was made transitive with fī because it carries the meaning of being gracious, i.e. be gracious to me in my offspring; or it was treated as intransitive and then made transitive with fī to convey the pervasion of righteousness in them and their being like a vessel for it, because of its firmness in them; and this is what the author intended, and it is the best.» (إن) and its noun, and the clause (تبت) is its khabar; (إليك) are attached to (تبت); and (إني من المسلمين) is conjoined to (إني تبت إليك). (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ ما عَمِلُوا) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذين) its khabar; the clause (نتقبل عنهم) is the ṣila; (أحسن) is a direct object; (ما) is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause (عملوا) is the ṣila. (ما) may also be maṣdariyya, i.e. "the best of their deeds". (وَنَتَجاوَزُ عَنْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ فِي أَصْحابِ الْجَنَّةِ وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِي كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ) (ونتجاوز) is conjoined to (نتقبل), falling within the domain of the ṣila; (عن سيئاتهم) are attached to (نتجاوز); and (في أصحاب الجنة) is a ḥāl. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «If you say: what is the meaning of His words (في أصحاب الجنة)? I say: it is like your saying "the emir honoured me among people of his companions", meaning he honoured me among the whole of those he honoured of them and placed me in their number. Its position is accusative as a ḥāl, in the sense of "being among the people of the Garden and counted among them".» Abū al-Baqāʾ and others permitted the preposition and its genitive noun to be in the position of nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are among the people of the Garden". (وعد الصدق) is a maṣdar made accusative by its implied verb, i.e. Allah promised them the promise of truth, i.e. a truthful promise; it is a maṣdar emphasising the content of the preceding clause. (الذي) is an adjective of (وعد الصدق); the clause (كانوا يوعدون) is the ṣila of the relative noun, and the clause (يوعدون) is the khabar of (كانوا). (يوعدون) is a passive nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَالَّذِي قالَ لِوالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَكُما) (والذي) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar will come later; the clause (قال) is the ṣila; (لوالديه) are attached to (قال). (أفّ) is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, meaning "I am vexed"; the discussion of it has been given before. (لكما)
is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, because the lām is for clarification (li-l-bayān). (أَتَعِدانِنِي أَنْ أُخْرَجَ وَقَدْ خَلَتِ الْقُرُونُ مِنْ قَبْلِي) The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (تعدانني) is a nominative imperfect verb, its agent and its direct object; (أن أخرج) is interpreted as a maṣdar, a second object of (تعدانني), or accusative by removal of the preposition; (أخرج) is a passive imperfect verb. (وقد): the wāw is of ḥāl and (قد) is a particle of realisation; (خلت القرون) is a verb and its agent; (من قبلي) are attached to (خلت). (وَهُما يَسْتَغِيثانِ اللَّهَ وَيْلَكَ آمِنْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ فَيَقُولُ ما هذا إِلَّا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (هما) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يستغيثان) is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; and the Name of Majesty is a direct object. Istaghātha is transitive sometimes by itself and at other times with the bāʾ, but in the Qur'an it occurs only as transitive by itself. Al-Rāzī said: «Its meaning is: they seek help from Allah against his disbelief; when the preposition was dropped, the verb reached [the object] directly. It was also said: istighātha is supplication, so there is no need for the bāʾ.» (ويلك) is a maṣdar whose verb the Arabs have let die out, and the clause is governed by an implied saying, i.e. they say "woe to you, believe!"; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. they seek Allah's help, saying… The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «(ويلك) is a maṣdar whose verb is not used; and it was said that it is a direct object, i.e. may Allah make your woe binding on you.» (آمن) is an imperative verb from īmān, and it is part of what they say. (إن) with its noun and khabar, and the clause gives the reason for the command and has no grammatical position. The fāʾ is conjoined to the omitted saying; (ما) is negating; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أساطير الأولين) is the khabar of (هذا); and the clause is the object of the saying.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا» there is a synecdochic trope (majāz mursal) whose relation is adjacency, because al-fiṣāl is weaning, and what is meant by it here is its period, which weaning follows.

* Benefits:
1- These verses contain unique teachings on dutifulness to parents, because honouring them is among the deeds that Allah the Exalted loves, and it equals the reward of striving in His path. No wonder, for Allah has joined His good pleasure to theirs. This has already been mentioned in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, where He, Exalted is He, says: «واعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا»; and He, Exalted is He, said in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt: «ووصّينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما إليّ مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون». Muslim narrated by way of Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd from his father, who said: Umm Saʿd swore that she would never speak to him until he disbelieved in his religion. She said: "You claim that Allah has enjoined you concerning your parents; I am your mother and I command you to do this." Then the verse was revealed. And from Abū Bakra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shall I not tell you of the greatest of the major sins?" — three times. We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to parents." He had been reclining, and he sat up and said: "And beware of false speech and false testimony", and he kept repeating it until we said: "Would that he would stop." Narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. The meaning is: we wished he would stop out of concern for him, because of the signs of his agitation over that which they saw. Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd said: his concern ﷺ with false testimony may be because it occurs more easily among people, they are more careless about it, and its harm occurs more often; for a Muslim recoils from shirk and one's nature recoils from disobedience to parents, but as for false speech, the motives for it are many, so it was fitting to give it attention — and that is not because of its gravity relative to what was mentioned with it.
2- The period of pregnancy: Abū Ḥayyān said: (وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا), i.e. the period of his carrying and his weaning. This can only be if one of the two ends is reduced: either the woman gives birth at six months and suckles for two years, or she gives birth at nine months, as is customary, and suckles for two years less a quarter of a year. If the period of pregnancy increases, the period of suckling decreases, so the period of suckling is a year and nine months, and completing the two years is for whoever wishes to complete the suckling. Experience has shown that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, as the Qur'an states. Galen said: I investigated the length of pregnancy intensively, and I saw a woman who gave birth after one hundred and eighty-four nights; and Ibn Sīnā claimed that he witnessed that. As for the maximum period of pregnancy, there is nothing in the Qur'an indicating it. It is related that Aristotle said: the period of gestation of every animal is fixed except for man; she may give birth at seven months or at eight, and the child seldom survives in the eighth except in certain lands such as Egypt.
3- A subtle point: He, Exalted is He, mentioned the mother in three degrees — in His words (بوالديه), in her carrying him, and in her suckling him, expressed by weaning — and mentioned the father in one, in His words (بوالديه). This accords with what the Messenger said, assigning three quarters of dutifulness to the mother and a quarter to the father, when a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, to whom should I be dutiful?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then whom?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then whom?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then whom?" He said: "Your father."

dervis-irab:18-26.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأحقاف) He said in al-Qāmūs: «al-ḥiqf, with kasra, is a curved stretch of sand; the plural is aḥqāf, ḥiqāf and ḥuqūf, and the plural of the plural is ḥaqāʾif and ḥiqafa; or it is a great round sand-hill, or an elongated overlooking one; or they are elongated sands in the region of al-Shiḥr.» Its commentator said in al-Tāj: «And by it His words, Exalted is He, were explained: "And mention the brother of ʿĀd, when he warned his people at al-Aḥqāf". Al-Jawharī said: and it is the land of ʿĀd. Ibn ʿArafa said: the people of ʿĀd had their dwellings among the sands, and those are al-Aḥqāf. In al-Muʿjam: it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is a valley between ʿUmān and the land of Mahra. Ibn Isḥāq said: al-Aḥqāf is sand between ʿUmān and Ḥaḍramawt. Qatāda said: al-Aḥqāf are sands overlooking Hajar in al-Shiḥr, in the land of Yemen. Yāqūt said: so these are three views that do not differ in meaning.» Also in al-Qāmūs: «al-shajr, like al-manʿ, is opening the mouth; and the seacoast between ʿUmān and ʿAdan; and it may be pronounced with kasra.» [Translator's note: so printed (al-shajr, with jīm); the place-name under discussion is al-Shiḥr, with ḥāʾ.] Abū Ḥayyān said: «al-ḥiqf is an elongated, raised stretch of sand with curvature and bending in it; from it comes iḥqawqafa al-shayʾ, the thing became curved. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فلما أجزنا ساحة الحيّ وانتحى ... بنا بطن خبت ذي حقاف عقنقل
(When we had crossed the tribe's open ground and the hollow of a low plain with winding, piled-up sand-dunes turned aside with us.)»
His commentator al-Zawzanī said: «al-ḥiqf is overlooking, curved sand; the plural is aḥqāf and ḥiqāf.» The wording of al-Kashshāf: «al-Aḥqāf is the plural of ḥiqf, which is elongated raised sand with a bend in it, from iḥqawqafa al-shayʾ when it became curved. ʿĀd were people of pillars, dwelling among sands overlooking the sea in a land called al-Shiḥr, in the country of Yemen; and it was said: between ʿUmān and Mahra.» Ibn Zayd said: «They are sands overlooking the sea, elongated like mountains, but not reaching the point of being mountains.» Muqātil said: the dwellings of ʿĀd were in Yemen, in Ḥaḍramawt, at a place called Mahra, to which the Mahrī camels are attributed. Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī] said, satirising Kāfūr:
ويلمّها خطة ويلم قابلها ... لمثلها خلق المهرية القود
(Woe to such a plan, and woe to the one who accepts it — for the like of it the long-necked Mahrī camels were created [i.e. to flee from it].)
Abū al-Baqāʾ said in his commentary on the Dīwān: al-mahriyya: attributed to Mahra ibn Ḥaydān, a clan of Quḍāʿa.
(عارِضاً) Al-ʿāriḍ: the cloud that spreads across the horizon of the sky. Abū Ḥayyān said: al-ʿāriḍ is the rain-bearing cloud that stretches across the sky; from it is the poet's saying:
يا من رأى عارضا أرقت له ... بين ذراعي وجبهة الأسد
(O you who saw a spreading cloud for which I stayed awake, between the two forearms and the forehead of the Lion [constellation].)
Al-Aʿshā said:
يا من رأى عارضا قد بتّ أرمقه ... كأنه البرق في حافاته الشعل
(O you who saw a spreading cloud that I spent the night watching, as though the lightning on its edges were flames.)

* I'rab:
(أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلُ فِي أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذين) its khabar (predicate); the clause (حق عليهم القول) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (في أمم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the noun made genitive by (على); the clause (قد خلت) is an adjective of (أمم); (من قبلهم) are attached to (خلت); and (من الجن) is a second adjective of (أمم). (إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا خاسِرِينَ) (إن) and its noun, and the clause (كانوا) is its khabar; (خاسرين) is the khabar of (كانوا); and the clause has no grammatical position because it gives a reason. (وَلِكُلٍّ دَرَجاتٌ مِمَّا عَمِلُوا وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ أَعْمالَهُمْ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; (لكل) is a fronted khabar and (درجات) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (مما) is an adjective of (درجات), and the clause (عملوا) is the ṣila. (وليوفّيهم):
the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is causal; (يوفّيهم) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted thing that is given a cause, as though it were said "and He recompensed them with that in order to pay them in full". The hāʾ is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (أعمالهم) a second direct object. The wāw is of ḥāl; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يظلمون) its khabar; and the clause is accusative as an emphatic ḥāl. (وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ فِي حَياتِكُمُ الدُّنْيا وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِها) The wāw is resumptive; (يوم) is an adverb of time attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "it will be said to them, 'You exhausted…', on the day of their being exposed"; the clause (يعرض) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (يعرض) is a passive imperfect verb; (الذين) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (على النار) are attached to (يعرض). (أذهبتم) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (طيباتكم) is a direct object; (في حياتكم) are attached to (أذهبتم); and (الدنيا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (الحياة). More discussion of this verse will come in the section on Rhetoric. (فَالْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الْهُونِ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); (اليوم) is an adverb of time attached to (تجزون); (تجزون) is a passive nominative imperfect verb; (عذاب الهون) is a second direct object; (بما) are attached to (تجزون); (ما) is a relative noun, and it may be maṣdariyya; the clause (كنتم) has no grammatical position; the clause (تستكبرون) is the khabar of (كنتم); (في الأرض) are attached to (تستكبرون); and (بغير الحق) is a ḥāl. (وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ) Conjoined to what preceded; (ما) may be made maṣdariyya or a relative noun, and the maṣdariyya is preferable. (وَاذْكُرْ أَخا عادٍ إِذْ أَنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالْأَحْقافِ) The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to command that the story of ʿĀd be mentioned to these polytheists so that they take warning from it. (اذكر) is an imperative verb, its agent latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (أخا عاد) is a direct object; (إذ) is an adverb of past time, and it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of (أخا عاد), because the brother of ʿĀd — Hūd — is bound up with the time of his warning and what happened to him with them. The clause (أنذر قومه) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; and (بالأحقاف) is a ḥāl of (أخا عاد), and not attached to (أنذر) as appears at first glance, i.e. in the state of their being at al-Aḥqāf; as for the complement of (أنذر), it will come later. (وَقَدْ خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ) The wāw is parenthetical and the clause is parenthetical; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (خلت النذر) is a verb and its agent; (من بين يديه) is a ḥāl, and (من خلفه) is conjoined to (من بين يديه). (أن) is maṣdariyya, or lightened from the heavy [أنّ] with its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and the clause (لا تعبدوا) its khabar; in either case, it together with what it governs is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أنذر). (لا) is prohibitive; (تعبدوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive (لا); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and the Name of Majesty is the object of (تعبدوا). (إِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ) (إن) and its noun, and the clause (أخاف) is its khabar; (عليكم) are attached to (أخاف); (عذاب يوم) is a direct object, and (عظيم) is a naʿt of (يوم); and the clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for the prohibition. (قالُوا أَجِئْتَنا لِتَأْفِكَنا عَنْ آلِهَتِنا) (قالوا) is a verb and its agent; the hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (جئتنا) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; the lām is causal; (تأفكنا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; and (عن آلهتنا) are attached to (تأفكنا). (فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (ائت) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (نا) is a direct object; (بما) are attached to (ائت); and the clause (تعدنا) is the ṣila. (إن) is conditional; (كنت) is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (كنت): (كان) and its noun, and (من الصادقين) is its khabar; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then bring us what you promise us". (قالَ إِنَّمَا الْعِلْمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) (قال) is a past verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "he", i.e. Hūd; (إنما) is the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (العلم) is a mubtadaʾ; (عند الله) is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar; and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَأُبَلِّغُكُمْ ما أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ وَلكِنِّي أَراكُمْ قَوْماً تَجْهَلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, i.e. as for me, my task is only conveying the message, not bringing the punishment, since I am not able to do it; the only One able to do it is Allah the Exalted. (أبلغكم) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "I", and the kāf is a direct object; (ما) is a direct object; the clause (أرسلت) is the ṣila; (أرسلت) is a passive past verb; (به) are attached to (أرسلت). The wāw is a conjunction; (لكن) and its noun, and the clause (أراكم) is its khabar; (قوما) is a second direct object, and the clause (تجهلون) is an adjective of (قوما). (فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عارِضاً مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قالُوا هذا عارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنا) The fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted, implied clause, its implied form being "so they persisted in their insistence and their demand for
the punishment, and it came to them; and when they saw it…". (لما) is temporal ("when") or linking; (رأوه) is a past verb, its agent and its direct object; (عارضا) is a ḥāl, because the seeing is visual; and it was said that it is a tamyīz (specification). (مستقبل أوديتهم) is a naʿt; this is permitted because the annexation is not pure, so it does not make it definite, and it can therefore serve as an adjective of the indefinite noun, i.e. heading and moving towards them. The clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of (لما), which contains the sense of condition in any case. (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ and (عارض) its khabar; (ممطرنا) is a naʿt of (عارض), and the adjective is permitted for the reason given above, i.e. "bringing rain to us". Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj said: the pronoun in (رأوه) refers to something not mentioned, which is made clear by His words (عارضا); so the pronoun refers to the cloud, i.e. when they saw the cloud spreading across. (بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ رِيحٌ فِيها عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) (بل) is a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb) — Hūd said that. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (ما) the khabar; the clause (استعجلتم) is the ṣila, and (به) belongs to the ṣila; (ريح) is a badal (substitute) of (ما), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a wind"; (فيها) is a fronted khabar, (عذاب) a postponed mubtadaʾ and (أليم) a naʿt; and the clause (فيها عذاب أليم) is a naʿt of (ريح). It was also said that it is part of the speech of Allah the Exalted, but the first is more fitting and more grounded in eloquence. (تُدَمِّرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ بِأَمْرِ رَبِّها) The clause is a second naʿt of (ريح); (تدمر) is an imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "it"; (كل شيء) is a direct object; (بأمر) are attached to (تدمر) [Translator's note: printed «بندمر», an evident misprint]; and (ربها) is muḍāf ilayhi. (فَأَصْبَحُوا لا يُرى إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. Hūd said that, then the wind overtook them, and they became such that nothing was seen but their dwellings. If the saying is from Allah the Exalted, the fāʾ is merely a conjunction. (كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْقَوْمَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) (كذلك) is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); (نجزي) is an imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "We"; (القوم) is a direct object, and (المجرمين) a naʿt of (القوم). (وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِيما إِنْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ) The wāw is the wāw of oath, and the lām is [the lām of] the reply to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (مكناهم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (فيما) are attached to (مكناهم); (ما) is a relative noun in the sense of "that which", or a described [indefinite] noun. On (إن) there are three views. The first: it is conditional, with its apodosis omitted, and the conditional clause is the ṣila of (ما), the implied form being "in that in which, if We had established you in it, you would have transgressed". The second: it is redundant (zāʾida), by likening the relative mā to the negating mā and the temporal mā. The third, and it is the most probable: it is negating, in the sense of mā, i.e. We established them in that in which We have not established you — of strength, expansion and abundance of provision; and the negating mā was avoided in favour of in to escape bringing together two words identical in sound. A fuller exposition of this discussion will come in the section on Benefits. (مكناكم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object, and (فيه) are attached to (مكناكم). (وَجَعَلْنا لَهُمْ سَمْعاً وَأَبْصاراً وَأَفْئِدَةً فَما أَغْنى عَنْهُمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَلا أَبْصارُهُمْ وَلا أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ) (جعلنا) is a verb and its agent; (لهم) are attached to (جعلنا), because it means "We created"; (سمعا) is a direct object, and (أبصارا) and (أفئدة) are conjoined to (سمعا). The fāʾ is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (أغنى) is a past verb; (عنهم) are attached to (أغنى); (سمعهم) is the agent, and (ولا أبصارهم ولا أفئدتهم) are conjoined to (سمعهم); (من) is a redundant preposition, and (شيء) is genitive in form and accusative in position as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. any of availing. (إِذْ كانُوا يَجْحَدُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) (إذ) is an adverb of past time conveying cause, attached to the meaning of the negation, because what is given a cause is the negation, i.e. the benefit of these senses was denied them because they used to reject. The author of al-Kashshāf pointed to this, saying: «If you say: by what is (إذ كانوا يجحدون) made accusative? I say: by His words, Exalted is He, (فما أغنى). If you say: why does it function as a statement of cause? I say: because what a statement of cause and an adverb convey is the same in your saying "I struck him for his wrongdoing" and "I struck him when he did wrong", since if you struck him at the time of his wrongdoing, you struck him only because of the existence of his wrongdoing in it; except that "idh" and "ḥaythu" have prevailed in this over the other adverbs» — to the point that it has almost become attached to their conventional meanings. The clause (كانوا) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يجحدون) is its khabar; (بآيات الله) are attached to (يجحدون). (وحاق بهم): the wāw is a conjunction; (حاق) is a past verb, indeclinable on fatḥa; (بهم) are attached to (حاق); (ما) is the agent of (حاق); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يستهزئون) is the khabar; and (به) are attached to (يستهزئون).

* Rhetoric:
In His words, Exalted is He, «ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار» to the end of the verse, there is the device of inversion (fann al-qalb), which has been discussed before, according to the view of some, and that the original is "the Fire will be presented to them". On this view, it is said to them before entering it, i.e. on beholding it. Among those who held this view are al-Zamakhsharī and al-Jalāl. The text of al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «Their being exposed to the Fire is their being punished by it, from their saying "the Banū so-and-so were exposed to the sword" when they were killed by it; and from it are His words, Exalted is He: (النار يعرضون عليها). It may also be meant that the Fire is presented to them, from their saying "the she-camel was presented to the watering-trough", meaning the presenting of the trough to her, so they inverted it. The explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, indicates this: they will be brought to it and it will be uncovered for them.» It was said in rebuttal of al-Zamakhsharī that there is nothing compelling inversion [in the camel example] except that [the trough] is inanimate, without perception, while the she-camel is the perceiving one, so she is the one to whom the trough is presented; as for the Fire, texts have come stating that it will then be perceptive with the perception of animals, indeed the perception of those endowed with knowledge, so the matter in the verse is on its apparent meaning. The wording of Zāda in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī: «ʿArḍ is made transitive with lām and with ʿalā; one says "I presented to him (ʿaraḍtu lahu) such-and-such a matter" and "I presented the thing to him (ʿalayhi)", i.e. I showed it to him. He, Exalted is He, said: (وعرضنا جهنم للكافرين عرضا). Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. We brought it out so that the disbelievers looked at it. So the one to whom something is presented must be one possessed of awareness, and the Fire is not one of them; so the presenting must be taken as punishing figuratively, by way of expressing a thing by the name of what leads to it, as one says "the Banū so-and-so were exposed to the sword and were killed by it"; or it remains on its original meaning, and the speech is taken as inversion, the original being "and the day the Fire will be presented to those who disbelieved", i.e. shown and brought out before them. The subtle point in regarding it as inversion is hyperbole, by claiming that the Fire has discernment, domination and mastery.»
As for Shaykh Abū Ḥayyān, he rejected the inversion and said, in the course of rebutting al-Zamakhsharī: «The Qur'an should not be taken as inversion, since the correct view on inversion is that it is among the things to which one is forced in poetry. If the meaning is sound and clear without inversion, what necessity calls for it? Neither their saying "I presented the she-camel to the trough" nor the explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās contains anything indicating inversion, because presenting the she-camel to the trough and presenting the trough to the she-camel are each sound, since presenting is a relative matter that may be attributed to either the she-camel or the trough.»

* Benefits:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «(إن) is negating, i.e. in that in which We have [not] established you [Translator's note: the printed quotation reads «فيما مكنّاكم فيه», without the negating مَا that the sense requires], except that in is better in sound because of the repugnant repetition involved in mā's being joined with its like, and the like of that is avoided. Do you not see that the origin of mahmā is mā mā, and because of the repugnance of the repetition they changed the alif to hāʾ? Abū al-Ṭayyib was clumsy in his saying:
لعمرك ما ما بان منك لضارب ... بأقتل مما بان منك لغائب
(By your life, what showed from you to one who strikes is not more deadly than what showed from you to one absent.)
What would it have harmed him to imitate the sweetness of the wording of the Revelation and say "laʿamruka mā in bāna minka li-ḍāribin"? And in has been made a connective [redundant particle] just like it in what al-Akhfash recited:
يرجى المرء ما إن لا يراه ... وتعرض دون أذناه الخطوب
(A man hopes for what he will not see, while misfortunes block the way before [even] the nearest of it.)»
This is what al-Zamakhsharī said. The reading in his Dīwān is:
يرى أن ما ما بان منك لضارب ... بأقتل مما بان منك لعائب
(He sees that what showed from you to one who strikes is not more deadly than what showed from you to one who reproaches.)
Ibn Jinnī said: «The first mā is redundant, and the second is in the sense of "that which", and the noun of anna is implied in it.» Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ said: «Al-Mutanabbī said: the first mā is in the sense of laysa, and the second in the sense of "that which".» The meaning he intends is that what showed from you to one who strikes is not more deadly than what showed to a reproacher who finds fault with you; he means that reproach is harsher than killing. This is taken from the saying of Ḥabīb ibn Aws, Abū Tammām al-Ṭāʾī:
فمتى لا يرى أن الفريصة مقتل ... ولكن يرى أن العيوب مقاتل
(A young man who does not see the shoulder-flesh as a mortal spot, but sees that faults are the mortal spots.) [Translator's note: the first word is printed «فمتى»; the gloss follows the evident reading «فتى».]

dervis-irab:27-32.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنا ما حَوْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْقُرى وَصَرَّفْنَا الْآياتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ) Resumptive speech, introduced to address the people of Mecca by way of illustration. The lām is the reply to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (أهلكنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حولكم) is an adverb attached to an omitted element that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (من القرى) are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (صرفنا) is conjoined to (أهلكنا), and (الآيات) is a direct object; (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (يرجعون) is its khabar (predicate). (فَلَوْلا نَصَرَهُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قُرْباناً آلِهَةً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), equivalent to hallā; (نصرهم) is a past verb and a fronted direct object; (الذين) is a postponed agent; the clause (اتخذوا) is the ṣila; (من دون الله) are attached to (اتخذوا). The first object of (اتخذوا) is omitted, and it is the referent pronoun of the relative noun; (قربانا) is accusative as a ḥāl, and (آلهة) is a second object. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Ḥūfī held that the first object is likewise omitted, as established above, with (قربانا) as the second object and (آلهة) a badal (substitute) of it. Al-Zamakhsharī condemned this view and said that the meaning is corrupted by it, but he did not explain how the meaning is corrupted; we shall explain it, and say: if (قربانا) were the second object, with the meaning "a means of drawing near", the meaning would come to be that they were rebuked for failing to take Allah as a means of drawing near; because when a master rebukes his slave and says "you have taken a master other than me", it means only blame for attributing mastership to someone other than him. That is not the intent here, for Allah the Exalted is the One to whom one draws near, not the One by whom one draws near to another. The rebuke fell only on attributing divinity to other than Allah the Exalted, so the speech properly requires that (آلهة) be the second object and nothing else. Abū Ḥayyān and Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted parsing (قربانا) as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with (آلهة) as the second object and the first object omitted, as above. (بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ وَذلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ وَما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ) (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction, for moving from the denial of help to something more specific than it, since the denial of help would hold true with their [gods] being present with them without helping; so by the digression He conveyed that they were not present at all, let alone helping them. (ضلوا) is a verb and its agent; (عنهم) are attached to (ضلوا). The wāw is a conjunction; (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (إفكهم) a khabar. (وما): the wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is maṣdariyya or a relative noun, the meaning being "and their fabrication" or "and what they fabricate"; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يفترون) is the khabar of (كان). (وَإِذْ صَرَفْنا إِلَيْكَ نَفَراً مِنَ الْجِنِّ يَسْتَمِعُونَ الْقُرْآنَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذ) is an adverb governed by an omitted (اذكر); the clause (صرفنا) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (صرفنا) is a verb and its agent; (إليك) are attached to (صرفنا); (نفرا) is a direct object; (من الجن) is an adjective of (نفر); and the clause (يستمعون القرآن) is a second adjective of (نفرا), or a ḥāl, because it has been specified by the adjective. (فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قالُوا: أَنْصِتُوا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (لما) is temporal ("when") or linking; (حضروه) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the clause (أنصتوا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and the pronoun in (حضروه) refers to the Qur'an. (فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ وَلَّوْا إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ) Conjoined to what preceded; (قضي) is a passive past verb; the clause (ولّوا) has no grammatical position; (إلى قومهم) are attached to (ولّوا); and (منذرين) is a ḥāl. (قالُوا يا قَوْمَنا إِنَّا سَمِعْنا كِتاباً أُنْزِلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسى مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ) (قالوا) is a verb and its agent; (إن) and its noun, and the clause (سمعنا) is its khabar; (كتابا) is a direct object; the clause (أنزل) is an adjective of (كتابا), and it is passive, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; (من بعد) are attached to (أنزل), and (موسى) is muḍāf ilayhi; (مصدقا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (كتابا); (لما) are attached to (مصدقا); (بين) is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (يديه) is muḍāf ilayhi. (يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ وَإِلى طَرِيقٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ)
The clause (يهدي) is a second naʿt of (كتابا), or a ḥāl of it because it has been described — the rule has been given before. (إلى الحق) are attached to (يهدي), and (إلى صراط مستقيم) is conjoined to (إلى الحق) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads (وإلى طريق مستقيم)]. (يا قَوْمَنا أَجِيبُوا داعِيَ اللَّهِ وَآمِنُوا بِهِ يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُجِرْكُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ) (يا) is a vocative particle, and (قومنا) is an annexed munādā (one addressed); (أجيبوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (داعي الله) is a direct object; (آمنوا) is conjoined to (أجيبوا), and (به) are attached to (آمنوا). (يغفر) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the reply to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); (لكم) are attached to (يغفر), and (من ذنوبكم) are also attached to (يغفر), i.e. some of them, so (من) is partitive — the secret of the partitive will come in the section on Rhetoric. (ويجركم من عذاب أليم) is conjoined to what preceded. (وَمَنْ لا يُجِبْ داعِيَ اللَّهِ فَلَيْسَ بِمُعْجِزٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (من) is conditional, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ;
(لا) is negating; (يجب) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, and (داعي الله) is its object. The fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition, because the apodosis is a non-inflecting (jāmid) verb. (ليس) is a defective past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) particle, and (معجز) is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the khabar of (ليس), whose noun is latent, referring to (من); (في الأرض) are attached to (معجز). (وَلَيْسَ لَهُ مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءُ أُولئِكَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; (ليس) is a defective past verb; (له) is the fronted khabar of (ليس); (من دونه) is a ḥāl; (أولياء) is the postponed noun of (ليس). (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (في ضلال) is the khabar of (أولئك), and (مبين) is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم» there is the device of pointed allusion (fann al-tankīt): He expressed it with the partitive (من) to indicate that forgiveness falls on private sins; as for the rights of [Allah's] servants, they cannot be forgiven except after their owners are satisfied, for Allah the Exalted does not forgive, through faith, the sins of wrongs done to others.

dervis-irab:33-35.t:
* I'rab:
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى) The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the wāw is conjoined to an implied clause; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past meaning] and jussive; (يروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (أن) and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of (يروا). (أن) and its noun; (الذي) is an adjective of (الله), and the clause (خلق السموات والأرض) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذي). The wāw is a conjunction; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; (يعي) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم); (بخلقهنّ) are attached to (يعي). The bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (قادر) is genitive in form and nominative in position because it is the khabar (predicate) of (أن); the redundant bāʾ entered only because the negation at the beginning of the verse includes أن and what is in its domain. More of this discussion will come in the section on Benefits. (على أن يحيي الموتى) is attached to (قادر). (بَلى إِنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (بلى) is a particle of answer for cancelling a negation: it cancels the negation and affirms its opposite; the discussion of the difference between it and naʿam has been given before. (إن) and its noun, and (قدير) is its khabar; (على كل شيء) are attached to (قدير). (وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ أَلَيْسَ هذا بِالْحَقِّ) The wāw is resumptive; (يوم) is an adverb attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "it will be said to them", and the clause is resumptive. The clause (يعرض) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (يعرض) is a passive imperfect verb; (الذين) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; (على النار) are attached to (يعرض). The clause (أليس هذا بالحق) is the object of the saying that makes the adverb accusative. The hamza is of disapproving, rebuking interrogation; (ليس) is a defective past verb; (هذا) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and (الحق) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ليس). (قالُوا بَلى وَرَبِّنا قالَ فَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ) (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (بلى) is a particle of answer; the wāw is of oath; (ربنا) is genitive by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an implied verb, its implied form being "I swear". (قال) is a past verb; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); (ذوقوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; (العذاب) is an object; (بما) are attached to (ذوقوا); the bāʾ is causal and (ما) is maṣdariyya, i.e. because of your disbelief; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (تكفرون) is its khabar. (فَاصْبِرْ كَما صَبَرَ أُولُوا الْعَزْمِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if the end of the disbelievers is as mentioned, then be patient with their harm. (اصبر) is an imperative verb, indeclinable on sukūn, its agent latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (كما صبر) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a ḥāl (circumstantial); (أولو العزم) is the agent of (صبر), and (من الرسل) is a ḥāl. (وَلا تَسْتَعْجِلْ لَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ما يُوعَدُونَ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا ساعَةً مِنْ نَهارٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تستعجل) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا), its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (لهم) are attached to (تستعجل); and the object of (تستعجل) is omitted, its implied form being "the descent of the punishment". (كأن) and its noun; (يوم) is an adverb attached to the negation conveyed by (لم); the clause (يرون) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (يرون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (يوعدون) is the ṣila. The clause (لم يلبثوا) is the khabar of (كأن); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ساعة) is an adverb attached to (يلبثوا); and (من نهار) is an adjective of (ساعة). (بَلاغٌ فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْفاسِقُونَ) (بلاغ) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this with which you have been admonished is a proclamation"; and it was said its implied form is "this Qur'an". The fāʾ is made a conjunction [Translator's note: the source reads «فجعل الفاء عاطفة», apparently for «والفاء عاطفة», "the fāʾ is a conjunction"]; (هل) is an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation; (يهلك) is a passive imperfect verb; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (القوم) is the deputy agent, and (الفاسقون) an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His words, Exalted is He, «ولم يعي بخلقهن» there is a synecdochic trope (majāz mursal) whose relation is causality, because ʿayy, i.e. fatigue, is impossible for Him, Exalted is He; and it is a cause of ceasing work, or of deficiency in it and delay in completing it — that is the relation in this trope.

* Benefits:
Al-Zajjāj said: «If you said "I did not think that Zayd was standing (bi-qāʾimin)", it would be permissible; it is as though it were said "Is not Allah able (bi-qādirin)?" Do you not see that (بلى) occurs affirming the power over everything — the resurrection and other things — not their seeing?» Abū Ḥayyān said in comment on it: «The correct view is to restrict that to what is heard [from the Arabs] (al-samāʿ).»
Ibn Hishām said: a thing may be given the ruling of what resembles it in meaning, in wording, or in both. As for the first, it has many forms, one of which is the entry of the bāʾ into the khabar of anna in His words, Exalted is He: (أو لم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السموات والأرض ولم يعي بخلقهنّ بقادر), because it is in the sense of "Is not Allah able?"; and what made that implied structure easy is the distance between the two [i.e. anna and its khabar]. For that reason it did not enter in: (أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السموات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم). Similar is the insertion of the bāʾ in (كفى بالله شهيدا), because of the meaning "be content with Allah as witness" that has entered it, unlike his saying:
قليل منك يكفيني
(A little from you suffices me.)
And in his saying:
سود المحاجر لا يقرأن بالسور
(Black around the eyes, they do not recite the surahs.)
because of the meaning "they do not draw near [to Allah] by reciting the surahs" that has entered it. For this reason al-Suhaylī said: you may not say "your letter reached me, so I read with it (qaraʾtu bihi)" on the pattern of his saying "lā yaqraʾna bi-l-suwar", because it is devoid of the meaning of drawing near.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ مَّا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, then He said: ﴿أَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقُواْ﴾ and did not say خلقت or خلقن, because He meant only the idols, so He made their action like the action of people and their like; for the idols are spoken to, worshipped, frequented and exalted as princes and their like are exalted, so He treated them like people.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is: مَن تعبدون من دون الله, making it (مَن); and this is an explicit statement of resemblance to people, in the verb and in the noun. And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: أريتكم; and generally what is in his reading of the saying of Allah أريت and أريتم is, in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, with kāf, so that in his reading there is even: "أرَيْتك الذى يُكذِّب بالدين".
His saying: ﴿أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ﴾.
The generality read it: "أثارة"; and some of them read it, he said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read, as far as I know, "أثْرةً", light [without a vowel on the thāʾ]. And it is reported of some readers: "أثَرة". The meaning in all of them is: a remnant of knowledge, or something handed down (maʾthūr) from the books of the ancients.
Whoever reads "أثارة", it is like the maṣdar (verbal noun), as in your saying: al-samāḥa, al-shajāʿa.
Whoever reads "أَثَرة" built it on al-athar, as one says: qatara.
And whoever reads "أَثْرة", it is as though he meant something like His saying: ﴿إلا من خطِف الخطفة﴾, and al-rajfa.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّن يَدْعُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَن لاَّ يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ﴾.
By (من) He meant the idols; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "مالا يستجيب له"; and this is of what I mentioned to you concerning من and ما.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعاً مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ﴾.
He says: I was not the first to be sent; many prophets were sent before me.
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ﴾.
It was revealed concerning the Companions of the Prophet, Allah bless him. That was because they complained to him of what they were meeting from the people of Mecca before he was commanded to fight them. The Prophet, Allah bless him, said: "I have seen in my sleep that I emigrate to a land of palms, trees and water." They rejoiced at that; then they remained for a while without seeing it, and said to the Prophet, Allah bless him: "We do not see the fulfilment of what you said, while the harm has become severe on us." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعاً مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ﴾: will I go out to the place I was shown in my sleep or not? Then he said to them: "It is only something I was shown in my sleep, and I follow only what is revealed to me." He says: what I told you was not revealed to me; and had it been revelation, he, Allah bless him, would not have said: ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ﴾.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّن بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَىٰ مِثْلِهِ.﴾.
A man of the Jews bore witness to the like of what ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām bore witness to, of confirming the Prophet, Allah bless him, and that he is described in the Torah; so that man believed while you were arrogant.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لَوْ كَانَ خَيْراً مَّا سَبَقُونَآ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
When Muzayna, Juhayna, Aslam and Ghifār embraced Islam, the Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa, Ghaṭafān, Ashjaʿ and Asad said: "Had this been good, the herders of lambs would not have beaten us to it." This is the interpretation of His saying: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ خَيْراً مَّا سَبَقُونَآ إِلَيْهِ﴾.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهَـٰذَا كِتَابٌ مُّصَدِّقٌ لِّسَاناً عَرَبِيّاً﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: مصدق لما بين يديه لسانا عربيا. Its accusative in our reading is according to the interpretation of ʿAbd Allāh's reading, i.e. this Qurʾān confirms the Torah, [being] clear Arabic. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it may be [accusative] from مصدق, as I explained to you, and it may be a qaṭʿ (detached ḥāl) from the hāʾ in بين يديه.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لِّيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
البشرى may be nominative or accusative. The nominative is on: "and this is a Book confirming, and good tidings"; and the accusative is on: "that you may warn those who did wrong and give good tidings (وتبشر)"; so when you drop تبشر and put in its place بشرى or بشارة, you use the accusative. Like it in speech: "I seek refuge with Allah from you", and "Watering (سقيا) to so-and-so", as though he said: "and may Allah water so-and-so"; and "I came to honour you, and as a visit (زيارة) to you and fulfilment (قضاء) of your right", whose meaning is: to visit you and fulfil your right; so you put الزيارة and القضاء in the accusative by an implied verb.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ إِحْسَاناً﴾.
The people of Kūfa read it with the alif, and so it is in their codices; and the people of Medina and the people of Baṣra read: (حُسناً), and so it is in their codices; and their meaning is one, and Allah knows best.
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: حتّى إذا استوى وبلغ أشده وبلغ أربعين سنة; and the meaning in it is like the meaning in our reading, because it is allowed in Arabic to say: "When a child was born to you and you reached the age of men, you sacrificed [the ʿaqīqa] and did such-and-such", while the reaching comes before the birth. And it is said that al-ashudd here is forty.
I heard one of the shaykhs mention, with an isnad of his, concerning al-ashudd: thirty-three, and concerning al-istiwāʾ: forty.
And I heard that al-ashudd in other than this place is eighteen. The first is more likely to be correct, because forty is closer in sequence to thirty-three than to eighteen. Do you not see that you say: "I took most of the wealth, or all of it", which is better than saying: "I took the least of the wealth, or all of it"? Like it is His saying: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلمُ أَنّكَ تقُومُ أَدْنَى مِنْ ثُلُثَىِ الّليْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ﴾: some of these are close to others. This is the way of the speech of the Arabs [176/a]. And the second, meaning eighteen, [and] had it been joined to forty, would have been a valid view.
His saying: ﴿أَوْزِعْنِيۤ أَنْ أَشكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ﴾.
This verse was revealed concerning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah have mercy on him.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAnazī narrated it to me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: it was revealed concerning Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, up to His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِين نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ﴾ to the end of the verse.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read, and it is reported of some of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿نتقبَّلُ عنهم أحْسَنَ ما عَمِلوا ونتجاوز عن سيئاتهم﴾, with nūn. The reading of the generality is: "يُتقبل عنهم أحسن ما عملوا ويُتجاوز عن سيئاتهم", with yāʾ with ḍamma; and had it been read "تُتَقبَّل عنهم [أحسن ما عملوا] وتُتجاوز", it would have been correct.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿وَعْدَ ٱلصِّدْقِ ٱلَّذِي﴾: like your saying "a true promise (وعدا صدقا)", annexed to itself. Whatever maṣdar is in the meaning of "truly (ḥaqqan)" is accusative, whether definite or indefinite, like His saying in Yūnus: ﴿وَعد الله حقّاً﴾.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي قَالَ لِوَالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَّكُمَآ﴾. It is reported that it was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr who said this before he embraced Islam: (أُفٍّ لكما), "Filth to you both! Do you promise me that I shall be brought out of the grave?" The readers agreed on (أخرج) with ḍamma on the alif, its agent not named; and had it been read أن أَخْرُجَ, with fatḥa on the alif, it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿وَهُمَا يَسْتَغثِيَانِ ٱللَّهَ﴾ and they say: "ويلك آمن". The verb of saying is implied; He means Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, and his wife.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ﴾.
It was not revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr; rather, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: "Raise up [for me] Judʿān ibn ʿAmr and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAmr" (and they were among his forefathers) "so that I may ask them about what Muḥammad, Allah bless him and grant him peace, says: is it true or false?" So Allah sent down: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ﴾, meaning Judʿān and ʿUthmān.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّبَاتِكُمْ﴾: al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim and Nāfiʿ of Medina read it without a question, and al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar of Medina read it with the question: "أأذهبتم". The Arabs use the question for rebuke, and also do not use the question, so they say: "You went and did such-and-such", and they say: "Did you go and do such-and-such?" And all is correct.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ أَنذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِٱلأَحْقَافِ﴾.
The aḥqāf of sand; its singular is ḥiqf, and the ḥiqf is the elongated sand-dune rising upward.
His saying: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتِ ٱلنُّذُرُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ﴾.
Before him, "and from behind him": after him; and it is [176/b] in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "من بين يديه ومن بعده".

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضاً مُّسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ﴾.
They hoped it would be rain-cloud, and said: "This is what you promised us; this, by Allah, is the rain and the good." Allah said: Say to them: rather, it is the punishment you sought to hasten. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: قل [بل] ما استعجلتم به هى ريح فيها عذاب أليم. And هو and هى in this place are in the position of His saying: "مِنْ مَنِىٍّ تُمْنَى" and "يمنى".
Whoever says "هو" refers to the punishment, and whoever says "هى" refers to the wind.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأْصْبَحُواْ لاَ يُرَىٰ إِلاَّ مَسَاكِنُهُمْ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it: "لا يُرَى إلا مساكنهم".
Al-Farrāʾ said: and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, read it.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Khurāsānī narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he said: "لا تَرَى إلا مساكِنَهم".
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: and al-Kisāʾī narrated to me, from Qiṭr ibn Khalīfa, from Mujāhid, that he read: "فأصبحوا لا تَرى إلا مساكنهم". He said: and al-Ḥasan read: "فأصبحوا لا تُرى إلا مساكنُهم", and there is ugliness in it in Arabic, because the Arabs, when they put the verb of a feminine before إلا, make it masculine, saying: "None stood (لم يقم) but your slave-girl" and "None stood (ما قام) but your slave-girl", and they hardly say: "ما قامت إلا جاريتك". That is because what is left out is أحد (anyone), and أحد, whether it is for a feminine or a masculine, has a masculine verb. Do you not see that you say: "If anyone (أحد) of them (fem.) stands, strike him", and you do not say "if she stands" except under compulsion; and it is nevertheless allowed on that basis. He said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
وَنارنُا لم تُر ناراً مِثْلُها * قد عِلِمت ذكـَ ا معدّ أكْرما
(And our fire: no fire like it has been seen; Maʿadd has known [ours] to be the most generous.)
So he made the verb of (مثل) feminine because it is for the fire; and the best speech is to say: ما رُئى إلا مثلها.
«[Translator's note: the second hemistich is partly corrupt in the source («ذكـَ ا»); the gloss is tentative.]»

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَاهُمْ فِيمَآ إِن مَّكَّنَّاكُمْ﴾.
He says: in that in which We have not established you; and (إن) is in the position of ما in negation (jaḥd).
His saying: ﴿وَحَاقَ بِهِم﴾.
In the speech of the Arabs it is: it came back upon them; and it came in the exegesis: it encompassed them and descended on them.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَذَلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ﴾.
It is also read أَفَكُهُم and أَفَكَهُم. As for al-ifk and al-afak, they are in the position of your saying: al-ḥidhr and al-ḥadhar, al-nijs and al-najas. And as for whoever says أَفكَهُم, he puts the hāʾ and mīm in the position of the accusative, saying: that turned them away from faith, and their lie; as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يُؤفَكُ عنه مَن أُفِكَ﴾, i.e. he is turned away from it who is turned away.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقَادِرٍ﴾.
The bāʾ entered because of لم. The Arabs bring it in with negation (al-juḥūd) when it puts what precedes it in the nominative, and they bring it in when a verb that needs two nouns falls upon it, as in your saying: "I do not think you are standing (بقائم)", and "I do not think that you are standing" [177/a], and "You were not standing". When you leave out the bāʾ, you put what it was in into the accusative by the verb that governs it; and had you dropped the bāʾ from قادر in this place, it would be nominative, because it is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ. He said: and one of them recited to me:
فما رَجعت بخائبةٍ رِكابٌ * حكيمُ بنُ المسيِّب مُنتهاها
(No riding camels whose destination was Ḥakīm ibn al-Musayyab ever came back disappointed.)
So he brought the bāʾ into a verb [i.e. a predicate] which, had it been dropped from it, would be accusative by the verb, not by the bāʾ. Analogize on this and what resembles it.
It is reported of some readers that he read (يَقدِر) in place of (بقادر), as Ḥamza read: "وَمَا أنتَ تهدى العمى", while the reading of the generality is: "بهادى العمى".

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلَيْسَ هَـٰذَا بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
In it there is an implied verb of saying: "it is said: is this not the truth?". بلاغٌ: i.e. "this is a proclamation", nominative by resumption (istiʾnāf).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «تنزيل».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «ما خلقنا» is resumptive; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «خلقنا»; «وأجل» is a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «الحق». «ما» in «عَمَّا» is maṣdariyya, and the genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to «معرضون».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: His words «أرأيتم» mean "tell me", and it takes two objects: the first is the relative «ما», and the second is the clause «ماذا خلقوا». The preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما». His words «ماذا»: «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» is a relative noun, khabar (predicate). The preposition «من الأرض» is attached to «خلقوا». The clause «أروني» is parenthetical, reinforcing «أرأيتم». «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, and the clause after it is resumptive within the scope of the saying. The preposition «في السماوات» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «شرك». The clause «ائتوني» is resumptive within the scope of the saying. The preposition «من قبل» is attached to a naʿt of «كتاب», and the preposition «من علم» is attached to a naʿt of «أثارة». The clause «إن كنتم صادقين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «ومن أضل» is resumptive; «من»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) [Translator's note: i.e. «من» is the mubtadaʾ and «أضل» its khabar]. The preposition «ممن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أضل»; the preposition «من دون» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَنْ»; «مَنْ» is a relative noun, the object of «يدعو». The clause «وهم غافلون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «لا يستجيب», and the preposition «عن دعائهم» is attached to «غافلون».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The conditional clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause «مَنْ أضل»; the preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أعداء»; and the preposition «بعبادتهم» is attached to «كافرين».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «بينات» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آياتنا». The clause «لما جاءهم» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb) of «لما» is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The clause «هذا سحر» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one. The clause «فلا تملكون» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "you do not possess", and the clause (فأنتم لا تملكون) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شيئاً». The clause «هو أعلم» is resumptive; the clause «كفى به شهيداً» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), the hāʾ is the fāʿil (agent), and «شهيداً» is a tamyīz (specification). The adverb «بيني» is attached to «شهيداً», and the clause «وهو الغفور الرحيم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «كفى به».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The preposition «من الرسل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «بدعاً». The clause «ما أدري» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying). His words «ما يفعل بي»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause suspends «أدري» from governing, so it stands in place of its two objects. «إن» is negative; the clause «إن أتبع» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and the clause «وما أنا إلا نذير» is conjoined to the clause «أتبع».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The two objects of «أرأيتم» are omitted, i.e. "Have you considered your state: if it were so, would you not be wrongdoers?" The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then you have done wrong". The clause «وشهد شاهد» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «كفرتم»; the preposition «من بني» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «شاهد»; the preposition «على مثله» is attached to «شهد»; and the clause «فآمن» is conjoined to the clause «شهد».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «وقال» is resumptive, and the conditional clause is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying); the noun (ism) of «كان» refers to the Qur'an. His words «وإذ»: the wāw is conjunctive; «إذ» is an adverb of past time attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied verb, i.e. "their obstinacy became evident when they were not guided", and the clause of the implied verb is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «قال». It is not attached to his words «فسيقولون», because the two times differ and because what follows the fāʾ does not govern what precedes it. The clause «فسيقولون» is conjoined to the clause of the implied verb.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «ومن قبله كتاب» is resumptive; «إماماً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كتاب موسى». The clause «وهذا كتاب» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause. «لساناً» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مصدق»; the ḥāl here is a non-derived noun, and its being qualified is what permits it. The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «لينذر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مصدق»; «بشرى» is a noun conjoined to «مصدق», and the preposition «للمحسنين» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «بشرى».

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «استقاموا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «قالوا»; the clause «فلا خوف» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ»; the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and «لا» is negative and inoperative (muhmala).

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «خالدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «أصحاب»; «جزاء» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governing word is implied, i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense"; the preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) «جزاء».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «ووصينا» is resumptive; «إحساناً» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, the implied form being "that he do good to them with good". The clause «حملته أمه» is resumptive; «كرهاً» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "a carrying in hardship". The clause «وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «حملته أمه». «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), and the clause after it is resumptive; «أربعين» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «قال» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause «أوزعني» is the response to the vocative, resumptive. «أن» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the second object, and the second maṣdar is conjoined to the first. «صالحاً» is a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause «ترضاه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «صالحاً». The clause «إني تبت» is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «أولئك الذين»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The preposition «في أصحاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عنهم». «وعد» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and the clause (نَعِدهم وَعْدَ) is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «نتقبَّل». «الصدق» is muḍāf ilayhi.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «والذي قال......» is resumptive. «أف»: a verbal noun of imperfect meaning (ism fiʿl muḍāriʿ), meaning "I am vexed". The preposition «لكما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied "I mean", i.e. "the saying of 'uff' is to you two". The clause «أتعدانني» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن أخرج» is the second object of «تَعِدانني». The clause «وقد خلت» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause «وهما يستغيثان» is a ḥāl from «والديه». His words «ويلك»: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of a disused (muhmal) verb, and the clause «ويلك آمن» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of an implied saying which is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) in «يستغيثان», i.e. "they say: woe to you, believe". The clause «آمن» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, as is the clause «إن وعد الله حق». The clause «فيقول» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the implied clause of saying; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr), and «أساطير» is the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «أولئك الذين» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذي» in the previous verse. The preposition «في أمم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليهم»; the clause «قد خَلَتْ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أمم»; the preposition «من الجن» is attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «خلت»; and the clause «إنهم كانوا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «ولكل درجات» is resumptive; the preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «درجات». The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليوفيهم» is attached to an implied verb, i.e. "He recompensed them with that", and the implied clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «لكل درجات». The clause «وهم لا يظلمون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: His words «ويوم»: the wāw is resumptive; «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied verb, i.e. "it will be said to them on the day". The clause «يعرض» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause «أذهبتم» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of an implied saying; the preposition «في حياتكم» is attached to «أذهبتم». His words «فاليوم»: the fāʾ is conjunctive and «اليوم» is an adverb attached to «تجزون»; the clause «تجزون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the implied clause "it will be said". «عذاب» is the second object; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to «تجزون». The preposition «بغير» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «تستكبرون», and the second interpreted maṣdar «بما كنتم» is conjoined to the first maṣdar.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «واذكر» is resumptive; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from «أخا». The preposition «بالأحقاف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قومه»; the clause «وقد خلت» is a ḥāl. «أن» is explicative (mufassira), and the clause after it is explicative; the clause «إني أخاف» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «فأتنا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «جئتنا»; the clause «إن كنت من الصادقين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «وأبلِّغكم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying); «ما» is a relative noun, the second object; «قومًا» is the second object, and the clause «تجهلون» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. «عارضًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «رأوه»; «مستقبل» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «عارضًا», and its annexation is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa), because it is an active participle; hence it may be a naʿt (adjective) of an indefinite noun. Likewise «مُمْطرنا» is a naʿt of «عارض». «ما» is a relative noun, khabar (predicate) of «هو»; «ريح» is a badal (substitute) from «هو», and the clause «فيها عذاب» is a naʿt of «ريح».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «تدمر» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {رِيحٌ}; the preposition «بأمر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تدمر». The clause «فأصبحوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «تدمر», and the clause «لا يرى» is the khabar (predicate) of the defective (nāqiṣa) «أصبحوا»; «مساكنهم» is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The kāf in «كذلك» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "We recompense with a recompense like that recompense", and the clause «نجزي» is parenthetical between the two conjoined clauses.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause of the oath and its response is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {فَأَصْبَحُوا}. «ما» is a relative in the position of the genitive; «إن» is negative, i.e. "We established them in that in which We did not establish you, of power"; the negative «ما» was avoided in favour of «إن» so that two identical words would not come together. The preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل», and the clause «فما أغنى» is conjoined to the clause «جعلنا». «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), emphasising the negation. «وشيء» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a little or a great sufficing", and «مِنْ» is redundant. «إذ» is an adverb of time attached to «أغنى». The clause «حاق» is conjoined to the clause «ما أغنى»; «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent); the preposition «به» is attached to «يستهزئون».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «ولقد أهلكنا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «لقد مكنَّاهم»; «حولكم» is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); «من القرى» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما»; and the clause «لعلهم يرجعون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «فلولا نصرهم» is resumptive; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). The preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آلهة». The first object of «اتخذوا» is omitted, i.e. "they took them"; «قربانًا» is a ḥāl, and «آلهة» is the second object of «اتخذ». The clause «ضلوا» is resumptive, as is the clause «وذلك إفكهم». His words «ما»: a relative noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «إفكهم».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The wāw is resumptive; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, the object of an implied "remember". The preposition «من الجن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نفراً», and the clause «يستمعون» is a second naʿt of «نفراً». The clause «فلما حضروه» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «صَرَفْنا»; the conditional clause «فلمَّا قضي» is resumptive; «منذرين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ولَّوْا».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «أنزل» is a naʿt (adjective); «مصدقاً» is a naʿt of «كتاباً»; the lām in «لما» is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening; «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the adverb «بين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); and the clause «يهدي» is a naʿt of «كتاباً».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «يا قومنا» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the clause «يغفر» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «ومن لا يجب» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «آمنوا», the response to the vocative. «من» is conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «فليس بمعجز» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate). The preposition «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «معجز»; the preposition «من دونه» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أولياء»; and the clause «أولئك في ضلال» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «أولم يروا» is resumptive, and «أنَّ» with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «يروا». The clause «ولم يعي» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «خلق», and the verb is jussive (majzūm) by dropping the weak letter. The bāʾ in «بقادر» is redundant (zāʾida); its addition is made acceptable by the statement being equivalent to (أليس الله بقادر؟). The preposition «على أن يحيي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قادر». «بلى» is a particle of response, and the clause after it is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The wāw is resumptive; «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "it will be said". The clause «أليس هذا بالحق» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of the implied saying, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ليس». The clause «بلى وَرَبِّنا» (هو الحق) is the maqūl al-qawl; the wāw in «وربِّنا» is of the oath, and the genitive noun is attached to an implied "I swear". The clause «فذوقوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. «إن أقررتم فذوقوا» (if you acknowledge it, then taste); «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to «فذوقوا».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «فاصبر» is resumptive; the kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "be patient with a patience like the patience of those of resolve". The preposition «من الرسل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أولو العزم». The clause «كأنهم يوم يرون ... » is resumptive; «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to «يلبثوا»; «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «ساعة» is an adverb attached to «يلبثوا»; the preposition «من نهار» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «ساعة». «بلاغ» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a proclamation", and the clause is resumptive, as is the interrogative clause.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted, {وَمن أضلّ مِمَّن يَدْعُو}: من is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is interrogative, and what follows it is its khabar (predicate). The third من is in the accusative position, governed by يدعو; it is in the sense of الذي (relative noun), and what follows it is its ṣila (relative clause).

His saying {إِمَامًا وَرَحْمَة}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from الكتاب.

[Translator's note: إماما ورحمة is in āya 12, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {كفى بِهِ شَهِيدا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or as specification (bayān); به is the fāʿil (agent), and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying {لِسَانا عَرَبيا}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the latent nominative pronoun in مصدّق, or from الكتاب, because it has been given an adjective, مصدّق, and so approaches a definite noun, or from ذا; what governs the ḥāl is then the pointing or the drawing of attention (tanbīh). It has also been said that عربيا is the ḥāl and لسانا a preparatory element (tawṭiʾa) for the ḥāl.

His saying {وبشرى} is in the nominative position, conjoined to كتاب. It has also been said that it is in the accusative position as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:15-15.t:
His saying {بِوَالِديهِ حسنا}: its pattern is فُعْل, not فُعْلى, because فُعْلى is not fully declined, whether definite or indefinite; and moreover فُعْلى in a position like this is used only with the alif and lām.
