The interrogative, if one reads «أذهبتم» [Translator's note: i.e. the interrogative form], is for rebuke and making them acknowledge (taqrīr). He chose «أذهبتم» without the interrogative only because when the interrogative carries the meaning of taqrīr it becomes a negation if [the statement] is affirmative, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تُمْنُونَ أَأَنْتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ [al-Wāqiʿa: 58–59], and if it is a negation it becomes an affirmation, because the negation of a negation is an affirmation, as [the poet] said [metre: al-wāfir]:
422- ألستم خير من ركب المطايا ... وأندى العالمين بطون راح
(Are you not the best of those who have ridden mounts, and the most generous in the world in the palms of [your] hands?)
However, whoever reads «أذهبتم» [with the interrogative] does not, in his view, take its meaning in this way; rather its implied form is: "Did you exhaust your good things in your worldly life and [yet] seek salvation in the Hereafter?"
فَالْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الْهُونِ: the governor of اليوم is تجزون, intended as postponed [i.e. the adverb is fronted]. بِما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ, i.e. your arrogance and your transgression. When «ما» is a maṣdar-forming particle like this, it does not need a resumptive pronoun.

nahhas-irab:21-23.t:
وَاذْكُرْ أَخا عادٍ: عاد is fully declined (munṣarif) because it is the name of the tribe-as-people (al-ḥayy); if it were made a name of the tribe (al-qabīla) it would be a diptote, even though it has three letters. Likewise, if you named a woman Zayd it would be a diptote; and if you named her Hind, declining it fully would be permissible according to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ — except that the preferred choice according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is not to decline it fully, while according to al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ full declension is better. As for Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj], he used to say: if you named a woman Hind, full declension is not permissible at all; and this is the analogical rule, because it is feminine and definite.
As for the statement of some grammarians that if you name [someone] with a past verb it is a diptote, Sībawayh refuted it from what was heard from the Arabs contrary to what he said, and [showed] that it has a counterpart among nouns; likewise one says «كتبت أبا جاد» (I wrote Abū Jād) with full declension and nothing else.
إِذْ أَنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالْأَحْقافِ: Mujāhid said: al-Aḥqāf is a land. Ibn Abīn Nuʿaym said: al-Aḥqāf is the name of a land. [Translator's note: the name is so printed; it is probably a misprint, e.g. for Ibn Abī Najīḥ.] Wahb ibn Munabbih said: al-Aḥqāf in Yemen — the idols and the images, and they had overpowered people by their numbers and their strength. [Translator's note: this statement appears defective in the source; it is translated as written.] Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the singular of al-aḥqāf is ḥiqf, which is compacted sand, not very large, with a curve in it. He said: and one says احقوقف الشيء when the thing bends until its two ends almost meet, as [the poet] said [metre: al-rajaz]:
423- سماوة الهلال حتّى احقوقفا
(the outline of the crescent, until it curved.)
الأحقاف is fully declined, even though it is the name of a land, because it has alif and lām. Sībawayh said: Know that every diptote becomes fully declined when alif and lām enter it or it is made muḍāf (put in genitive construct).
وَقَدْ خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ: plural of nadhīr, which is the messenger; النذر may also be a noun of the maṣdar. Al-Farrāʾ said: مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ: before him, وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ: after him. أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ: «أن» is in the position of an accusative, i.e. «بأن» (that) [by removal of the preposition]. إِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ: [عظيم is] a naʿt (adjective) of اليوم; if it were a naʿt of عذاب it would be accusative. Genitive by proximity (al-jiwār) is not permissible in the Book of Allah the Exalted; it occurs only in error.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عارِضاً has two answers. The implied form may be "when they saw the clouds", even though the clouds were not mentioned before, because the pronoun is known and «عارضا» indicates it. The other answer is that it is a reply to their saying فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا, i.e. when they saw what they were promised as a cloud. مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ: tanwīn is implied in it [i.e. the construct is not one of definiteness, so it can qualify the indefinite عارضا], and likewise قالُوا هذا عارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنا, i.e. «ممطر لنا» (raining upon us), as [the poet] said [metre: al-basīṭ]:
424- يا ربّ غابطنا لو كان يطلبكم
(Many a one who envies us, if he were seeking you…)
i.e. «غابط لنا».
بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ: al-Farrāʾ said: In the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: «قل بل ما استعجلتم به هي ريح فيها عذاب أليم». He said: هي and هو are like مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنى [al-Qiyāma: 37] and «تُمنى» [Translator's note: the source prints «ويمنى» again; the variant reading is «تُمنى» with tāʾ]. Whoever says هو refers it to the punishment, and whoever says هي refers it to the wind.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: «فأصبحوا لا تَرى إلّا مساكنَهم»: this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, and it is the known reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and of Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read فَأَصْبَحُوا لا يُرى إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ, and it is the known reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Mujāhid. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «فأصبحوا لا تُرى إلّا مساكنُهم» with tāʾ and with المساكن in the nominative as the noun of the passive verb [nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. [Translator's note: the source prints the first and third readings unvocalized; the vocalization given follows the descriptions.] This reading is far-fetched according to al-Farrāʾ, because when a verb of a feminine noun comes first and is followed by an affirmation [with إلّا], the Arabs make it masculine, as he claimed, and he reported: «لم يقم إلا هندٌ» (none stood except Hind), because the meaning according to him is "no one stood except Hind".

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِيما إِنْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: «ما» has the meaning of "that which" (alladhī), and «إن» has the meaning of «ما» [i.e. negative], i.e. "We had established them in that in which We have not established you". وَجَعَلْنا لَهُمْ سَمْعاً وَأَبْصاراً وَأَفْئِدَةً: hearing came in the singular and what follows it in the plural, and there is more than one answer for this. Among them: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and so was not pluralized for that reason; among them: that there is something omitted in it, i.e. "and We gave them possessors of hearing"; and among them: that it is a singular indicating a plural. فَما أَغْنى عَنْهُمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَلا أَبْصارُهُمْ وَلا أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ: «ما» may be a naʿt, having no position in i'rab [Translator's note: «نعتا» here is almost certainly a misprint for «نفيا», "a negation", which fits "having no position in i'rab" and the contrast with the interrogative]; if you make it interrogative, its position is accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ, i.e. returned [upon them]; he said: and the people of exegesis say: encompassed and befell.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنا ما حَوْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْقُرى: this is the lām of emphasis. «قد» according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh has the meaning of expectation with the past; when it is with the imperfect it conveys the meaning of infrequency; you say «قد يقوم», i.e. that is infrequent from him.
فَلَوْلا نَصَرَهُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قُرْباناً آلِهَةً بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ وَذلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ وَما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ (28) فَلَوْلا نَصَرَهُمُ: لولا and هلّا (why not) are the same, as [the poet] said [metre: al-ṭawīl]:
425- بني ضوطرى لولا الكميّ المقنّعا
(O sons of Ḍawṭarā, why not [count] the armoured, helmeted warrior?)

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
i.e. هلّا (why not). قُرْباناً آلِهَةً: «قربانا» may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and may be a mafʿūl (object), with «آلهة» a badal (substitute) for it. بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ: if you wish, you may assimilate the lām into the ḍād. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh claimed that the ḍād comes out from the right side [of the tongue], and with some people from the left side.
وَذلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ: «ذلك» is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), «إفكهم» is its khabar (predicate), and the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of a genitive by being muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct); and its like is the same in i'rab and meaning [Translator's note: the source is elliptical here; it presumably refers to the variant «أَفْكُهُم», which al-Farrāʾ's remark then explains]. Al-Farrāʾ said: ifk and afk are like ḥidhr and ḥadhar, i.e. both have one meaning.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read «أَفَكَهُم» as a past verb, the hāʾ and mīm on this reading being in the position of an accusative; there is doubt about its chain of transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās. However, it was read out to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq, from Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, from Ḥammād ibn Salama, who said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, saying: I heard Abū ʿIyāḍ reading وَذلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ [Translator's note: so printed, identical to the received text; given what follows, Abū ʿIyāḍ's reading was a past verb such as «أَفَكَهُم» or «أَفَّكَهُم»]. On this reading وَما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ is in the position of a nominative in one of two ways. Either it is conjoined to the pronoun latent in «أفكهم», the meaning being "and that ruined them and destroyed them — it and their fabrication" — except that conjoining to a nominative latent pronoun is far-fetched in Arabic unless it is emphasized or the speech is lengthened: if you said «قمتُ وعمروٌ» it would be ugly, until you say «قمتُ أنا وعمروٌ» or «قمتُ في الدار وعمروٌ». The second way is that «وما كانوا يفترون» is conjoined to ذلك, i.e. "that destroyed them and led them astray, and their fabrication too destroyed them and led them astray".
The clear reading, on which rests the authority of the community, is «وذلك إفكهم», i.e. "and that is their lie", and وما كانوا يفترون on this reading is conjoined to إفكهم, i.e. "and that is their lie and their fabrication". ما with the verb would be a maṣdar, and so does not need a resumptive pronoun, because it is a particle. If you make it mean "that which" (alladhī), a resumptive pronoun is inevitable, implied or overt, so the implied form would be "and that which they used to fabricate (yaftarūnahu)"; then the hāʾ is omitted, and its omission is good for several reasons: among them the length of the noun [i.e. the relative with its ṣila], that masculine is not confused with feminine, that it is the end of a verse, and that it is an attached pronoun. If it were detached, omission would be far-fetched — even though some have read تَماماً عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ [al-Anʿām: 154] [i.e. «أَحْسَنُ»] with the meaning "upon the one who is better", and some interpreted Sībawayh's statement «هذا باب علم ما الكلم» as meaning "which is الكلم", and some narrated «هذا باب علمِ ما الكلمُ» without tanwīn on the basis that هو has likewise been omitted; and there is in it the far-fetchedness we mentioned. When it is attached, omission is good, as it has been read «وفيها ما تشتهي الأنفس» [al-Zukhruf: 71] and «تشتهيه». Abū Isḥāq reported «وذلك أأفكهم», i.e. "the most lying of them" [Translator's note: i.e. «آفَكُهُم», an elative].

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: وَإِذْ صَرَفْنا إِلَيْكَ نَفَراً مِنَ الْجِنِّ: «إذ» is in the position of an accusative. It is said: the meaning of «صرفنا» is "We directed them (waffaqnāhum) to that", so it was called ṣarf (turning) figuratively. [Translator's note: the source reads «مضى صرفنا وقفناهم»; «مضى» is probably a misprint for «معنى», and «وقفناهم» may be for «وفّقناهم»; translated by the likely sense.] فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ, i.e. its recitation was finished, وَلَّوْا إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ, i.e. warning them against refusing to accept the truth; «منذرين» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: قالُوا يا قَوْمَنا إِنَّا سَمِعْنا كِتاباً: Sībawayh allowed, in some dialects, «أنّ» with fatḥa after a verb of saying. أُنْزِلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسى مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ: «يهدي» is in the position of an accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب; it may also be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is [itself] nominative because it is an imperfect verb.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: يا قَوْمَنا أَجِيبُوا داعِيَ اللَّهِ وَآمِنُوا بِهِ يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ: the apodosis (jawāb) of the imperative, and likewise وَيُجِرْكُمْ.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ: this is not from fatigue; for fatigue one says أعيا يعيي; and عيي بالأمر يعيى and عيّ به when he does not find his way to it.
«بقادر»: this is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «يقدر». [Translator's note: the source prints the first form as «بقدر», evidently for «بِقادِرٍ», the received reading which the following discussion assumes.] Some grammarians claimed that the reading «يقدر» is preferable because the bāʾ enters only in negation, and this is an affirmation, and expressed surprise at Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, how such a thing could have escaped them so that they erred in it, given their standing in Arabic. Abū Jaʿfar said: In this is an attack on those by whose reading authority is established. Moreover, the imams agreed in reading أَوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِقادِرٍ [Yā Sīn: 81], and we know of no difference between the two, and the community does not agree on what is impermissible. The grammarians have spoken about the verse that perplexed the one who said this. Al-Kisāʾī said: the bāʾ entered only because of «لم»; this is a sound view, and I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān explain it clearly. He said: the bāʾ enters in negation, so you say «ما زيدٌ بقائمٍ» (Zayd is not standing); when the interrogative enters upon the negation, it does not change it from what it was, so you say «أما زيدٌ بقائمٍ», and likewise «بقادر», because before it is a particle of negation, namely «لم». Abū Isḥāq said: the bāʾ enters in negation and does not enter in affirmation: you say «ظننتُ زيدا منطلقا» (I thought Zayd was leaving), and «ظننتُ زيدا بمنطلقٍ» is not permissible; if you bring a negation, you say «ما ظننتُ زيدا بمنطلقٍ»; and likewise His saying, Mighty and Majestic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقادِرٍ, and the meaning is: "Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able, in their sight and in their knowledge?"
Abū Jaʿfar said: If someone says, "Why does the bāʾ occur in negation and not in affirmation?", the answer according to the Basrans is that it entered to emphasize the negation, because it may happen that the one addressed does not hear «ما» or imagines a mistake; when you bring the bāʾ, he knows that it is a negation. As for the statement of the Kufans: the bāʾ in negation corresponds to the lām in affirmation.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ: with the meaning "and remember a day".

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: بَلاغٌ: there are two views on its meaning. One is that it means "a little"; one says "he has no provisions except بلاغ", i.e. a little. The other view is that the meaning is "in what they have been admonished with there is بلاغ (sufficient communication)", as al-Akhfash said. Some said: al-balāgh is the Qur'an. It is nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that is بلاغ"; whoever puts it in the accusative makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun) or a naʿt (adjective) of ساعة. فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْفاسِقُونَ, i.e. those who transgressed in this world. It is said that this verse is among the most hope-giving verses in the Qur'an, except that Ibn ʿAbbās said: the most hope-giving verse in the Qur'an is وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلى ظُلْمِهِمْ [al-Raʿd: 6].

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِن كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّن بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَىٰ مِثْلِهِ فَآمَنَ وَٱسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾.
It is said: there is an omission (ḥadhf) in the speech because the listener knows it.
And the meaning is: Have you considered, if it is from Allah, and a witness from the Children of Israel — one of those whom you trust and whose truthfulness and knowledge you recognise — has testified to what the Prophet ﷺ testified to, and you have disbelieved in it, have you not been deluded, and committed an ugly act, and been audacious about it?!
As for the witness from the Children of Israel, it is said that he is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām". «[Translator's note: the printed text has غنه, evidently a misprint for إنه, "that he".]»
Mālik related from Abū al-Naḍr, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, who said: "I never heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say of anyone walking on the face of the earth, 'He is among the people of Paradise', except of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām; and concerning him was revealed ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّن بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَىٰ مِثْلِهِ فَآمَنَ وَٱسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾."
And al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّن بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And there are two other views on the verse:
a- Masrūq said: It is not "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām", because the sura is Meccan; and the meaning refers to Moses ﷺ, the Torah and the People of the Book: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed the Torah to Moses, and the People of the Book believed in it; ﴿وَكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ is an address to Quraysh. He said: ﴿وَسَبَقُونَا إلَيْهِ﴾ means the People of the Book.
b- Ibn ʿAwn related from al-Shaʿbī concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّن بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَىٰ مِثْلِهِ﴾: he said: He is a man of the People of the Book, and not ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, because the sura is Meccan, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām only embraced Islam two years before the death of the Prophet ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This objection is not binding. "Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn" was asked about this very point, and he said: A verse would be revealed and they would be told: Attach it to such-and-such a sura.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So this is an answer to that.
And it is possible that the verse was revealed in Mecca, and the meaning is: Have you considered, if it is from Allah, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to the like of it, will you believe?
And al-Ḥasan said: This was revealed in Mecca, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām believed in Medina.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لَوْ كَانَ خَيْراً مَّا سَبَقُونَآ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
Masrūq said: They are the People of the Book.
And al-Ḥasan said: [They are] Aslam and Ghifār; so Quraysh said: If it were good, they would not have beaten us to it.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهَـٰذَا كِتَابٌ مُّصَدِّقٌ لِّسَاناً عَرَبِيّاً لِّيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
There are two answers on it:
One of them: that the meaning is: confirming it, i.e. the Book of Moses ﷺ; then it was omitted, because before it is ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ مُوسَىٰ إِمَاماً وَرَحْمَةً﴾.
And ﴿عَرَبِيّاً﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and ﴿لِّسَاناً﴾ is a preparatory element (tawṭiʾa) for the ḥāl, i.e. a reinforcement, as one says: jāʾanī Zaydun rajulan ṣāliḥan (Zayd came to me, a righteous man). What strengthens this is that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is ﴿وَهَذا كتابٌ مصدِّقٌ [لما بين يديه] لِسَاناً عَرَبيّاً﴾.
And the other answer: that ﴿لِّسَاناًً﴾ is a mafʿūl (object), by which the Prophet ﷺ is meant, and the meaning is: [confirming] one possessing an Arabic tongue.
Then He said ﴿لِتُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: and it is glad tidings.
And that the meaning is: and you give glad tidings to the doers of good, a glad tiding [i.e. bushrā as a maṣdar (verbal noun)].

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَامُواْ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾.
We have already explained the meaning of ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَامُواْ﴾ earlier.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ إِحْسَاناً﴾.
﴿إِحْسَاناً﴾: that is, he should do good to them, a doing of good [Translator's note: i.e. a maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb].
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهاً وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهاً﴾.
And it is read ﴿كَرْهاً﴾ with a fatḥa on the kāf, and according to some of the experts in Arabic this is a solecism (laḥn), because they distinguish between the two.
Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: al-kurh is hardship.
And al-Farrāʾ and a group of the experts in Arabic hold that al-karh with a fatḥa on the kāf is compulsion and coercion; so according to this view it would be a solecism.
And al-Kisāʾī said: al-karh and al-kurh have one meaning; and so it is according to all the Basrans — I know of no disagreement among them — because al-karh is the maṣdar (verbal noun) and al-kurh is a noun with its meaning.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةًً﴾.
Mujāhid said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ﴾, and he said: thirty-some years.
Mujāhid said: thirty-three.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And it is said: al-ashudd is eighteen years.
The first is more likely, because of the coherence of the speech — do you not see that after it is ﴿وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً﴾?
And also, one who has reached thirty-three years is more deserving of this name, because he is more complete.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِيۤ أَنْ أَشكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيۤ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَيَّ﴾.
Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus related from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿أَوْزِعْنِيۤ أَنْ أَشكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيۤ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَيَّ﴾: he said: He is Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq; neither a father nor a mother of his disbelieved. He said: and ﴿أَوْزِعْنِيۤ﴾: inspire me.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي قَالَ لِوَالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَّكُمَآ أَتَعِدَانِنِيۤ أَنْ أُخْرَجَ وَقَدْ خَلَتِ ٱلْقُرُونُ مِن قَبْلِي﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿أُفٍّ لَّكُمَآ﴾: that is, filth to you both. ﴿أَتَعِدَانِنِيۤ أَنْ أُخْرَجَ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: "This is an evil servant whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has described; he said to his parents: Do you promise me that I will be resurrected?"

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّبَاتِكُمْ فِي حَيَاتِكُمُ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
And Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read ﴿أَأَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّبَاتكُمْ فِي حَيَاتِكُمُ
الدُّنْيَا﴾? as a question.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The Arabs establish [a fact against someone] and rebuke both with a question and without a question.
And it is related that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, saw Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh with a man carrying something, and he said: What is this? He said: Meat I bought for a dirham. He said: Is it that whenever one of you has a craving he buys meat for a dirham? By Allah, if I wished to be the one of you with the finest food and the softest garment, I would do it; but Allah says: ﴿أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّبَاتِكُمْ فِي حَيَاتِكُمُ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾? So I leave my good things. «[Translator's note: the text has قام ("rose up"); the sense of the well-known report is "whenever one of you craves something", and the translation follows the evident intent.]»
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذَابَ ٱلْهُونِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: al-hūn is humiliation (al-hawān).

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ أَخَا عَادٍ إِذْ أَنذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِٱلأَحْقَافِ وَقَدْ خَلَتِ ٱلنُّذُرُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: ʿĀd were clans of Yemen; their dwellings were by the sands and the low mounds.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Ḥiqf according to the lexicographers is curved sand [dunes], and its plural is ḥiqafa and aḥqāf. And in the ḥadīth, the Prophet ﷺ passed by a gazelle ḥāqif, i.e. curled up, bent over.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتَأْفِكَنَا عَنْ آلِهَتِنَا﴾.
The meaning of ﴿لِتَأْفِكَنَا﴾ is: to turn us away.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضاً مُّسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قَالُواْ هَـٰذَا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا﴾.
That is, when they saw what they had been threatened with, like a cloud spreading across [the horizon], which had come across, containing punishment — and they did not know that it contained punishment — they said: This is a cloud bringing us rain.
Ṭāwūs related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "ʿĀd had a valley; when rain or clouds came from its direction it was [beneficial] rain. So Allah sent the punishment upon them from its direction. When Hūd ﷺ promised them the punishment and they saw the cloud, they said: ﴿هَـٰذَا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا﴾. Hūd, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿بَلْ هُوَ مَا ٱسْتَعْجَلْتُم بِهِ رِيحٌ فِيهَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾. They said: You have lied, you have lied."
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا لاَ يُرَى إلاَّ مَسَاكِنُهُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَاهُمْ فِيمَآ إِن مَّكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ سَمْعاً وَأَبْصَاراً وَأَفْئِدَةً﴾.
Qatāda said: Allah has informed us that He had established them in something in which He has not established us.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So "in" according to this view has the meaning of "mā" (negation).
And it has been said that it is zāʾida (redundant); but the first is more appropriate, because its redundancy is only known in negation, while in affirmation [the redundant particle] is "an" with a fatḥa.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ صَرَفْنَآ إِلَيْكَ نَفَراً مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ يَسْتَمِعُونَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ﴾.
Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh said: They were nine persons.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
That is, except for the establishing of the truth.
Then He said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ عَمَّآ أُنذِرُواْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾.
That is, they turned away after the truth had become clear to them from the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱصْبِرْ كَمَا صَبَرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلْعَزْمِ مِنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ﴾.
Qatāda said: They are four: "Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus", may Allah bless them.
And Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said: Those of resolve among the messengers are five: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muḥammad, may Allah bless them.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلاَغٌ فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلاَّ ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْفَاسِقُونَ﴾.
That is, that is a conveyance [Translator's note: i.e. khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject)].
And ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read ﴿بَلاَغاً﴾, and Abū Mijlaz read ﴿بَلِّغْ﴾ as an imperative.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلاَّ ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْفَاسِقُونَ؟﴾ [Verse 35].
That is, will any be destroyed — given Allah's mercy and His bounty — except the defiantly disobedient people?

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
Then He argued against them concerning what they worship, saying: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ مَّا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
﴿أَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقُواْ مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ؟﴾.
That is, in the creation of the heavens.
﴿ٱئْتُونِي بِكِتَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِ هَـٰذَآ﴾: that is, with a book containing proof of what you have said.
﴿أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: someone who transmits knowledge.
And al-Ḥasan said: something that is stirred up or extracted.
And Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿أَثَارَةٍ﴾: a remnant.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another, because a remnant is something transmitted; and it is well known in the language to say: saminat al-nāqatu ʿalā athāratin, i.e. the she-camel grew fat upon a remnant of [earlier] fatness.
And it is read ﴿أَوْ أَثَرَةٍ﴾.
Abū Salama related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿أَثَارَةٍ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ﴾: he said: writing (al-khaṭṭ).
Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad — known as al-Jurayjī — narrated to us: Bundār narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd informed us, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym, from Umm Salama, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ﴾: he said: writing.
And Saʿīd related from Qatāda: ﴿أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ﴾: he said: a special portion of knowledge.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says "so-and-so has an atharatun or uthratun with me", i.e. something with which I single him out; and from it comes āthartu fulānan ʿalā fulānin (I preferred so-and-so over so-and-so).
And it is possible that ﴿أَثَرَةٌ﴾ is a report from one of the prophets, may Allah bless them, from athartu al-ḥadītha (I transmitted the report); and this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, what you say.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعاً مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعاً مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ﴾: that is, the first one sent.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ﴾ — while He said in another place: ﴿لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ﴾.
The answer to this is that it is not of that [kind]; rather the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: and I do not know what will be done with me or with you, of drought or otherwise.
What makes this clear is that it is related that the Prophet ﷺ saw a dream that delighted his Companions, and they found its fulfilment slow in coming; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ﴾.

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being "it will be said to them" ... (الذين) a relative noun in the position of nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (على النار) preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يعرض), (في حياتكم) attached to (أذهبتم), (بها) attached to (استمتعتم), (الفاء) a conjunction linking the effect to the cause, (اليوم) an adverb attached to (تجزون), (ما) a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم) is in the position of genitive through the causal bāʾ, attached to (تجزون). (في الأرض) attached to (تستكبرون), (بغير) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of تستكبرون, (الواو) a conjunction and (ما) a maṣdar particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ...) is in the position of genitive through the second causal bāʾ, attached to what the first maṣdar is attached to. Clause: «(يقال) ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «يعرض الذين ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (second term of a genitive construct). Clause: «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين). Clause: «أذهبتم ...» is in the position of nominative, nāʾib fāʿil of the omitted verb. Clause: «استمتعتم ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أذهبتم ...
Clause: «تجزون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause. Clause: «كنتم ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما), the first. Clause: «تستكبرون ...» is in the position of accusative, khabar (predicate) of كنتم. Clause: «كنتم (the second)» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما), the second. Clause: «تفسقون» is in the position of accusative, khabar of the second كنتم.

* Rhetoric:
The art of inversion (qalb): in the words of the Exalted: «وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ».
This follows their saying: "The sons of so-and-so were exposed to the sword," when they were killed by it. As for the inversion, it is possible that what is meant is: the Fire is exposed to them, from their saying "I exposed the she-camel to the trough," meaning they intended "I exposed the trough to her," and so they inverted it. This is supported by the explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him: they are brought to it, and it is uncovered for them.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of accusative, badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for (أخا), (بالأحقاف) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «قومه», (الواو) circumstantial (قد) a particle of affirmation (من بين) attached to (خلت), and likewise (من خلفه), which is conjoined to the first (أن) explicative [Note: Or: lightened from the heavy (أنّ), its noun being an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) ... or a maṣdar particle, and the clause لا تعبدوا is the quoted speech of an implied "saying".], (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle (إلّا) for restriction (عليكم) attached to (أخاف) ...
Clause: «اذكر ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «أنذر ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. Clause: «قد خلت النذر ...» is in the position of accusative, ḥāl - or parenthetical with no grammatical position - Clause: «لا تعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position, explicative [Note: Or: in the position of nominative, khabar of the lightened (أن), the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of genitive through an omitted preposition attached to (أنذر), that is: warn his people that they should not worship ... except Allah ...] Clause: «إنّي أخاف ...» has no grammatical position, causal. Clause: «أخاف ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(عاد) is a proper noun for the people of Hūd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ, who lived in Yemen in a land called Shiḥr, or in a place called Mahra - Shiḥr with sukūn on the ḥāʾ - a place between ʿUmān and ʿAdan on the sea coast ...
(الأحقاف) is a proper noun for a place in Yemen, or between ʿUmān and ʿAdan. Al-aḥqāf is originally the plural of ḥiqf, which is a long, winding mass of sand. It is also said that al-aḥqāf is the plural of ḥiqāf, and this is a plural of ḥiqf ... The wazn of أحقاف is أفعال.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) interrogative (اللام) of purpose (تأفكنا) an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied أن after the lām (عن آلهتنا) attached to (تأفكنا), (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition (بما) attached to (ائتنا), the returning pronoun being omitted (كنت) a defective past verb, in the position of jussive, protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) (من الصادقين) attached to the khabar of كنت ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تأفكنا ...) is in the position of genitive, attached to (جئتنا). Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «أجئتنا ...» is in the position of accusative, quoted speech. Clause: «ائتنا ...» is in the position of jussive, apodosis of an implied condition, that is: if you are truthful, bring us ...
Clause: «تعدنا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما). Clause: «كنت من الصادقين ...» has no grammatical position, explicative of the implied condition - or resumptive - and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

* Morphology:
(آلهتنا) is the plural of ilāh, the name for what is worshipped; its verb is alaha ya'lahu (fatḥ pattern) meaning "he worshipped". Its wazn is فعال with kasra on the first letter, and the wazn of آلهة is أفعلة; the madda (lengthening sign) is two hamzas, the first with fatḥa and the second with sukūn [Note: And see verse (74) of Sūrat al-Anʿām.]

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) a restricting particle and the one restricted (kāffa and makfūfa) (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (به) attached to (أرسلت) (قوما) second direct object (mafʿūl bihi) ...
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position, explanatory resumption. Clause: «إنّما العلم عند الله ...» is in the position of accusative, quoted speech. Clause: «أبلّغكم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the quoted speech. Clause: «أرسلت به ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما). Clause: «لكنّي أراكم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the quoted speech. Clause: «أراكم ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of lakinna. Clause: «تجهلون ...» is in the position of accusative, naʿt (adjective) of (قوما).

safi-cedvel:24-28.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, attached to the apodosis (jawāb) «قالوا» (رأوه) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied ḍamma on the omitted alif because of the meeting of two sākin letters, and (الواو) is the agent (fāʿil), and (الهاء) is the pronoun referring back to (ما) (ما تعدنا) [Note: in verse (22).] direct object (mafʿūl bihi) (عارضا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the third-person pronoun (مستقبل) naʿt (adjective) of (عارضا), accusative like it [Note: This adjective is in the sense of detachment, that is: "facing their valleys" ... or this genitive construct does not give definiteness, and on this basis it is correct for (مستقبل) to be a second ḥāl.], (ممطرنا) a second khabar (predicate), nominative [Note: Or a naʿt of (عارض), nominative, and the genitive construct does not prevent that because it is not a true (non-restrictive) construct, like (مستقبل); or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.], (بل) for transitional rejoinder (iḍrāb) (ما) a relative noun in the position of nominative, khabar (به) attached to (استعجلتم), (ريح) badal (substitute) for (ما), nominative [Note: Or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it" (hiya or huwa).], (فيها) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب) ...
Clause: «رأوه ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition. Clause: «هذا عارض ...» is in the position of accusative, quoted speech. Clause: «هو ما استعجلتم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «استعجلتم ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما). Clause: «فيها عذاب ...» is in the position of nominative, naʿt of ريح. 25- (بأمر) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of تدمّر (الفاء) a conjunction linking the effect to the cause (لا) negative (إلّا) for restriction (مساكنهم) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the verb governing it being نجزي ...
Clause: «تدمّر ...» is in the position of nominative, second naʿt of ريح [Note: It is possible that it is an explanatory resumption, in which case it has no grammatical position.] Clause: «أصبحوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, that is: "so it destroyed them and so they became ..." Clause: «لا يرى إلّا مساكنهم» is in the position of accusative, khabar of أصبحوا. Clause: «نجزي ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical.
26- (الواو) conjunction (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of affirmation (ما) a relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to (مكنّاهم), (إن) a negative particle [Note: What confirms the meaning of negation is His saying, the Exalted: ... مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ ما لَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَكُمْ (al-Anʿām / 6) .. or it is a conditional particle and the apodosis is omitted, that is: "you would have transgressed" ... and some made it redundant, which is refuted by the verse of al-Anʿām.], (فيه) attached to (مكّنّاكم), (الواو) conjunction (لهم) in the position of the second object (الفاء) conjunction (ما) negative (عنهم) attached to (أغنى), (لا) redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis of the negation in both places (أبصارهم، أفئدتهم) conjoined to «سمعهم», both nominative like it (شيء) genitive in form, accusative in position, a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the verbal noun, that is: "any benefit", or "something of benefit" (إذ) an adverb of past time in the position of accusative, attached to (أغنى), (بآيات) attached to (يجحدون), (بهم) attached to (حاق), (ما) a relative noun in the position of nominative, agent, with an omitted muḍāf (first term of a construct), that is: "the recompense of what they used to ..." (به) attached to (يستهزئون). Clause: «مكّنّاهم ...» has no grammatical position, answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause is conjoined to the clause أصبحوا, so it has no grammatical position. Clause: «إن مكنّاكم فيه ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما). Clause: «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause مكنّاهم. Clause: «ما أغنى عنهم سمعهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause جعلنا. Clause: «كانوا ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. Clause: «يجحدون ...» is in the position of accusative, khabar of كانوا. Clause: «حاق بهم ما ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما أغنى ...
Clause: «كانوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (ما). Clause: «يستهزئون» is in the position of accusative, khabar of the second كانوا. 27- (الواو) conjunction (لقد أهلكنا ...) like «لقد مكنّا», (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, direct object (حولكم) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of ما (من القرى) tamyīz (specification) of the relative noun [Note: Or a ḥāl from the returning pronoun in the implied ṣila.] ...
Clause: «أهلكنا ...» has no grammatical position, answer to the implied oath ... and the oath clause is conjoined to the first oath clause. Clause: «صرّفنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the oath's answer. Clause: «لعلّهم» has no grammatical position, explanatory resumption. Clause: «يرجعون ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of laʿalla. 28- (الفاء) conjunction (لولا) for reproach (من دون) attached to a ḥāl of آلهة (قربانا) second direct object, its governing verb being اتّخذوا [Note: It is possible that it is a ḥāl from the omitted first object, the second object being آلهة ... and Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is: "for drawing near".], and the first object is implied, that is: "they took them" [Note: The third-person pronoun refers back to the idols expressed by the relative noun (الذين), and the agent of اتّخذوهم refers back to the unbelievers.], (آلهة) badal of (قربانا), accusative (بل) for transitional rejoinder (iḍrāb) (عنهم) attached to (ضلّوا) by implying the meaning "they were absent" (الواو) resumptive, and the second is a conjunction, (ما) a relative noun in the position of nominative, conjoined to (إفكهم) [Note: It may be a maṣdar particle, in which case the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to إفكهم.] and the returning pronoun is omitted. Clause: «لولا نصرهم الذين ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the previous resumptive clause. Clause: «اتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). Clause: «ضلّوا عنهم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «ذلك إفكهم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «كانوا يفترون ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما). Clause: «يفترون ...» is in the position of accusative, khabar of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(24) عارض: the name of the cloud that appears across the horizon, as given in al-Mukhtār; its wazn is فاعل. (مستقبل) an active participle from the six-letter verb istaqbala; its wazn is مستفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. (ممطر) an active participle from the four-letter verb amṭara; its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. (25) كلّ: a noun coined for the inclusion of the individuals of a plurality, or for the generality of the parts of a single thing; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- لولا..
We spoke about (لولا) in detail elsewhere. We will speak here about an aspect specific to the verse at hand: in this verse it conveys the meaning of reproach and regret, in His saying, the Exalted: فَلَوْلا نَصَرَهُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قُرْباناً آلِهَةً. When lawlā is for reproach and regret, it is specific to the past tense, as in the noble verse, and in His saying, the Exalted: لَوْلا جاؤُ عَلَيْهِ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ and لَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُمْ ما يَكُونُ لَنا أَنْ نَتَكَلَّمَ بِهذا. Here the verb is postponed, and the implied form is (لولا قلتم).
As for the saying of Jarīr:
تعدون عقر النيب أفضل مجدكم ... بني ضوطري لولا الكمّي المقنّعا
(You count the hamstringing of aged she-camels as the best of your glory ... O sons of the fool-woman, why not rather the armoured knight!)
the verb is hidden and the implied form is (لولا عددتم الكمي). The meaning of النيب is aged she-camels, and ضوطرى means a foolish woman.
Lawlā has been separated from the verb by إذ, by إذا, and by a parenthetical conditional clause. With إذ, as in His saying, the Exalted: فَلَوْلا إِذْ جاءَهُمْ بَأْسُنا تَضَرَّعُوا; with إذا, as in His saying, the Exalted: فَلَوْلا إِذا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلكِنْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ تَرْجِعُونَها إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ.
The meaning: why do you not return the soul when it reaches the throat, if you are not to be called to account, while your state is that you are watching that, and We are nearer to the dying person than you by Our knowledge, or by the angels, but you do not see it; and the second lawlā is a repetition of the first. It is not hidden that the most important uses of (لولا) are as a non-jussive conditional particle, being a particle of "prevention because of existence", specific to entering on a noun, such as "لولا المشقة ساد الناس كلهم" (Were it not for hardship, all people would have become masters). The noun after it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is obligatorily omitted, and the mastery of all people was prevented because of the existence of hardship.

safi-cedvel:29-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of accusative, direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (إليك) attached to صرفنا (من الجنّ) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (نفرا), (الفاء) conjunction (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the apodosis «قالوا» ... (فلمّا قضي) like «لمّا حضروا», attached to (ولّوا), and the pronoun of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) refers back to the Noble Qur'an (إلى قومهم) attached to (ولوا) (منذرين) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the agent of ولّوا ...
Clause: «صرفنا ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; and the implied clause "remember" has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «يستمعون ...» is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from (نفرا). Clause: «حضروه ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition. Clause: «أنصتوا ...» is in the position of accusative, quoted speech. Clause: «قضي ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. Clause: «ولّوا ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition. 30- (من بعد) attached to (أنزل), (لما) attached to (مصدّقا) [Note: Or the lām is redundant for reinforcement, and (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, direct object of the active participle (مصدّقا).], (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of ما (إلى الحقّ) attached to (يهدي) and likewise (إلى طريق), conjoined to the first.
Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, explanatory resumption. Clause: «يا قومنا ...» is in the position of accusative, quoted speech. Clause: «إنّا سمعنا ...» has no grammatical position, answer to the vocative. Clause: «سمعنا ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna. Clause: «أنزل ...» is in the position of accusative, naʿt of (كتابا). Clause: «يهدي ...» is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from (كتابا) - or a second naʿt.
31- (به) attached to (آمنوا), (من ذنوبكم) attached to (يغفر), likewise (لكم); and (من) is partitive (من عذاب) attached to the verb (يجركم).
Clause: «يا قومنا (the second)» has no grammatical position, a resumption within the sphere of the quoted speech. Clause: «أجيبوا ...» has no grammatical position, answer to the vocative. Clause: «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative. Clause: «يغفر ...» has no grammatical position, apodosis of an implied condition, not joined by the fāʾ. Clause: «يجركم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis. (الواو) conjunction (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) (لا) negative (الفاء) linking the apodosis (معجز) genitive in form through the bāʾ, accusative in position, khabar of ليس (في الأرض) attached to (معجز) (له) attached to the second khabar of ليس (من دونه) attached to a ḥāl from (أولياء), which is the noun of ليس (في ضلال) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
Clause: «من لا يجب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative. Clause: «لا يجب ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ. Clause: «ليس بمعجز ...» is in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined by the fāʾ. Clause: «ليس له ... أولياء» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause of the apodosis. Clause: «أولئك في ضلال مبين» has no grammatical position, explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(30) طريق: a non-derived noun for what is walked upon, in plain or mountain; its wazn is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
The art of tankīt (pointed precision): in the words of the Exalted «يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ».
That is, "He will forgive you some of your sins," so (من) is partitive. He expressed it so as to indicate that He, the Exalted, forgives what falls purely within the right of Allah the Exalted, for the rights of servants are not forgiven by faith.

* Benefits:
The jinn listening to the Qur'an and their becoming Muslim..
This verse shows that the Prophet ﷺ was sent to both jinn and humans, and that the jinn are charged with the commands of the Law. The gist of the story: the Prophet ﷺ travelled to al-Ṭāʾif to call it to Islam, met its notables and called them, but they refused him and incited their fools against him, who harmed him until his feet bled. He turned back to Mecca, and when he was at Baṭn Nakhla he stood in the depth of the night to pray. A band of the jinn of Naṣībīn, who were heading for Yemen, passed by him and listened to him. When he finished his prayer they went back to their people as warners; they had believed in him and answered when they heard the Qur'an, so Allah narrated their story to him.
In another hadith, the Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions: "I have been commanded to recite to the jinn tonight, so which of you will follow me?" ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd followed him. He said: We set out, and when we were in the upper part of Mecca, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ entered the pass of al-Ḥajūn and drew a line for me, then commanded me to sit in it and said: "Do not leave it until I return to you." He went on until he stood before them and began reciting the Qur'an. I began to see shapes like eagles swooping down, and I heard a great clamour, until I feared for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ; many black forms covered him and came between me and him, so that I could not hear his voice. Then they began to disperse, like pieces of cloud, going away. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished with them at dawn, and came to me and said to me: "Did you sleep?" I said: No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I intended several times to call the people for help, until I heard you striking them with your staff, saying to them: "Sit down." He said: "Had you gone out, I would not have been safe for you that some of them might snatch you away." Then he said: "Did you see anything?" I said: Yes, I saw black men wearing white garments. He said: "Those are the jinn of Naṣībīn. They asked me for provision, and provision is food, so I provided for them every old bone, and dung and droppings. As for the bone, it is their food, and as for the dung and droppings, it is fodder for their animals." They said: O Messenger of Allah, people will foul these for us. So the Prophet ﷺ forbade cleaning oneself with bone or dung.
He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, what does that avail them? He said: "They never find a bone but they find on it the flesh it had on the day it was eaten, nor any dung but they find in it its grain as it was on the day it was eaten." I said: O Messenger of Allah, I heard a great clamour. He said: "The jinn disputed about a man who was killed among them; they brought their dispute to me and I judged between them with the truth."
Among the jinn there are many communities, as among humans: among them are Jews, Christians, Zoroastrians and idol-worshippers. The verifying scholars are agreed that all of them are charged with obligations. Ibn ʿAbbās was asked whether the jinn have reward, and he said: Yes, they have reward and they have punishment.

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) interrogative of reproach (الواو) conjunction (الذي) a relative noun in the position of accusative, naʿt (adjective) of the name of Majesty (Allah) (الواو) conjunction (بخلقهنّ) attached to (يعي), (قادر) genitive in form, nominative in position, khabar of أنّ ... [Note: The bāʾ was added to the khabar of anna although the sentence is affirmative, because the meaning is on the implied form "Is not Allah able?", and the general rule in grammar states: a thing may be given the ruling of what resembles it in meaning.]
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله ...) is in the position of accusative, standing in for the two objects of يروا; and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يحيى ...) is in the position of genitive through (على), attached to (قادر). (بلى) a particle of response affirming the opposite of the negation, that is: He is able to give life to the dead (على كلّ) attached to (قدير). Clause: «يروا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, that is: "Were they heedless and did they not see ..?"
Clause: «خلق ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (الذي). Clause: «لم يعي ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause. Clause: «يحيى ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن). Clause: «إنّه ... قدير» has no grammatical position, a justification of the implied answer.

* Morphology:
(يعي) it contains an i'lāl (weak-letter change) by omission, in keeping with the jussive; its original is يعيا. Its wazn is يفع.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal (unrestricted figurative usage): in the words of the Exalted «وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ», that is: He did not tire nor weary at all by that, or He was not incapable of it. Fatigue is the cause of ceasing work, or of deficiency in it and delay in completing it. So the relation of this figure is causality.

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "it will be said" ... (على النار) attached to (يعرض), (الهمزة) interrogative (الحقّ) genitive in form through the bāʾ, accusative in position, khabar of ليس (بلى) a particle of response (الواو) the wāw of oath (ربّنا) genitive through the wāw, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition (ما) a maṣdar particle, and (الباء) causal ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ...) is in the position of genitive through the bāʾ, attached to (ذوقوا). Clause: «(يقال) يوم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «يعرض الذين ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. Clause: «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). Clause: «أليس هذا بالحقّ ...» is in the position of nominative, nāʾib fāʿil. Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, explanatory resumption ... and the quoted speech is omitted after the particle of response, that is: "Yes, it is the truth". Clause of oath: «ربّنا ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical. Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «ذوقوا ...» is in the position of jussive, apodosis of an implied condition, that is: if you acknowledge the disbelief, then taste ...
Clause: «كنتم تكفرون» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما). Clause: «تكفرون» is in the position of accusative, khabar of كنتم.

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition (ما) a maṣdar particle (من الرسل) attached to a ḥāl from (أولو العزم) and the interpreted maṣdar (ما صبر ...) is in the position of genitive through the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), that is: "patience like the patience of those of firm resolve".
(الواو) conjunction (لا) prohibitive (لهم) attached to (تستعجل), (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يلبثوا), (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, direct object, the returning pronoun being omitted, and (الواو) in (يوعدون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (إلّا) for restriction (ساعة) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يلبثوا), (من نهار) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (ساعة) (بلاغ) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "this" - or "it" - the reference being to the Qur'an or the legislation ... (الفاء) resumptive (هل) interrogative containing the sense of negation (إلّا) for restriction (القوم) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative. Clause: «اصبر ...» is in the position of jussive, apodosis of an implied condition, that is: if you are harmed, then be patient. Clause: «صبر أولو العزم ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما). Clause: «لا تستعجل ...» is conjoined to the clause of the apodosis. Clause: «كأنّهم ... لم يلبثوا» has no grammatical position, causal - or explanatory resumption. Clause: «يرون ...» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «يوعدون ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما). Clause: «لم يلبثوا ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar of ka'anna. Clause: «(هذا) بلاغ ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive. Clause: «يهلك إلّا القوم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(ساعة) the name of the known, fixed span of time; its wazn is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ, ʿayn and lām. It contains an i'lāl by substitution: its original is سوعة with fatḥa on the three letters; the wāw, being vowelled after a fatḥa, was changed to alif.

* Benefits:
- Those of firm resolve among the messengers..
This verse mentions those of firm resolve among the messengers. Ibn ʿAbbās said: the meaning of "ulū l-ʿazm" is those possessed of resoluteness. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: those possessed of earnestness and patience. The scholars differed over who the ulū l-ʿazm among the messengers are. Ibn Zayd said: all the messengers were ulū l-ʿazm, and all the prophets possess resoluteness, patience, judgement, perfection and intellect. This view is the choice of Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī, because the word (من) in His saying "from the messengers" is explanatory, not partitive, as you say "a garment of silk". Some said they are the noble ones of the messengers mentioned in Sūrat al-Anʿām, and they are eighteen, because He said after mentioning them: (أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده). Al-Kalbī said: they are those who were commanded to fight and who showed hostility toward the enemies of Allah. It was also said: they are six: Nūḥ, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Lūṭ, Shuʿayb and Mūsā, who are mentioned in sequence in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf and al-Shuʿarāʾ. Muqātil said: they are six: Nūḥ, who was patient with the harm of his people; Ibrāhīm, who was patient with the fire; Yaʿqūb, who was patient with the loss of his son and the dimming of his sight; Yūsuf, who was patient with the well and the prison; and Ayyūb, who was patient with affliction. Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda said: they are Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, ʿĪsā and Muḥammad, may Allah's blessings be upon them all, for they are the bearers of the laws, and Allah mentioned them specifically and by name in His saying: وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثاقَهُمْ وَمِنْكَ وَمِنْ نُوحٍ وَإِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ.
Al-Baghawī narrated with his chain from ʿĀʾisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This world is not fitting for Muḥammad nor for the family of Muḥammad. O ʿĀʾisha, Allah was not pleased with the ulū l-ʿazm except with patience over its disagreeable things, and He was not pleased except to charge me with what He charged them, saying: (فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل). And I, by Allah, must obey Him; by Allah, I shall be patient as they were patient, and I shall strive, and there is no power but with Allah."
The last view is the most preferable. These are the views, and Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:1-2.t:
* I'rab:
(تنزيل) a mubtadaʾ, nominative. (من الله) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
The clause: «the nominal clause ... » has no grammatical position (inceptive).

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative, and the second is a relative noun in the position of an accusative, conjoined to السموات. (إلّا) for restriction. (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of خلقنا or from its object [Note: Or attached to an omitted absolute object, the bāʾ being that of accompaniment.]. (أجل) conjoined to الحقّ by the wāw, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "and the appointing of a term". (عمّا) attached to the khabar (معرضون), and the (الواو) in (أنذروا) is the nāʾib fāʿil ...
Clause: «ما خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).
Clause: «أنذروا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (ما), whether noun or particle).

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(أرأيتم) meaning "tell me", and the hamza is for interrogation. (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, a first direct object. (من دون) attached to a ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun [Note: Or a tamyīz (specification) of (ما).]. (ماذا) a mubtadaʾ and khabar. (من الأرض) attached to (خلقوا) [Note: Or to a ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun.]. (أم) is the detached (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل, together with the hamza. (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ شرك. (في السموات) attached to (شرك), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "in the creation of the heavens". (بكتاب) attached to (ائتوني). (من قبل) an adjective (naʿt) of كتاب. (أو) a conjunction. (أثارة) conjoined to كتاب. (من علم) attached to an adjective of (أثارة). (كنتم) an incomplete past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis ...
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «رأيتم ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «تدعون» has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (ما)).
Clause: «أروني ... » has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumptive clause).
Clause: «ماذا خلقوا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the second direct object of the second verb of seeing, and the object of the first verb of seeing is omitted, indicated by what is mentioned.
Clause: «خلقوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (ذا)).
Clause: «لهم شرك ... » has no grammatical position (a resumptive within the scope of the saying).
Clause: «ائتوني ... » has no grammatical position (a resumptive within the scope of the saying).
Clause: «كنتم صادقين» has no grammatical position (resumptive) ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

* Morphology:
(أثارة): a samāʿī (heard, not rule-based) maṣdar of the verb أثر, triliteral, of the chapter of نصر, meaning "he reported the ḥadīth or the report or other", its pattern is فعالة with fatḥa on the fāʾ, like ضلالة, i.e. a remnant of knowledge..

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (من) an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (أضلّ). (ممّن) attached to (أضلّ). (من دون) attached to a ḥāl from the relative: من لا يستجيب. (لا) negative. (له) attached to (يستجيب). (إلى يوم) attached to (يستجيب). (الواو) a conjunction - or a ḥāl wāw. (عن دعائهم) attached to (غافلون) ..
Clause: «من أضلّ ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «يدعو ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (من)).
Clause: «لا يستجيب ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the second relative (من)).
Clause: «هم ... غافلون» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause لا يستجيب) [Note: Or it is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يستجيب which refers to the second (من) ...].
6- (الواو) conjunction. (لهم) attached to a ḥāl from (أعداء), the khabar of كانوا. (بعبادتهم) attached to the second khabar of كانوا. (كافرين).
Clause: «حشر الناس» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi..
Clause: «كانوا ... (the first)» has no grammatical position (apodosis of a non-jussive condition).
Clause: «كانوا ... (the second)» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause كانوا (the first)).

* Rhetoric:
1- A rhetorical point: in His saying, the Exalted, «إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ».
In it there is a fine and wonderful point, namely that He made the Day of Resurrection the limit of the non-response, and the nature of a limit is that the thing ends at it. But the non-response continues beyond this limit, because on the Day of Resurrection too they will not respond to them. So the explanation is that it belongs to those limits which indicate that what comes after them, though it agrees with what came before, exceeds it by a clear excess that attaches it to the second, so that the two states, though one in kind, are, because of the difference between them, like a thing and its opposite. That is, the first state, whose limit was made the Resurrection, does not go beyond non-response, while the second state, that of the Resurrection, adds to non-response enmity and their disbelief in the worship they offered them; and that is mentioned in the verse after it. It belongs to the same vein as what came earlier in Sūrat al-Zukhruf in His saying «بَلْ مَتَّعْتُ هؤُلاءِ وَآباءَهُمْ حَتَّى جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ وَرَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ وَلَمَّا جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ وَإِنَّا بِهِ كافِرُونَ».
2- Predominance of the rational (al-taghlīb): in His saying, the Exalted, «مَنْ لا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ وَهُمْ عَنْ دُعائِهِمْ غافِلُونَ». Here He ascribed to what they call upon besides Allah, the idols, what is ascribed to those possessed of knowledge, namely responding and being heedless, by way of predominance. That is because they used to describe them as having discernment, out of ignorance and stupidity.

safi-cedvel:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (عليهم) attached to (تتلى), and the pronoun of the third person refers to the disbelievers of Mecca. (بيّنات) an accusative ḥāl from آياتنا. (للحق) attached to (قال), and (اللام) is of purpose, i.e. "on account of it". (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", devoid of conditionality, attached to (قال).
Clause: «تتلى عليهم ... » is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi ... and the condition, its verb and its apodosis are resumptive.
Clause: «قال الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position (apodosis of a non-jussive condition).
Clause: «جاءهم ... » is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «هذا سحر ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
8- (أم) the detached (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل, together with the hamza of denial. (افتريته) a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis. (الفاء) linking the apodosis. (لا) negative. (لي) attached to (تملكون), by its being given the sense of "you put forward". (من الله) attached to a ḥāl from (شيئا), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "from the punishment of Allah". (بما) attached to أعلم. (فيه) attached to (تفيضون). (الهاء) in (به): its remote position is the fāʿil of كفى, and its near position is genitive by the redundant bāʾ. (شهيدا) an accusative ḥāl - or a tamyīz (specification). (بيني) an accusative adverbial attached to (شهيدا). (بينكم) conjoined to بيني and attached to (شهيدا). (الواو) conjunction. (الرحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
Clause: «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «افتراه ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «افتريته ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «لا تملكون ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being أنتم, and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
Clause: «هو أعلم ... » has no grammatical position (giving the reason for the preceding negation).
Clause: «تفيضون ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (ما)).
Clause: «كفى به ... » has no grammatical position (a resumptive within the scope of the saying).
Clause: «هو الغفور ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause كفى به).

* Morphology:
(كفى): it contains a weakening by substitution (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its origin is كفى, its imperfect يكفي: the yāʾ received a vowel after a fatḥa, so it was turned into alif. [Translator's note: The source writes the origin in the same form as the word itself; the intended original form is presumably كفِيَ with yāʾ.]

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative. (من الرسل) attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (بدعا). (الواو) conjunction. (ما) like the first, and the third is an indefinite noun with a descriptive clause, in the position of an accusative, a direct object [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of an accusative ... or an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يفعل.. and the interrogative clause stands in for the two objects of أدري, which is suspended by the interrogative.]. (بي) attached to (يفعل). (لا) redundant, for emphasis of the negation. (بكم) attached to (يفعل), so it is conjoined to the first prepositional phrase. (إن) a particle of negation. (إلّا) for restriction. (ما) a relative in the position of an accusative, a direct object, and the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb (يوحى) is the returning pronoun. (إليّ) attached to (يوحى). (الواو) conjunction. (ما) negative, non-operative. (إلّا) like the first ...
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «ما كنت بدعا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «ما أدري ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the quoted speech.
Clause: «يفعل ... » is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of (ما) [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, as the ṣila of the relative (ما).].
Clause: «أتّبع ... » has no grammatical position (giving a reason).
Clause: «يوحى ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (ما)).
Clause: «ما أنا إلّا نذير ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause giving a reason) [Note: Or it is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the quoted speech.].

* Morphology:
(بدعا): the maṣdar of بدع يبدع, of the chapter of فتح, its pattern is فِعل with kasra then sukūn, and it means "he invented the thing and made it on a unique model" ... or it is of the chapter of كرم but is an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), i.e. "he was a bidʿ", that is, unique ...

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
The two objects of the verb (رأيتم) are implied, i.e. "Have you considered your state, if it is thus ... are you not wrongdoers?" (كان) an incomplete past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis. (من عند) attached to the khabar of كان. (به) attached to (كفرتم). (من بني) attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (شاهد). (على مثل) attached to (شهد). (الفاء) conjunction. (لا) negative ...
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «أرأيتم ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «كان من عند الله ... » has no grammatical position (parenthetical, between the verb and its two implied objects), and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "you have lost".
Clause: «كفرتم به ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause كان ...) [Note: It is possible for the clause to be a ḥāl clause with an implied قد, and likewise the clauses following it by conjunction.].
Clause: «شهد شاهد ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause كان).
Clause: «آمن ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause شهد).
Clause: «استكبرتم ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause آمن).
Clause: «إنّ الله لا يهدي ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

* Benefits:
The truthfulness of prophethood..
This verse indicates the truthfulness of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ. A scholar from among the Jews bore witness to it and believed. But the disbelievers were arrogant and did not believe. The scholars differed about this witness, and the majority hold that he was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām. This is indicated by what
is reported on the authority of Anas ibn Mālik, who said: News of the Prophet's ﷺ arrival in Medina reached ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, so he came to him and said: "I am going to ask you about three things that none knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food the people of Paradise will eat? And from what does the child incline to its father? And from what does the child incline to its mother" - and in another narration "to its maternal uncles"? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Gabriel has just informed me of them." ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām said: "That is the enemy of the Jews." So he recited this verse: مَنْ كانَ عَدُوًّا لِجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلى قَلْبِكَ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west; as for the first food the people of Paradise will eat, it is the extra lobe of the fish's liver; and as for the resemblance of the child, when a man has intercourse with a woman and his fluid precedes hers, the resemblance is to him, and when hers precedes, the resemblance is to her." He said:
"I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." Then he said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people of slander (liars). If they learn of my conversion to Islam before you ask them about me, they will slander me before you." So the Jews came, and ʿAbd Allāh entered the house, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What kind of man is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām among you?" They said: "The most knowledgeable of us and the son of our most knowledgeable, our best and the son of our best." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you see, if ʿAbd Allāh becomes a Muslim?" They said:
"May Allah protect him from that." Then ʿAbd Allāh came out to them and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." They said: "Our worst and the son of our worst," and they attacked him. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām said: "This is what I feared, O Messenger of Allah." Al-Bukhārī transmitted it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (للذين) attached to (قال), and (اللام) means "on account of". (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle, and the ism of (كان) is omitted, referring to what the Messenger brought of faith and the Qur'an, understood from the context. (ما) negative. (إليه) attached to (سبقونا). (الواو) conjunction. (إذ) an adverb of past time attached to an omitted element required by the context, i.e. "they said what they said", or "their obstinacy appeared" [Note: Attachment to (يقولون) is not permitted because of the difference of the two times and because of the presence of the fāʾ.]. (به) attached to the negated (يهتدوا). (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause. (السين) a particle of futurity ....
Clause: «قال الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (الذين)).
Clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the (second) relative (الذين)).
Clause: «كان خيرا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «ما سبقونا ... » has no grammatical position (apodosis of a non-jussive condition).
Clause: «لم يهتدوا ... » is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «سيقولون ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the implied resumptive clause).
Clause: «هذا إفك ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (من قبله) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كتاب). (إماما) an accusative ḥāl from كتاب, its governor being the notion of settledness (istiqrār). (مصدّق) an adjective of كتاب - or a second khabar - nominative. (لسانا) a ḥāl from the pronoun in مصدّق [Note: Or from كتاب, its governor being the sense of the demonstrative ... The ḥāl came as a non-derived noun because it was qualified ... and (لسانا) is a direct object of the active participle - in the opinion of Abū al-Baqāʾ - on the basis that the demonstrative refers to something other than the noble Qur'an.]. (اللام) of purpose. (ينذر) an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (الواو) conjunction. (بشرى) conjoined to مصدّق, nominative [Note: Or conjoined to the position of (لينذر), which is accusative because it is an object of purpose; so said al-Zamakhsharī, and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him; or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ ...]. (للمحسنين) attached to (بشرى).
Clause: «من قبله كتاب ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive). Clause: «هذا كتاب ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause). Clause: «ينذر ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the implied particle (أن)), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن ينذر) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to مصدّق. Clause: «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (الذين)).

safi-cedvel:13-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) redundant in the khabar of إنّ, because the relative - the ism of إنّ - resembles a condition. (لا) negative. (خوف) a mubtadaʾ, nominative, relying on a negation. (عليهم) attached to an omitted khabar. (الواو) conjunction. (لا) redundant, for emphasis of the negation ...
Clause: «إن الذين ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (الذين)). Clause: «ربّنا الله ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech. Clause: «استقاموا» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause قالوا). Clause: «لا خوف عليهم ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
Clause: «هم يحزنون» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause of the khabar.
