Clause: «يحزنون» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
14- (أصحاب) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك. (خالدين) an accusative ḥāl from the latent pronoun in أصحاب, its governor being the demonstrative. (فيها) attached to (خالدين). (جزاء) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb, i.e. "they are recompensed a recompense". (ما) a maṣdar particle ... [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted, and the clause its ṣila.]
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا يعملون) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the implied verb - or to جزاء if it substitutes for its verb. Clause: «أولئك أصحاب ... » has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumptive clause - or giving a reason). Clause: «كانوا يعملون» has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle (ما)). Clause: «يعملون» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of كانوا.

safi-cedvel:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (بوالديه) attached to (وصّينا). (إحسانا) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb [Note: It may be a second direct object whose governor is وصينا, by its being given the sense of "We obligated" ... as it may also be an object of purpose.]. (كرها) an absolute object substituting for the maṣdar, so it is its adjective, i.e. "a bearing with hardship" [Note: Or a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl.], in both places. (الواو) conjunction in the six places. (حمله) a mubtadaʾ with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "the period of his bearing"; its khabar is (ثلاثون). (حتّى) a particle of commencement. (أربعين) a direct object, accusative. (ربّ) a vocative muḍāf, accusative, and the muḍāf ilayhi - the (yāʾ) of the speaker - is omitted. (التي) a relative in the position of an accusative, an adjective of نعمتك. (عليّ) attached to (أنعمت), and likewise (على والديّ), which is conjoined to the first ... (الواو) conjunction. (أن أعمل) like أن أشكر ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أشكر) is in the position of an accusative, a second direct object whose governor is أوزعني; and the interpreted maṣdar (أن أعمل) is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
(صالحا) a direct object, accusative [Note: Or an absolute object substituting for the maṣdar, so it is its adjective, with the object implied.]. (لي) attached to (أصلح), and likewise (في ذرّيّتي) [Note: As if the offspring were a container for the righteousness.]. (إليك) attached to (تبت). (من المسلمين) attached to the khabar of إنّ..
Clause: «وصّينا ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive). Clause: «(أحسن) إحسانا» has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumptive clause).
Clause: «حملته أمّه ... » has no grammatical position (giving a reason).
Clause: «وضعته ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause giving a reason). Clause: «حمله ... ثلاثون شهرا» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause giving a reason). Clause: «بلغ أشدّه» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi. Clause: «بلغ أربعين سنة» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause بلغ (the first). Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position (apodosis of a non-jussive condition). Clause: «the vocative and its answer ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech. Clause: «أوزعني ... » has no grammatical position (the answer to the vocative). Clause: «أشكر ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle (أن)). Clause: «أنعمت ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (التي)). Clause: «أعمل ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the second particle (أن)). Clause: «ترضاه ... » is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of (صالحا). Clause: «أصلح ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause answering the vocative). Clause: «إنّي تبت ... » has no grammatical position (a resumptive within the scope of the saying). Clause: «تبت ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ. Clause: «إنّي من المسلمين» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause إنّي تبت ...).
16- (عنهم) attached to (نتقبّل), by its being given the sense of "We receive". (ما) a maṣdar particle. (عن سيّئاتهم) attached to (نتجاوز). (في أصحاب) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (عنهم), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "among the company of the companions" ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عملوا) is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi. (وعد) an absolute object of an omitted verb, confirming the content of the preceding sentence. (الذي) a relative in the position of an accusative, an adjective of وعد, and the (الواو) in (يوعدون) is the nāʾib fāʿil, with the returning pronoun omitted. Clause: «أولئك الذين» has no grammatical position (resumptive). Clause: «نتقبّل ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (الذين)). Clause: «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle (ما)). Clause: «نتجاوز ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause نتقبّل). Clause: «(نعدهم) وعد ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive - or a ḥāl from the fāʿil of نتقبّل). Clause: «كانوا يوعدون» has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (الذي)). Clause: «يوعدون» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(والديه): the dual of والد, a noun meaning "father", on the pattern فاعل; the feminine is والدة. (ثلاثون): one of the words of the decades, a name of a number, attached to the sound masculine plural. (تبت): it contains a weakening by omission, to suit the construction on sukūn; its origin is توبت - with a wāw between the tāʾ and the bāʾ - and when two sukūns met, the wāw was dropped; its pattern is فُلت with ḍamma on the fāʾ as an indication of the omitted wāw.

* Rhetoric:
The loose figurative expression (al-majāz al-mursal): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصالُهُ ثَلاثُونَ شَهْراً».
Al-fiṣāl is weaning (al-fiṭām), and what is meant here is its period which weaning follows, so its relation is contiguity.

* Benefits:
1- The cases in which the verb can only be intransitive. In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted, وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي, and the verb "أصلح" came intransitive because it means (بارك) "bless". The grammarians have mentioned the cases in which the verb is intransitive, and they are:
1- If it is on the pattern فعل [Translator's note: the source gives the patterns without vowel marks; the examples شرف and ظرف indicate the pattern فَعُلَ]: such as شرف - ظرف.
2- If it is on the pattern فعل or فعل [Translator's note: as written in the source, without vowels], and their adjective on the pattern فعيل, such as: ذلّ and قوي.
3- If it is on the pattern أفعل, meaning "he became possessed of", such as: أحصد الزرع, i.e. "the crop became possessed of harvest".
4- If it is on the pattern افعللّ such as: اقشعرّ - اشمأزّ.
5- If it is on the pattern افعنلل, with both lāms being radical, such as احرنجم (he gathered).
6- If it is on the pattern (افعنلى), such as احرنبى الديك, when the rooster ruffles its feathers.
7- If it is on the pattern انفعل such as: انطلق and انكسر.
8- If it is given the sense of an intransitive verb, as in His saying, the Exalted: أَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي meaning (بارك), as occurs in this very verse we are dealing with.
9- If it is quadriliteral augmented, such as: تدحرج - اطمأنّ.
10- If it denotes a natural disposition, like لؤم, جبن and شجع, or an accidental state (a transient condition), like فرح and حزن, or what denotes purity or defilement such as طهر and نجس, or a colour like أحمرّ and أخضر, or an adornment: like دعج - وكحل - وسمن - وهزل.
And the meaning of: "إن البغاث بأرضنا يستنسر" is: the weak bird becomes strong like the eagle.
This is a proverb applied to the lowly who becomes mighty.
2- Dutifulness to parents..
This verse calls to dutifulness to parents. This is mentioned in several places in the noble Qur'an; the Exalted said: وَقَضى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُما أَوْ كِلاهُما فَلا تَقُلْ لَهُما أُفٍّ وَلا تَنْهَرْهُما وَقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلًا كَرِيماً.
The scholars said: Had there been a word lesser than the word (أف) expressing ill-treatment of the parents, Allah the Exalted would have mentioned it.
We also notice how Allah the Mighty and Majestic joined obedience to the parents with obedience to Himself, to draw attention to the greatness of their standing and the loftiness of their station,
and it is reported that a man served his mother for a long time, took her, performed the pilgrimage with her, and circumambulated and ran between Ṣafā and Marwa with her, and thought that he had fulfilled her right; so he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he, upon him be peace and blessings, said to him: "You have not fulfilled even [one of] her [...] in her belly during pregnancy." [Translator's note: the source word «بعطة» is unclear; the sense is apparently one pang or sigh of hers during pregnancy.]
He, upon him be peace and blessings, also foretold the conversion to Islam of Uways from Yemen, and used to instruct his companions to seek supplication from him. Uways al-Qaranī, may Allah be pleased with him, was unable to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, met him during the pilgrimage and said to him: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed us to seek supplication from you; you must have a righteous deed." Uways said: "I was eager to meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but serving my mother kept me from him."
By this we see the measure of the importance and regard that parents have.
3- The duration of pregnancy and nursing....
The jurists derived from His saying, the Exalted, وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصالُهُ ثَلاثُونَ شَهْراً that the shortest period of pregnancy is six months, and the longest period of nursing is twenty-four months. Ibn ʿAbbās said:
When a woman carries for nine months she nurses for twenty-one months, and when she carries for six months she nurses for twenty-four months.
3- The occasions of revelation of His saying, the Exalted: «أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ..»
The soundest view is that it was revealed concerning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him. That was because he accompanied the Prophet ﷺ, when twenty years old, on a trading journey to Syria. They stopped at a halting place in which there was a lote tree, and the Prophet ﷺ sat in its shade, while Abū Bakr went to a monk there to ask him about religion. The monk asked him about the man in the shade of the lote tree, and he said:
"He is Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib." The monk said: "By Allah, this is a prophet. No one has sat in its shade since ʿĪsā, upon him be peace and blessings, except this man, and he is the prophet of the end of time." Certainty and belief settled in Abū Bakr's heart, so he never left the Prophet ﷺ, on journey or at home. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached forty years, Allah the Exalted honoured him with prophethood and distinguished him with His message, and Abū Bakr believed in him and affirmed his truth, at thirty-eight years of age. When he reached forty years he called upon Allah the Mighty and Majestic (قالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلى والِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صالِحاً تَرْضاهُ وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي إِنِّي تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ), and his Lord answered him, so his parents and his sons embraced Islam, may Allah be pleased with them all.

safi-cedvel:17-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (الذي) a relative, a mubtadaʾ in the position of a nominative, meant as a generic; its khabar is the clause (أولئك الذين) ... (لوالديه) attached to (قال). (أفّ) an imperfect verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning "I am vexed", and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا" (I). (لكما) attached to the verbal noun (أفّ). (الهمزة) of interrogation expressing denial, and the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive (أخرج) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا" (I); the interpreted maṣdar (أن أخرج) is in the position of an accusative, a second direct object whose governor is تعدانني [Note: Or in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, the bāʾ, attached to (تعدانني).]. (الواو) a ḥāl wāw. (قد) a particle of confirmation. (من قبلي) attached to (خلت). (الواو) the second is also a ḥāl wāw. (ويلك) an absolute object of an omitted, disused verb. (الفاء) conjunction. (ما) negative. (إلّا) for restriction ...
Clause: «الذي قال ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive). Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (الذي)). Clause: «أفّ لكما ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, being parenthetical, and the clause تعدانني becomes the quoted speech.]. Clause: «أتعدانني ... » has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumptive clause). Clause: «أخرج ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle (أن)). Clause: «قد خلت القرون» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the nāʾib fāʿil. Clause: «هما يستغيثان ... » is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from والديه. Clause: «يستغيثان ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هما. Clause: «ويلك ... » has no grammatical position (parenthetical, a supplication). Clause: «آمن ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech of an implied saying; and this implied saying is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil in (يستغيثان), i.e. "saying: Woe to you! Believe". Clause: «إنّ وعد الله حقّ ... » has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumptive clause - or giving a reason). Clause: «يقول ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the implied saying. Clause: «ما هذا إلّا أساطير ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
18- (عليهم) attached to (حقّ). (في أمم) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (عليهم) [Note: Or attached to the "word" (al-qawl) meaning the punishment.]. (من قبلهم) attached to (خلت). (من الجنّ) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of خلت ...
Clause: «أولئك الذين ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذي قال ... ).
Clause: «حقّ عليهم القول ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (الذين)). Clause: «قد خلت ... » is in the position of a genitive, an adjective of أمم. Clause: «إنّهم كانوا خاسرين» has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumptive clause).
Clause: «كانوا خاسرين» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
19- (الواو) resumptive. (لكلّ) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (درجات). (ممّا) attached to an adjective of (درجات). (الواو) conjunction. (اللام) of purpose. (يوفّيهم) an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (أعمالهم) a second direct object, accusative. (الواو) a ḥāl wāw. (لا) negative.
Clause: «لكلّ درجات ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive). Clause: «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative (ما)). Clause: «يوفّيهم ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the implied particle (أن)), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يوفّيهم) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He recompensed them" ... and the implied clause is conjoined to the clause لكلّ درجات, with no grammatical position.
Clause: «هم لا يظلمون» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
Clause: «لا يظلمون» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
أفّ: a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, coined ad hoc (murtajal); some made it a maṣdar of the triliteral أفّ يؤفّ meaning "he perished and was ugly"; its pattern is فُعل with ḍamma then sukūn.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
His saying: {عَمَّآ أُنذِرُواْ}: «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, i.e. "away from their being warned," or have the sense of "that which," i.e. "away from that of which they were warned." «عن» is attached to the turning away, and «مُعْرِضون» is the khabar of the relative noun.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: its ruling has been given. «أَرُوْني» occurs after it, so it admits two aspects. The first: it is emphasis of it, because both mean "tell me." On this basis, the second object of «أَرَأَيْتُمْ» is His saying «ماذا خَلَقوا», because it is an interrogative, and the first object is His saying «ما تَدْعُون». The second aspect: it is not emphasis of it. On this basis the question is of the chapter of mutual contention (tanāzuʿ), because «أَرَأَيْتُمْ» requires a second object, and «أرُوْني» likewise, and His saying «ماذا خَلَقوا» is the thing contended over; and the question is one of applying the second verb's operation, with omission from the first. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed that «أَرَأَيْتُم» not be transitive, and made «ما تَدْعُوْن» an interrogative whose meaning is reproach. He said: "«تَدْعُوْنَ» means 'you worship.'" I say: this is the opinion of al-Akhfash, and he said so regarding His saying: {قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَآ إِلَى الصخرة} [al-Kahf: 63], and that has passed.
His saying: «من الأرض»: this is the clarification of the vagueness in His saying «ماذا خَلَقُوا».
His saying: «أَمْ لهم»: this is the disconnected «أم». And الشِّرْك means partnership.
His saying: {مِّن قَبْلِ هاذآ}: an adjective of «كتاب», i.e. "with a book sent down before this." Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it so. It is better to imply/ an absolute being, i.e. "existing before this."
His saying: «أَو أَثَارَةٍ»: the majority read «أَثارة», which is a maṣdar on the pattern fa ʿāla, like السَّماحَة, الغَواية and الضَّلالة, and its meaning is "remnant," from their saying: "the she-camel became fat on a remnant (athāra) of flesh," when she was fat, then grew lean, and a remnant of her fat remained, then she grew fat. The use of الأثارة predominantly applies to the remnant of nobility. One says: "So-and-so has an athāra," i.e. a remnant of nobility, and it is used in other senses. al-Rāʿī said:
وذاتِ أثارَةٍ أكلَتْ عليها ... نباتاً في أكِمَّتِهِ قِفارا
(And one with a remnant of flesh, on which she ate plants in its desolate hills.)
It is also said that its derivation is from أَثَر كذا, i.e. he traced it back (asnadahu). From it comes the saying of ʿUmar: "I have not sworn, whether reporting from myself or transmitting (āthiran)," i.e. attributing it to someone else. al-Aʿshā said:
4039 - أإنَّ الذي فيه تَمارَيْتُما ... بُيِّنَ للسامعِ والآثِرِ
(Indeed that over which you two disputed has been made clear to the hearer and to the transmitter.)
Other things have been said about it. ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿIkrima, among others, read «أَثَرَة» without alif, which is the singular. It is pluralised as أَثَر, like قَتَرَة and قَتَر. al-Kisāʾī read «أُثْرَة» and «إثْرَة», with ḍamma and kasra on the hamza respectively, and sukūn on the thāʾ. Qatāda and al-Sulamī read it with fatḥa and sukūn. The meaning is: "by what is transmitted and narrated," i.e. "bring me a single report that testifies to the soundness of your claim." This is by way of descending (to their level), given the knowledge that the claimant is lying. And «مِن عِلْمٍ» is an adjective of «أَثارة».
[Translator's note: the source numbers the verse of al-Aʿshā here 4039 and the verse in the next entries of this surah, 46:9, is also numbered 4039; the verse of al-Rāʿī above is unnumbered in the source. Reproduced as printed.]

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar.
His saying: {مَن لاَّ يَسْتَجِيبُ}: «مَنْ» is an indefinite described or a relative, and it is the object of «يَدْعُو».
His saying: {وَهُمْ عَن دُعَآئِهِمْ}: the two pronouns may refer back to «مَنْ» in His saying {مَن لاَّ يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ}, which are the idols, and «مَنْ» is applied to them because they treat them as they treat rational beings, or because he meant everything worshipped besides Allah and gave priority to the rational; and so he has regarded the meaning of «مَنْ», therefore it is plural in His saying «وهم», after having regarded its wording, so it is singular in His saying «يَسْتَجيب». It is also said that it refers back to «مَنْ» in His saying «ومَنْ أضَلُّ», and it was first carried according to its wording, so it is singular in His saying «يَدْعُو», then according to its meaning, so it is plural in His saying {وَهُمْ عَن دُعَآئِهِمْ غَافِلُونَ}.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {قَالَ الذين كَفَرُواْ لِلْحَقِّ}: here he put two overt nouns in the place of two pronouns; for the original is "they said of it," i.e. of the verses, but he made them overt because of the two attributes mentioned. The lām in «للحق» is for cause.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {بِدْعاً}: there are two aspects. The first: with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "possessor of novelty" (dhā bidʿ); Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. This is on the basis that al-bidʿ is a maṣdar. The second: al-bidʿ is itself an adjective on the pattern fiʿl in the sense of badīʿ, like al-khiff and al-khafīf. al-Bidʿ and al-badīʿ mean what has not been seen to have an equal, and it is from ibtidāʿ, which is invention. Quṭrub recited:
4039 - فما أنا بِدْعٌ مِنْ حوادِثَ تَعْتَري ... رجالاً عَرَتْ مِنْ بعدِ بُؤْسَى بأَسْعُدِ
(I am no novelty among the misfortunes that befall men, which befell after Buʾsā with Asʿud.)
ʿIkrima, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «بِدَعاً» with fatḥa on the dāl, the plural of بِدْعة, i.e. "you were not the possessor of novelties." al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be an adjective on the pattern fiʿal, like «دِين قِيَم» and «لحم زِيَم». The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "Sībawayh did not establish an adjective on the pattern fiʿal except «قوماً عِدَا», and «لحم زِيَم», i.e. scattered, was added against him, and it is sound. As for «قِيَم», it is a shortened form of قيام, and were it not so, its ʿayn would have remained sound as it remained in حِوَل and عِوَض. As for the saying of the Arabs «مكان سِوَىً», «ماء رِوَىً», «رجل رِضَا» and «ماء صِرَىً», these are interpreted according to the morphologists." I say: their interpretation is either as maṣdars or by shortening, like قِيَم for قيام.
Abū Ḥaywa also read, and Mujāhid, «بِدَع» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra on the dāl, which is an adjective like حَذِر.
His saying: «يُفْعَلُ»: the majority read it in the passive. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it in the active, i.e. Allah the Exalted. The apparent view is that «ما» in His saying {مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي} is interrogative, nominative through the inceptive, with what follows it as the khabar, and it suspends «أَدْري» from operating, so it stands in for its two objects. al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a relative in the accusative, meaning that it is transitive to one object, i.e. "I do not know that which Allah the Exalted does."
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا يوحى}: the majority read «يُوحَى» in the passive. Ibn ʿUmayr read it with kasra on the ḥāʾ, in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: its two objects are omitted, the implied form being "Have you considered your state, if it was such, are you not wrongdoers?"/ and the apodosis of the condition is also omitted, its implied form being "then you have done wrong"; therefore he put the verb of the condition in the past. al-Zamakhsharī implied it as "are you not wrongdoers?" The Shaykh rejected him: "Because if it were so, the fāʾ would be obligatory, since an interrogative clause, whenever it falls as the apodosis of a condition, must take the fāʾ. Then if the interrogative particle is a hamza, it precedes the fāʾ, as in: 'If you visit us, do we not honour you?'; and if it is other than that, the fāʾ precedes it, as in: 'If you visit us, do you see anything but good?'" I say: al-Zamakhsharī mentioned an implied matter by which he explained the meaning, not the i'rab.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«أَرَأَيْتُمْ» may be an alerter, so it is a word set down for questioning that does not require an object; and it may be that the clause «كان» and what it operates on stands in for its two objects." The Shaykh said: "This is contrary to what the grammarians established." I say: the verification of what they established has been given. It is also said: the apodosis of the condition is His saying «فآمَن واستكْبَرْتُمْ». It is also said: it is omitted, its implied form being "who then is in the right among us, and who in the wrong?" And it is said: "who then is more astray?"
His saying: «وكَفَرْتُمْ به»: the clause is a ḥāl, i.e. "and you have disbelieved." Some do not imply «قد» in the like of it.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ}: it may be the lām of cause, i.e. "for their sake," or it may be for conveyance. Had they followed what the address requires, they would have said "you did not precede us," but they turned to the third person and said "they did not precede us." The pronouns in «كان» and «إليه» refer back to the Qur'an, or to what the Messenger brought.
His saying: {وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُواْ}: the operator in «إذْ» is implied, i.e. "their stubbornness appeared, and His saying «فسَيقولون» results from it." «فسَيقولون» cannot operate on «إذ», because of the opposition of the two times, and also because of the fāʾ.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ موسى}: the majority read the mīm of «مِنْ» with kasra, as a preposition. It with its genitive noun is a fronted khabar. The clause is a ḥāl or a resumptive khabar.
al-Kalbī read «الكتابَ» accusative, its implied form being "and He sent down before it the Book of Moses." It was also read «ومَنْ» with fatḥa on the mīm and «كتابَ موسى» accusative, on the basis that «مَنْ» is a relative, the first object of an implied «آتَيْنا», and «كتابَ موسى» its second object, i.e. "and We gave the one before it the Book of Moses."
His saying: «إماماً ورَحْمَةً»: two ḥāls from «كتاب موسى». It is also said they are accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "We sent it down as a guide"; there is no need for it. On their being two ḥāls, they are accusative by what «مِن قبل» is accusative by, namely the settled-in-place meaning.
His saying: «لِساناً»: a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُصَدِّقٌ». It may also be a ḥāl from «كتاب», the operator being the alerting or the sense of pointing; and «عربيَّاً» is an adjective of «لساناً», and it is what justifies this inert noun falling as a ḥāl. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a direct object, governed by «مُصَدِّقٌ». On this basis the pointing is to something other than the Qur'an, because by "Arabic tongue" is meant the Qur'an, which is contrary to the apparent view. It is also said to be with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "confirming the possessor of an Arabic tongue," who is the Prophet ﷺ. It is also said to be with removal of the preposition, i.e. "in a tongue," which is weak.
His saying: «ليُنْذِرَ»: attached to «مصدِّق». And «بُشْرَى» is conjoined to its position, its implied form being "for warning and for glad tidings," and since the cause and the effect differ, the operator reaches it by the lām [this applies to whoever read with the second-person tāʾ. As for whoever read with the third-person yāʾ, and that was given earlier in Yā Sīn, the two are the same. It is also said: «بُشْرى»] is conjoined to the wording of «لتنذِرَ», i.e. it is genitive only. It is also said it is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it is glad tidings." It is also said that it is conjoined to «مُصَدِّقٌ». And it is said it is accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "and give glad tidings." The Shaykh related the accusative aspect, conjunction upon the position of «لتنذِرَ», from al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ. Then he said: "This is not sound according to the sound view among the grammarians' schools, because they stipulate for carrying onto the position that it be by right of originality, and that the place have a secure basis, and here the position is not by right of originality, since the original in the mafʿūl lahu is the genitive, and the accusative arises from it, but when it became frequent, with the stipulated conditions, the verb reached it and made it accusative." End quotation.
His saying "the original in the mafʿūl lahu is the genitive by the particle" is not conceded, by the proof of the grammarians' saying that it is accusative on conditions which they mentioned. Then they say: "and it may be made genitive with a lām"; so their saying "it may" is apparently a sign that it is a secondary form, not an original.
And «للمُحْسِنين» is attached to «بُشْرَى» or to an omitted element as an adjective of it.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَلاَ خَوْفٌ}: the fāʾ is redundant in the khabar of the relative noun, because of the sense of condition in it, and «إنَّ» does not prevent that because the sense of the inceptive remains, unlike «ليت», «لعلَّ» and «كأن».

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {خَالِدِينَ}: accusative as a ḥāl. And «جزاءً» is accusative as a maṣdar, either through an implied operator, i.e. "they are recompensed a recompense," or through what preceded, because the meaning of «أولئك أصحاب الجنة» is the meaning of "We recompensed them with that."

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {إِحْسَاناً}: the Kufans read «إحْساناً» and the rest of the seven read «حُسْناً» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the sīn. On the first reading, «إحساناً» is accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "We enjoined him to do good to them both, a doing of good." It is also said: rather it is a direct object by containing in «وصَّيْنا» the sense of "We obliged," so it is a second object. It is also said: rather it is accusative as a direct object, i.e. "We enjoined him concerning them kindness from us toward them." It is also said: it is accusative as a maṣdar, because the meaning of «وصَّيْنا» is "We did good," so it is a pure maṣdar. And the second object / is what is genitive through the bāʾ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is attached either to «وَصَّيْنا» or to «إحساناً»." The Shaykh rejected this second: it is an interpreted maṣdar, so what it governs cannot precede it; and «أَحْسَنَ» is not made transitive with the bāʾ, only with the lām; you do not say "aḥsantu bi-Zayd" in the sense of the arrival of goodness to him. Some have rejected this with His saying: {وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بي إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِي} [Yūsuf: 100]; and it is said that it is in a different sense. Some implied: "We enjoined man concerning his parents, as one possessed of good conduct," meaning it is a ḥāl. As for «حُسْناً», what was said under «إحسان» is said of it.
ʿĪsā and al-Sulamī read «حَسَناً» with fatḥa on both. The meaning of the two readings was given in al-Baqara and in Luqmān.
His saying: «كُرْهاً»: the disagreement about it has been given in al-Nisāʾ. And in it (the question whether) they are of one meaning or not. [Translator's note: the source wording here is «وله هما بمعنىً واحد أم لا؟»; translated as printed, and it appears to be garbled.] Abū Ḥātim said: "الكَرْه with fatḥa is not good, because with fatḥa it means force and compulsion." What he said is not heeded, given the mutawātir status of this reading. Its accusative is either as a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "possessing reluctance," or as an adjective of an implied maṣdar, i.e. "a reluctant bearing."
His saying: «وحَمْلُه», i.e. the period of his bearing. The majority read «فِصالُه», a maṣdar of فاصَلَ, as if the mother separated from him and he from her. al-Jaḥdarī, al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read «فَصْلُه». It is said: الفَصْل and الفِصال mean the same, like الفَطْم and الفِطام, and القَطْف and القِطاف. Had «ثلاثين» been made accusative as an adverbial occurring in the place of the khabar, it would have been permitted, and it is the original. This is when we do not imply a muḍāf; if we do, i.e. "the period of his bearing," that is not permitted and the nominative is required, because the khabar and what is reported about are coextensive.
His saying: {حتى إِذَا بَلَغَ}: an omitted clause is needed for which «حتى» is the end-point, i.e. "he lived and his life continued until, when…"
His saying: «أربعين»: i.e. its completion, so «أربعين» is a direct object.
His saying: {وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذريتي}: أَصْلَحَ is transitive by itself, per His saying: {وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 90]; it is transitivised with «في» only because it contains the sense of "be kind to me in my offspring," or because he made the offspring a container of righteousness, like the saying:
4040 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . يَجْرَحُ في عَراقيبها نَصْلي
(… my blade wounds in their hamstrings.)

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {نَتَقَبَّلُ}: the two companions (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read «نَتَقَبَّلُ» with fatḥa on the nūn, active, with «أَحْسَنَ» accusative as direct object, and likewise «ونتجاوَزُ». The others read both passive, with «أحسنُ» nominative as it stands in for the agent, and with a yāʾ with ḍamma in place of the nūn in both verbs. al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and ʿĪsā read with the yāʾ (below), the agent being Allah the Exalted.
His saying: {في أَصْحَابِ الجنة}: several aspects. The first, which is the apparent one: it is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "being among the people of Paradise," like your saying "the emir honoured me among his companions," i.e. among their number. The second: «في» is in the sense of «مع». The third: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are among the people of Paradise."
His saying: «وَعْدَ الصدقِ»: an emphatic maṣdar of the content of the preceding clause, because His saying {أولئك الذين نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ} is in the sense of a promise.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {أُفٍّ}: the discussion of «أُفّ» has been given in full, and «لكما» is a clarification, i.e. the saying "uff" is for you two, like {هَيْتَ} [Yūsuf: 23].
His saying: «أَتَعِدانِني»: the majority read it with two nūns with kasra: the first for the nominative and the second for protection (wiqāya); Hishām assimilated them, and Nāfiʿ in one transmission read with a single nūn. This is likened to His saying: {تأمروني أَعْبُدُ} [al-Zumar: 64]. al-Ḥasan, Shayba, Abū Jaʿfar and ʿAbd al-Wārith from Abū ʿAmr read the first nūn with fatḥa, as if they fled from the succession of two kasra-bearing like letters followed by a yāʾ. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is an irregular dialect, the fatḥa of the dual nūn." I say: if he means the dual nūn in nouns, as in the saying:
4041 - على أَحْوَذِيَّيْنَ اسْتَقَلَّتْ. . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(On two swift ones she rose… )
that is not this. If he means in the verb, that has not been established as a dialect, and the fatḥa here is only for what I mentioned.
His saying: «أَنْ أُخْرَجَ»: it is what is promised, so one may imply the bāʾ before «أَنْ» or not imply it.
His saying: «وقد خَلَتْ»: a circumstantial clause. Likewise {وَهُمَا يَسْتَغثِيَانِ الله}, i.e. "they ask Allah." اسْتَغاثَ is transitive by itself at times and with the bāʾ at others, although Ibn Mālik claimed it is transitive by itself only, and faulted the grammarians' "mustaghāth bihi." I say: but it has not occurred in the Qur'an except transitive by itself: {إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ} [al-Anfāl: 9], {فاستغاثه الذي} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 15], {وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُواْ يُغَاثُواْ} [al-Kahf: 29]. His saying: «وَيْلَكَ»: accusative as a maṣdar through a verb that meets it in meaning, not in derivation. Likewise: وَيْحَه, وَيْسَه and وَيْبَه. Or as a direct object, with the implied form "Allah impose upon you your woe." On both implications the clause is governed by an implied saying, i.e. "they say: woe to you, believe!" And the saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "they implore Allah, saying that."
His saying: {إِنَّ وَعْدَ الله حَقٌّ}: the majority read «إنَّ» with kasra, / as resumptive or causal. ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid and al-Aʿraj read it with fatḥa, governed by «آمِنْ» with the bāʾ omitted, i.e. "believe that the promise of Allah is true."

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {في أُمَمٍ}: like His saying: {في أَصْحَابِ الجنة} [al-Aḥqāf: 16].

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ}: what it justifies is omitted, its implied form being "He recompensed them with that." Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Hishām read with the yāʾ (below). The rest of the seven read with the nūn. al-Sulamī read with the tāʾ (above), ascribing the full payment to the degrees figuratively.
His saying: {وَهُمْ لاَ يُظْلَمُونَ}: either resumptive or an emphatic ḥāl.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ}: «اليومَ» is accusative through an implied saying, i.e. "it is said to them: you squandered, on the day of their being displayed." al-Zamakhsharī made this like "I displayed the she-camel to the water trough," so it would be an inversion (qalb). The Shaykh rejected him: it is a necessity (of poetry). Also, displaying is a relative matter, so its attribution to the she-camel and to the trough are both sound. The discussion of inversion has been given, and that there are three schools about it.
His saying: «أَذْهَبْتُم»: Ibn Kathīr read «أَأَذْهَبْتُمْ» with two hamzas, the first lightened and the second eased between the two (bayna bayna), without inserting an alif between them, and this is on his principle in {أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 6] and the like. Ibn ʿĀmir also read with two hamzas, but his two transmitters differed from him: Hishām eased the second and also lightened it, and inserted an alif in both aspects, though this is not on his principle, for he is of the people of taḥqīq. Ibn Dhakwān read with taḥqīq only, without inserting an alif. The others read with a single hamza, which is either a statement or an interrogative whose particle was dropped because of an indication to it; and the interrogative means rebuke and reproach.
His saying: «في حياتِكم»: it may be attached to «أَذْهَبْتُمْ», and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «طيباتكم».

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {إِذْ أَنذَرَ}: a badal of inclusion from «أَخا»; its verification has been given. الأَحْقاف is the plural of حِقْف, which is the long, curved sand dune; from it comes "the crescent became bent" (iḥqawqafa). Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4042 - فلمَّا أَجَزْنا ساحةَ الحيِّ وانتحى ... بنا بَطْنُ حِقْفٍ ذي قِفافٍ عَقَنْقَلِ
(When we passed the tribe's encampment, and the heart of a dune with ridges and tangled sands turned us aside.)
His saying: «وقد خَلَتْ»: it may be a ḥāl from the agent or from the object, the link being the wāw. النُّذُر is the plural of نَذير. It may also be parenthetical between «أَنْذَرَ» and {أَلاَّ تعبدوا}, i.e. "he warned them that they not…"

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضاً}: there are two sayings about the hāʾ of «رَأَوْه». The first: it refers back to «ما تَعِدُنا». The second: it is a vague pronoun which «عارضاً» explains, either as tamyīz or as ḥāl; al-Zamakhsharī said both. The Shaykh rejected him: the tamyīz that explains a pronoun is restricted to the chapter of «رُبَّ» and «نِعْمَ» and «بِئْس», and a ḥāl is not known to clarify a pronoun before it, and the grammarians do not know that.
His saying: «مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهم»: an adjective of «عارِضاً», and its annexation is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa), and therefore it was permissible for it to be an adjective of an indefinite; likewise «مُمْطِرُنا» occurs as an adjective of «عارِض». Similar is:
4043 - يا رُبَّ غابِطِنا لو كان يَطْلُبُكُمْ ... لاقى مباعَدَةً منكم وحِرْمانا
(O many an envier of us who, had he sought you, would have met distance and deprivation from you.)
العارِض is the cloud that spans across the sky. He said:
4044 - يا مَنْ رَأَى عارِضاً أَرِقْتُ له ... بين ذراعَيْ وجَبْهَةِ الأَسَدِ
(O you who saw a cloud for which I lay awake, between the two arms and the brow of the Lion.)
It has been given earlier that أَوْدِيَة is the plural of «وادٍ», and that the pattern afʿila is irregular as a plural of fāʿil in some words: such as وادٍ and أَوْدِيَة, نادٍ and أَنْدِية, جائِز and أَجْوِزة.
His saying: «ريحٌ»: it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a wind," or a badal from «هو». «ما استُعْجِلْتُمْ» was also read in the passive. «وفيها عذابٌ» is an adjective of «ريحٌ», and likewise «تُدَمِّرُ». {يَدْمُرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ} was also read with yāʾ (below), sukūn on the dāl and ḍamma on the mīm, with «كلُّ» nominative as the agent, i.e. "everything perishes." Zayd ibn ʿAlī likewise, except with tāʾ (above) and «كلَّ» accusative, the agent being the pronoun of the wind; on this the triliteral دَمَّر is both intransitive and transitive.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {فَأْصْبَحُواْ لاَ يرى إِلاَّ مَسَاكِنُهُمْ}: Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read «لا يُرَى» with ḍamma on the yāʾ (below), passive, with «مَسَاكنُهم» nominative as it stands in for the agent. The rest of the seven read with the second-person tāʾ with fatḥa, «مَساكنَهم» accusative as direct object. al-Jaḥdarī, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-Sulamī and Abū Rajāʾ read with ḍamma on the tāʾ (above), passive, «مساكنُهم» nominative as it stands in for the agent, except that this is not permitted according to the majority, I mean when the separator is «إلاَّ», for the attachment of the feminine mark to the verb is prevented except in necessity, as in the saying: /
4045 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وما بَقِيَتْ إلاَّ الضلوعُ الجراشِعُ
(… and nothing remained except the broad-chested ribs.)
and the saying of another:
4046 - كأنه جَمَلٌ هَمٌّ وما بَقِيَتْ ... إلاَّ النَّحِيزةُ والألواحُ والعَصَبُ
(As if he were a worn-out camel, and nothing remained except the nature, the planks (bones) and the sinews.)
ʿĪsā al-Hamdānī read «لا يُرى» with yāʾ (below), passive, «مَسْكَنُهم» singular. Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read with the second-person tāʾ, «مَسْكَنَهم» also singular and accusative; the singular was made to suffice for the plural.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {مَآ إِن مَّكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ}: «ما» is a relative or an indefinite described. There are three aspects regarding «إنْ»: conditional, with its apodosis omitted, and the conditional clause is the ṣila of «ما», the implied form being "in that in which, if We established you, you transgressed." The second: it is redundant, in likening the relative «ما» to the negative «ما» and the temporal «ما». This is like the saying:
4047 - يُرَجِّي المرءُ ما إنْ لا يَراهُ ... وتَعرِضُ دونَ أَدْناه الخُطوبُ
(A man hopes for what he may not see, and calamities intervene before the nearest of it.)
The third, which is the sound one: it is negative, in the sense: "We established them in that in which We did not establish you, of strength, stature and breadth of provisions." The saying of the Exalted in several places indicates it: {كانوا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً} [al-Rūm: 9] and the like. He departed from the word negative «ما» to «إنْ» only out of dislike of the meeting of two identical words. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Abū l-Ṭayyib (al-Mutanabbī) made it insipid in his saying:
4048 - لَعَمْرُك ما ما بان منك لِضاربٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(By your life, what [what] became manifest from you to a striker… )
What would it have harmed him had he followed the sweetness of the wording of the revelation and said «ما إنْ بانَ منك»?"
His saying: «فما أَغْنى»: «ما» may be negation, which is the apparent view, or an interrogative of affirmation. The Shaykh considered the latter unlikely because of His saying «مِنْ شيء». He said: "Because the implied form would become 'what thing availed them in the slightest,' so «مِنْ» would be added in the affirmative, which is not permitted on the sound view." I say: they said that its addition is permitted in the non-affirmative, and they explained the non-affirmative as negation, prohibition and interrogation, and this is an interrogative.
His saying: «إذ كانوا»: governed by «أَغْنى», and it carries a tinge of the meaning of cause, i.e. "because they were denying."

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {قُرْبَاناً آلِهَةَ}: four aspects. The most probable: the first object of «اتَّخذوا» is omitted, being the returning pronoun of the relative; «قُرْباناً» is accusative as a ḥāl, and «آلهةً» is the second object of the taking. The implied form: "Why did those whom they took as gods, as a means of drawing near by them, not help them?" The second: the first object is omitted, as stated, «قُرْباناً» is the second object and «آلهةً» a badal from it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Ḥūfī and Abū l-Baqāʾ inclined to it. But al-Zamakhsharī prevented this aspect, saying: "because of corruption of the meaning," and did not make clear the aspect of the corruption. The Shaykh said: "It appears that the meaning is sound on that i'rab." I say: the aspect of the corruption, and Allah knows best, is that qurbān is a name for what is used to draw near to the deity; so if we made it a second object, and «آلهةً» a badal from it, it would follow that the thing used for drawing near is gods, whereas the supposition is that it is other than the gods, rather it is something by which one draws near to them, so it is other than them; so how could the gods be a badal for it? This is not permitted. The third: «قُرْباناً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; the Shaykh attributed it to al-Ḥūfī. I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ also took this view, and on this «آلهةً» is a second object and the first is omitted as stated. The fourth: that it is a maṣdar; Makkī related it. Were it not that he mentioned a second aspect, the mafʿūl li-ajlihi, I would have interpreted his statement as meaning by "maṣdar" the mafʿūl li-ajlihi, given the remoteness of the sense of maṣdar.
His saying: «إفْكُهم»: the majority read it with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the fāʾ, a maṣdar of أَفَكَ يَأْفِك إفْكاً, i.e. "their lying." Ibn ʿAbbās read it with fatḥa, which is also a maṣdar of it. Ibn ʿAbbās also, ʿIkrima and al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read «أَفَكَهُمْ» with three fatḥas, a past verb, i.e. "he turned them away." Abū ʿIyāḍ and ʿIkrima also read likewise except with shadda on the fāʾ for multiplication. Ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn ʿAbbās also read «آفَكَهم» with elongation, also a past verb, and it may be on the pattern fāʿala, in which case the hamza is original, or on the pattern afʿala, in which case the hamza is added and the second is a substitute for a hamza. If we say it is afʿala, its hamza may be for transitivity, or afʿala may be in the sense of the bare form. Ibn ʿAbbās also read «آفِكُهم» with elongation, kasra on the fāʾ and nominative kāf, making it an active participle in the sense of "the one who turns them away." «أَفَكُهم» was also read with two fatḥas and nominative kāf, as a maṣdar of أَفَكَ too, so it would have three maṣdars: الأَفْك, الإِفْك (with fatḥa and with kasra on the hamza, with sukūn on the fāʾ) and with fatḥa on the hamza and the fāʾ. Abū l-Baqāʾ added that «آفَكُهم» was read with elongation, fatḥa on the fāʾ and nominative kāf. He said: "in the sense of 'the greatest liar among them'," making it an elative.
His saying: {وَمَا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ}: / «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, which is better so that it is conjoined to its like, or have the sense of "that which," with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "they used to fabricate." The maṣdar in His saying «إفْكُهم» may be annexed to the agent in the sense of "their lying," or to the object in the sense of "their being turned away."

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {وَإِذْ صَرَفْنَآ}: accusative through an implied "remember." «صَرَّفْنا» with shadda was also read, for multiplication. «من الجنِّ» is an adjective of «نَفَراً», and it may be attached to «صَرَفْنا», with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the range.
His saying: «يَسْتَمِعُون»: also an adjective of «نَفَراً», or a ḥāl because of its being specified by the adjective, if we say that «مِنَ الجنِّ» is an adjective of it; and he regarded the meaning of «النَّفر», so he returned the pronoun to it in the plural; had he regarded its wording and said «يَسْتمع», it would have been permissible.
His saying: «فلَمَّا حَضَرُوْه»: the hāʾ may be for the Qur'an, which is the apparent view, or for the Messenger, peace be upon him, in which case there is an iltifāt (shift of person) in the speech from His saying «إليك» to the third person in His saying «حَضَرُوه».
His saying: «قُضِي»: the majority read it passive, i.e. the recitation of the Qur'an was finished, which supports the hāʾ of «حَضَروه» referring to the Qur'an. Abū Mijlaz and Ḥabīb ibn ʿAbd Allāh read «قَضَى» active, i.e. the Messenger completed his recitation, and this supports its referring to the Messenger, peace be upon him.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ}: it may be partitive, or redundant according to those who hold that view.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {وَلَمْ يَعْيَ}: the majority read it with sukūn on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the yāʾ, the imperfect of عَيِيَ (with kasra) يَعْيا (with fatḥa); when the jussive particle entered, the alif was dropped. al-Ḥasan read «يَعِيْ» with kasra on the ʿayn and sukūn on the yāʾ. They said: its original is عَيِيَ with kasra; he turned the kasra into fatḥa in the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ, so it became «عَيا», as they said of بَقِيَ: بَقَا. When the past was built on faʿala with fatḥa, its imperfect came on yafʿilu with kasra, so it became يَعْيِي like يَرْمي. When the jussive entered, the second yāʾ was dropped, so it became «لم يَعْيِ» with a sukūn ʿayn and a kasra yāʾ; then the vowel of the yāʾ was moved to the ʿayn, so the word became as you see. It has already been given that عَيِيَ and حَيِيَ have two dialectal forms: unassimilated and assimilated. As for «حِيِي», it was given in al-Anfāl. And عَيَّ is as in the saying:
4049 - عَيُّوا بأَمْرِهِمُ كما ... عَيَّتْ ببَيْضَتِها الحمَامَهْ
(They were at a loss over their affair, as the dove is at a loss over its egg.)
And العِيّ is the failure to find the way to a direction. From it comes العِيّ in speech, and "he was at a loss about the matter" when he did not find its way.
His saying: «بقادرٍ»: the bāʾ is redundant. What makes its redundancy good is that the speech has the force of "Is Allah not able?"; al-Zajjāj analogised "I did not think anyone was standing (bi-qāʾim)" to it, but the sound view is to withhold judgement. ʿĪsā, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Jaḥdarī read «يَقْدِرُ», the imperfect of قَدَرَ, and the orthography admits it. His saying «بلى» is an affirmation of what the speech contains of negation in His saying {أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ}.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {أَلَيْسَ هذا}: governed by an implied saying which is a ḥāl, as given for its parallel earlier.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {فاصبر}: the fāʾ conjoins this clause to what preceded, and the causal sense in it is apparent.
His saying: «من الرسُل»: it may be partitive, and on that the messengers are those of resolve and those not of resolve. It may be explicative, and on that all of them are of resolve.
His saying: «بلاغٌ»: the majority read it nominative. There are two aspects. The first: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; some implied "that hour is a delivery (of the message)," from the indication of His saying {إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِّن نَّهَارٍ}. It is also said that the implied form is "this," i.e. the Qur'an and the law, "is a delivery." The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is His saying «لهم», which occurs after His saying «ولا تَسْتَعْجِلْ», i.e. "for them is a delivery," so one stops at «فلا تَسْتعجل». This is very weak because of the separation by the comparative clause, since the apparent view is that «لهم» is attached to the seeking haste, so it resembles making ready and cutting off. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read «بلاغاً» accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "he delivered a delivery," and the reading of Abū Mijlaz «بَلِّغْ» as an imperative supports it. He also read «بَلَغَ» as a past verb.
From the speech of Makkī it is taken that its accusative as an adjective of «ساعةً» is permitted, for he said: "Were «بلاغاً» to be read accusative as a maṣdar or as an adjective of «ساعةً», it would be permitted." I say: it has been read so, and it seems he did not come across that.
al-Ḥasan also read «بلاغ» genitive. It was derived as an adjective of «نهار» with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from a day of delivery," or the time was described by delivery for exaggeration.
His saying: «يُهْلَكُ»: the majority read it passive. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يَهْلِك» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the lām, active. From him also is fatḥa on the lām, which is a dialect; the past is هلِكَ with kasra. Ibn Jinnī said: "All of these are disfavoured." Zayd ibn Thābit read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the lām, / the agent being Allah the Exalted, «القومَ الفاسقين» accusative as direct object. And «نُهْلك» with nūn and «القوم» accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ إِحْسَانًا حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهًا وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهًا وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصَالُهُ ثَلَاثُونَ شَهْرًا حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً قَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَى وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي إِنِّي تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حُسْنًا): it is the second mafʿūl (object) of وَصَّى, and the meaning is: "We obliged him to (do) good" (أَلْزَمْنَاهُ حُسْنًا). [Translator's note: the verse as quoted above reads إِحْسَانًا; the author comments first on the reading حُسْنًا.]
It is also said that the implied wording is: "a bequest possessing goodness" (وَصِيَّةً ذَاتِ حُسْنٍ). It is also read حَسَنًا with two fatḥas, i.e. "a good enjoining" (إِيصَاءً حَسَنًا), or "We obliged him to a good deed" (أَلْزَمْنَاهُ فِعْلًا حَسَنًا).
It is also read إِحْسَانًا, i.e. "We obliged him to kindness" (أَلْزَمْنَاهُ إِحْسَانًا). And (كُرْهًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being unwilling" (كَارِهَةً).
(وَحَمْلُهُ), i.e. "and the period of his bearing" (وَمُدَّةُ حَمْلِهِ), (وَفِصَالُهُ ثَلَاثُونَ). And (أَرْبَعِينَ) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of بَلَغَ, i.e. "he reached the completion of forty".
And {فِي ذريتي}: فِي here is adverbial (ẓarf), i.e. "place righteousness in them".

ukberi-tibyan:16-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ مَا عَمِلُوا وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَنْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ فِي أَصْحَابِ الْجَنَّةِ وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِي كَانُوا يُوعَدُونَ (١٦) وَالَّذِي قَالَ لِوَالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَكُمَا أَتَعِدَانِنِي أَنْ أُخْرَجَ وَقَدْ خَلَتِ الْقُرُونُ مِنْ قَبْلِي وَهُمَا يَسْتَغِيثَانِ اللَّهَ وَيْلَكَ آمِنْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ فَيَقُولُ مَا هَذَا إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (١٧) أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلُ فِي أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا خَاسِرِينَ (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي أَصْحَابِ الْجَنَّةِ): i.e. they are counted among them, so it is in the position of the nominative. And (وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of وَعَدَ, the speech having indicated it. And (أُفٍّ) has been discussed in Subḥān [Translator's note: i.e. Sūrat al-Isrāʾ], and «لَكُمَا» is for clarification (tabyīn).
(أَتَعِدَانِنِي) with kasra on the first nūn. It has also been read with fatḥa on it, which is an anomalous (shādhdh) dialect in giving fatḥa to the nūn of the dual; it became somewhat acceptable here because of the many kasras.
And (أَنْ أُخْرَجَ), i.e. "of being brought out" (بِأَنْ أُخْرَجَ). It is also said that the bāʾ is not needed; its parallel has already passed.
(وَهُمَا يَسْتَغِيثَانِ اللَّهَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «اللَّهَ», glorified is He, is the mafʿūl (object) of يَسْتَغِيثَانِ, because it carries the meaning of "they ask". And (وَيْلَكَ) is a maṣdar whose verb is not used. It is also said that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "Allah has fastened your woe upon you" (أَلْزَمَكَ اللَّهُ وَيْلَكَ).
And (فِي أُمَمٍ), i.e. counted among them; and مِنْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَلَتْ».

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِكُلٍّ دَرَجَاتٌ مِمَّا عَمِلُوا وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ): what the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to is omitted, i.e. "and so that He may pay them in full for their deeds" — i.e. the recompense of their deeds — "He requited them", or "He punished them".

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّبَاتِكُمْ فِي حَيَاتِكُمُ الدُّنْيَا وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهَا فَالْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذَابَ الْهُونِ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَبِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ): i.e. "remember"; or the implied wording is: "and on the day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire, it will be said to them: أَذْهَبْتُمْ"; so it is an adverb (ẓarf) for the omitted element.

ukberi-tibyan:24-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضًا مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قَالُوا هَذَا عَارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنَا بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ رِيحٌ فِيهَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (٢٤) تُدَمِّرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ بِأَمْرِ رَبِّهَا فَأَصْبَحُوا لَا يُرَى إِلَّا مَسَاكِنُهُمْ كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الْقَوْمَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ): the annexation (iḍāfa) is in the sense of separation, i.e. مُسْتَقْبِلًا أَوْدِيَتَهُمْ ("facing their valleys"), and it is a naʿt (adjective) of عَارِض. And (مُمْطِرُنَا), i.e. مُمْطِرٌ إِيَّانَا ("bringing rain to us"), so it too is indefinite. In the speech there is an omission, i.e. "it is not as you supposed; rather it is what you sought to hasten". And (رِيحٌ) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a wind"; or it is a badal (substitute) for (مَا).
And (تُدَمِّرُ) is a naʿt of the wind.
And (لَا تَرَى) with tāʾ, as an address, and with the agent named (active voice).
And (مَسَاكِنُهُمْ) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
It is also read with the agent left unnamed, with yāʾ, i.e. لَا يُرَى إِلَّا مَسَاكِنُهُمْ, in the nominative; it is what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). It is also read with tāʾ with the agent left unnamed, and this is weak.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِيمَا إِنْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ سَمْعًا وَأَبْصَارًا وَأَفْئِدَةً فَمَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَلَا أَبْصَارُهُمْ وَلَا أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِذْ كَانُوا يَجْحَدُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَحَاقَ بِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِيمَا إِنْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ): «مَا» means "that which" (al-ladhī), or it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. And «إِنْ» has the meaning of the negating مَا. It is also said that «إِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "in that in which We established you".

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَوْلَا نَصَرَهُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قُرْبَانًا آلِهَةً بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ وَذَلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُرْبَانًا): it is the mafʿūl (object) of اتَّخَذُوا, and «آلِهَةً» is a badal (substitute) for it.
It is also said that «قُرْبَانًا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and «آلِهَةً» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the implied wording is: "in order to draw near (to Allah) by them".
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَذَلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ): it is read with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the fāʾ, i.e. "that is their lie".
It is also read with fatḥa on the hamza, as the maṣdar of أَفَكَ, i.e. "he turned (someone) away"; the maṣdar is annexed to the agent or to the object. It has also been read «أَفَكَهُمْ» in the form of the past verb, i.e. "it turned them away". It is also read so with shadda. It has also been read «آفَكَهُمْ» with a long vowel, i.e. "it made them liars". It has also been read «آفِكُهُمْ», with kasra on the fāʾ, a long vowel and ḍamma on the kāf, i.e. "that which turns them away". (وَمَا كَانُوا) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to إِفْكِهِمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ صَرَفْنَا إِلَيْكَ نَفَرًا مِنَ الْجِنِّ يَسْتَمِعُونَ الْقُرْآنَ فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قَالُوا أَنْصِتُوا فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ وَلَّوْا إِلَى قَوْمِهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ (٢٩))
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ صَرَفْنَا): i.e. "and remember when". And (يَسْتَمِعُونَ) is a naʿt (adjective) of نَفَر; since النَّفَر is a group, He said يَسْتَمِعُونَ; had He, Exalted is He, said «يَسْتَمِعُ», it would have been permissible, construing it according to the wording.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتَى بَلَى إِنَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَمْ يَعْيَ): the good dialect is عَيِيَ يَعِيَا [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the usual form is يَعْيَا], though عَيَّ يَعِيُّ has also occurred.
The bāʾ in (بِقَادِرٍ) is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ»; that is permissible because it is connected with the negation; were it not for that, it would not be permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاصْبِرْ كَمَا صَبَرَ أُولُو الْعَزْمِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ وَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلْ لَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ مَا يُوعَدُونَ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا سَاعَةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ بَلَاغٌ فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَاعَةً): an adverb (ẓarf) for يَلْبَثُوا.
And (بَلَاغٌ), i.e. "this is a proclamation" (هُوَ بَلَاغٌ). It is also read بَلَاغًا, i.e. "proclaim a proclamation" (بَلِّغْ بَلَاغًا).
It is also read in the genitive, i.e. "of a day possessing a proclamation" (مِنْ نَهَارٍ ذِي بَلَاغٍ). It is also read «بَلِّغْ» as an imperative. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كَانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَى مِثْلِهِ فَآمَنَ وَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ (١٠)).
His saying (وَكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ): i.e. "while you have disbelieved", so it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
As for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), it is omitted, its implied form being "are you not wrongdoers?".
It is also possible that the wāw is a conjunction joining it to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْ كَانَ خَيْرًا مَا سَبَقُونَا إِلَيْهِ وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا بِهِ فَسَيَقُولُونَ هَذَا إِفْكٌ قَدِيمٌ (١١)).
His saying (وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا بِهِ): what governs «إِذْ» is omitted, i.e. "when they were not guided, their obstinacy became manifest".

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ مُوسَى إِمَامًا وَرَحْمَةً وَهَذَا كِتَابٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِسَانًا عَرَبِيًّا لِيُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَبُشْرَى لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ (١٢)).
His saying (إِمَامًا وَرَحْمَةً): two ḥāls (circumstantials) of «كِتَابُ مُوسَى».
His saying (لِسَانًا): it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in مُصَدِّقٌ, or a ḥāl of كِتَابٌ because it has been qualified.
It may also be the object of مُصَدِّقٌ, i.e. "this Book confirms the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ".
(وَبُشْرَى) is conjoined to the position of «لِيُنْذِرَ».

ukberi-tibyan:13-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقَامُوا فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (١٣) أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (١٤)).
His saying (فَلَا خَوْفٌ): the fāʾ entered the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» because of the indefiniteness (ibhām) in «الَّذِينَ», and because the meaning of the mubtadaʾ (subject) remains [after إِنَّ], unlike with لَيْتَ and لَعَلَّ. And (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ».
And (جَزَاءً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of a verb indicated by the speech, i.e. "they were requited with a requital"; or it is in the position of a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ مَا تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ ائْتُونِي بِكِتَابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ هَذَا أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (٤)).
His saying (مِنْ قَبْلِ هَذَا): in the position of the genitive, i.e. "with a Book sent down before this".
(أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ): with alif, i.e. "a remnant"; and أَثَرَةٍ, with fatḥa on the thāʾ and with sukūn (أَثْرَةٍ), i.e. what is transmitted (yuʾthar), i.e. narrated.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ يَدْعُو مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَنْ لَا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ وَهُمْ عَنْ دُعَائِهِمْ غَافِلُونَ (٥)).
His saying (مَنْ لَا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ): «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative by يَدْعُو; it is a qualified indefinite noun (nakira mawṣūfa), or has the sense of الَّذِي (the one who).

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ مَا كُنْتُ بِدْعًا مِنَ الرُّسُلِ وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ وَمَا أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (٩)).
His saying (مَا كُنْتُ بِدْعًا): i.e. "one bringing a novelty" (ذَا بِدْعٍ); one says أَمْرُهُمْ بِدْعٌ, i.e. "newly invented".
It may also be an adjective, i.e. "I was not the first to claim messengership".
It is also read with fatḥa on the dāl (بِدَعًا), and it is the plural of بِدْعَةٌ, i.e. "one bringing novelties" (ذَا بِدَعٍ).

zajjaj:3-3.t:
Sūrat al-Aḥqāf
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما خَلَقْنا السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُما إلا بِالحَقِّ وأجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾: It has come in the exegesis: "We created them only for the truth," that is, for the establishment of the truth; and it may have the meaning: "The heavens and the earth stand only by the truth." And His saying right after this: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَمّا أُنْذِرُوا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾, that is, they turned away after the proof had been established for them by Allah's creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
Then He called them to the proof, for their sake, of the falsity of worshipping the idols they worship, and said: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ ما تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾. It is also read "أرَيْتُمْ", without alif. "ما تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ": "what you call upon as a god besides Allah." ﴿أرُونِي ماذا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الأرْضِ أمْ لَهم شِرْكٌ في السَّماواتِ﴾: that is, in the creation of the heavens; that is, so that for that reason you have made them partners in the worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
﴿ائْتُونِي بِكِتابٍ مِن قَبْلِ هَذا﴾: that is, "Bring me a book sent down containing proof of what you claim." ﴿أوْ أثارَةٍ مِن عِلْمٍ﴾: It is also read "أوْ أثَرَةٍ مِن عِلْمٍ", and it has been read "أوْ أثْرَةٍ مِن عِلْمٍ", with sukūn on the thāʾ. Its meaning, when one says "أثارَةٍ", is "a mark of knowledge"; it may also have the meaning "a remnant of knowledge"; and it may have the meaning "what is transmitted (yuʾthar) of knowledge."

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن أضَلُّ مِمَّنْ يَدْعُو مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ مَن لا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ وهم عَنْ دُعائِهِمْ غافِلُونَ﴾: that is, who is more astray than one who worships other than Allah?! Everything Allah has created is a proof of His oneness; so who is more astray than one who worships a stone that does not answer him? He said "وَمَن" and He said "وَهم", though it refers to what is not rational, because those who worshipped them treated them as things that discern, so they were addressed in accordance with their own way of speaking, as they said: ﴿ما نَعْبُدُهم إلا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إلى اللَّهِ زُلْفى﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]. Had it been "ما", that would have been good, as He said: ﴿لِمَ تَعْبُدُ ما لا يَسْمَعُ ولا يُبْصِرُ﴾ [Maryam: 42].

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذا حُشِرَ النّاسُ كانُوا لَهم أعْداءً وكانُوا بِعِبادَتِهِمْ كافِرِينَ﴾: that is, the idols will disown their worship of them, saying: "We did not call them to worship us."

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ فَلا تَمْلِكُونَ لِي مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا هو أعْلَمُ بِما تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾: that is, you have no power at all against Allah; that is, Allah has the greater power over His servants. ﴿كَفى بِهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكُمْ﴾: that is, He suffices as a witness; "بِهِ" is in the position of the nominative. And His saying in this place: ﴿وَهُوَ الغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾: its meaning is that whoever commits such of the great major sins as you have committed — fabricating lies against Allah, Majestic, Mighty and Exalted is He — and then repents, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful to him.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ ما كُنْتُ بِدْعًا مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾: that is, I was not the first to be sent; many messengers were sent before me.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما أدْرِي ما يُفْعَلُ بِي ولا بِكم إنْ أتَّبِعُ إلا ما يُوحى إلَيَّ﴾: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen in his sleep that he would go to a land of palm trees and other trees, while his Companions had complained of the hardship that had befallen them. When he informed them that he would go to a land of palms and trees, and that was delayed, they thought what he, peace be upon him, had said was slow in coming. So he informed them that what he follows is what is revealed to him: if he is commanded to fight or to move, and that command is revelation, he follows it; and the dreams of the prophets, peace be upon them, are revelation.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ كانَ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ وشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِن بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ فَآمَنَ واسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾: It has come in the exegesis «that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām came to the Prophet ﷺ and believed in him, and said to him: Ask the Jews about me, for they will commend me to you and tell you of my standing in knowledge. So the Prophet ﷺ asked them about him before they knew that he had believed, and they told him that he was the most knowledgeable of them in the Torah and in their doctrine, and that he was a scholar, son of a scholar, son of a scholar. Then he believed in their presence and bore witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, and they said, after his believing: You are the worst of us and the son of the worst of us.
He said: Has it not come to you in the Torah from Moses, peace be upon him: When you see Muḥammad, convey my greeting of peace to him and believe in him?! And he set about showing them places in the Torah containing mention of the Prophet ﷺ and his description, while they were arrogant, denied, and deliberately covered that with their hands. And the answer (jawāb) of "إنْ كانَ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ وشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِن بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ فَآمَنَ واسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ"»: "Will you believe?" «[Translator's note: i.e. the jawāb is implied as "أتُؤْمِنُونَ؟".]» Then He made known that these obstinate ones in particular would not believe, and said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي القَوْمَ الظّالِمِينَ﴾, that is, He has made their requital for their disbelief, after the guidance had become clear to them, His prolonging them in error. It has been said in the exegesis of His saying ﴿وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِن بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ﴾: to the like of the testimony of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām; but the better view — and Allah knows best — is that "عَلى مِثْلِهِ" means "to the like of the testimony of the Prophet ﷺ."
«[Translator's note: in the source the closing quotation mark of the reported narration falls after the grammatical remark on the jawāb; it is kept where the source places it.]»

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْ كانَ خَيْرًا ما سَبَقُونا إلَيْهِ﴾: It has come in the exegesis that when Juhayna, Muzayna, Aslam and Ghifār embraced Islam, Banū ʿĀmir, Ghaṭafān, Asad and Ashjaʿ said: If the religion these have entered were good, they would not have preceded us to it, for we are mightier than they; these are only herders of lambs.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتابُ مُوسى إمامًا ورَحْمَةً﴾: "إمامًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and His saying "وَرَحْمَةً" is conjoined to it. ﴿وَهَذا كِتابٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِسانًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "and it confirms what was before it, in an Arabic tongue," because of what comes after this place: ﴿قالُوا يا قَوْمَنا إنّا سَمِعْنا كِتابًا أُنْـزِلَ مِن بَعْدِ مُوسى مُصَدِّقًا لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ يَهْدِي إلى الحَقِّ﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 30]. "لَهُ" (to it) has been omitted here — I mean from His saying "وَهَذا كِتابٌ مُصَدِّقٌ" — because before it is "وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتابُ مُوسى"; so the meaning is: "And this is a Book confirming it," that is, "confirming the Torah." And "لِسانًا عَرَبِيًّا" are both accusative as ḥāl; the meaning is: "confirming what was before it, being Arabic," and "لِسانًا" is mentioned for emphasis (tawkīd), as you say "جاءَنِي زَيْدٌ رَجُلًا صالِحًا" (Zayd came to me, a righteous man), meaning "Zayd came to me righteous," and you mention "رَجُلًا" for emphasis. There is another aspect in it, with the meaning: "And this is a Book confirming an Arabic tongue," the meaning being "confirming the Prophet, peace be upon him," so the meaning would be: "confirming one possessed of an Arabic tongue."
And His saying: ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾: It is also read "لِتُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا". ﴿وَبُشْرى لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾: the better view is that "بُشْرى" is in the position of the nominative, the meaning being "and it is glad tidings for those who do good"; and it is possible that "بُشْرى" is in the position of the accusative, with the meaning: "to warn those who do wrong and to give the doers of good glad tidings."

zajjaj:13-13.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ قالُوا رَبُّنا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: the meaning of "ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا" is: they remained steadfast upon the oneness of Allah and the law of His Prophet, peace be upon him.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنا الإنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ إحْسانًا﴾: It is also read "حُسْنًا", and both are good. "إحْسانًا" is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of "وَصَّيْناهُ بِوالِدَيْهِ" is: We commanded him to do good to them with goodness.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهًا﴾, and "كَرْهًا" — both have been read. The meaning is: "His mother carried him with hardship and delivered him with hardship."
And His saying: ﴿وَحَمْلُهُ وفِصالُهُ ثَلاثُونَ شَهْرًا﴾: It has been read "وَفَصْلُهُ ثَلاثُونَ شَهْرًا". The meaning of "فِصالُهُ" is his weaning. The least that pregnancy can be is six months. The preferred [reading] is "وَفِصالُهُ", because what has come in the ḥadīth is: «"There is no suckling after al-fiṣāl,"» meaning after weaning.
And His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا بَلَغَ أشُدَّهُ وبَلَغَ أرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً﴾: It has come in the exegesis that "al-ashudd" (full strength) is thirty-three years; it has been said: al-ashudd is eighteen years; and it has been said: al-ashudd is reaching puberty. The prevailing view is that it is thirty-three, because the time at which a person becomes complete in his body, his strength and the firmness of his youth is when he reaches thirty-odd years, and likewise in his discernment.
And His saying: ﴿وَأصْلِحْ لِي في ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾: its meaning is: make my offspring righteous.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
And His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهم أحْسَنَ ما عَمِلُوا﴾: "أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يُتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهم أحْسَنُ ما عَمِلُوا" is also permissible. The reading is "يُتَقَبَّلُ" and "نَتَقَبَّلُ", and likewise "يُتَجاوَزُ" and "نَتَجاوَزُ". "يَتَقَبَّلُ" is permissible, but I do not know of anyone who read it so.
And His saying: ﴿وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِي كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ﴾: this is accusative because it is a maṣdar confirming what precedes it (maṣdar muʾakkid), because His saying ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهم أحْسَنَ ما عَمِلُوا﴾ has the meaning of a promise, since Allah has promised them acceptance; so "وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ" is an emphasis (tawkīd) of that.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والَّذِي قالَ لِوالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَكُما﴾: It has been read "أُفِّ لَكُما" and "أُفَّ لَكُما"; we have explained that in Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl.
And His saying: ﴿أتَعِدانِنِي أنْ أُخْرَجَ﴾: It is also read "أنْ أخْرُجَ" (that I will come out). "أتَعِدانِّي" with assimilation (idghām) is also permissible; or, if you wish, you pronounce both nūns distinctly; and if you wish you give the yāʾ sukūn, and if you wish you give it fatḥa. It has been transmitted from some of them as "أتَعِدانَنِي", with fatḥa, but that is a solecism (laḥn) with no justification, so do not ever read it so, because giving fatḥa to the nūn of the dual is an error; even if that is reported as an anomaly (shudhūdh), a reading is not to be based on anomaly. It is reported that His saying in the verse before this, up to His saying ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 16], was revealed concerning Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him. As for His saying ﴿والَّذِي قالَ لِوالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَكُما﴾, some of them said it was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [ibn Abī Bakr] before his embracing Islam; but this is invalidated by
«[Translator's note: the sentence continues in the next entry (al-Aḥqāf 18).]»

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ القَوْلُ في أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ مِنَ الجِنِّ والإنْسِ إنَّهم كانُوا خاسِرِينَ﴾: for Allah made known that the word of punishment has become due upon these; and when He made that known, He made known that they will not believe. But ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was a believer, among the most excellent of the believers and their nobles. The correct exegesis is that it was revealed concerning the undutiful disbeliever.

zajjaj:19-19.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ دَرَجاتٌ مِمّا عَمِلُوا ولِيُوَفِّيَهم أعْمالَهُمْ﴾, and "وَلِنُوَفِّيَهم" — both [are read], with nūn and with yāʾ.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلى النّارِ﴾: Most of the readers have fatḥa on the nūn and tafkhīm (full, unslanted pronunciation) in "اَلنّارِ"; but most of the speech of the Arabs inclines the alif towards kasra (imāla), and Abū ʿAmr reads so: "عَلى النِّارِ". He prefers the kasra on the rāʾ because the rāʾ, according to them, is a repeated (trilled) letter, so its kasra is as though it were two kasras.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ﴾: without the interrogative alif; and it is read "أأذْهَبْتُمْ" with two fully pronounced hamzas, and with two hamzas of which the second is lightened. This alif is for rebuke (tawbīkh); in rebuke you may retain the alif if you wish, or omit it if you wish, as you say: "يا فُلانُ أحْدَثْتَ ما لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ؟ جَنَيْتَ عَلى نَفْسِكَ" (O so-and-so, you have done what is not lawful for you? You have wronged yourself), when you rebuke him; or, if you wish: "أأخَذْتَ ما لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ؟ أجَنَيْتَ عَلى نَفْسِكَ؟" (Did you take what is not lawful for you? Did you wrong yourself?).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فاليَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الهُونِ﴾: its meaning is: al-hawān (humiliation).
«[Translator's note: "fatḥa on the nūn" is as in the source; in context the point concerns the alif of "النّار" (no imāla), and the source may intend that.]»

zajjaj:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واذْكُرْ أخا عادٍ إذْ أنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالأحْقافِ﴾: "اَلْأحْقافُ" are long, raised sand-dunes like mounds; these aḥqāf were the dwellings of ʿĀd.
